sourceRange.text: 初，秦宗權遣其弟宗衡掠地淮南，是歲，宗衡為其將孫儒所殺，儒攻楊行密于揚州。淮南大亂，行密走宣州，儒入揚州。大順元年春，遣龐師古攻孫儒于淮南，大敗而還。四月，宿州將張筠以宿州復歸于時溥，王自將攻之，不克。

context.beforeSource: 冬，大雨，水，不能軍而旋。
context.afterSource: 初，黃巢敗走，李克用追之，至于冤朐，不及而旋。

manualTranslations.zh: 初，秦宗權遣其弟宗衡掠地淮南，是歲，宗衡為其將孫儒所殺，儒攻楊行密于揚州。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, Qin Zongquan sent his younger brother Zongheng to raid territory in Huainan. That year, Zongheng was killed by his general Sun Ru, and Ru attacked Yang Xingmi at Yangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qin Zongquan sent his brother Zongheng to raid Huainan. That year Zongheng was killed by his own general Sun Ru, who then attacked Yang Xingmi at Yangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 淮南大亂，行密走宣州，儒入揚州。
manualTranslations.literal: Huainan was greatly disordered; Xingmi fled to Xuanzhou, and Ru entered Yangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huainan fell into chaos. Yang Xingmi fled to Xuanzhou, and Sun Ru entered Yangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 大順元年春，遣龐師古攻孫儒于淮南，大敗而還。
manualTranslations.literal: In spring of the first year of Dashun, he sent Pang Shigu to attack Sun Ru in Huainan; Shigu was badly defeated and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In spring, Dashun 1, he sent Pang Shigu against Sun Ru in Huainan, but Pang was routed and came back.

manualTranslations.zh: 四月，宿州將張筠以宿州復歸于時溥，王自將攻之，不克。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month, Suzhou general Zhang Jun returned Suzhou to Shi Pu. The Prince personally led troops to attack it, but could not take it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhang Jun, commander at Suzhou, restored Suzhou to Shi Pu. The Prince attacked in person but failed to take it.

sourceRange.text: 唐宦者劉季述作亂，天子幽于東宮。天復元年正月，護駕都頭孫德昭誅季述，天子復位。封王為梁王。遣張存敬攻王珂于河中，出含山，下晉、絳二州。王珂求救于晉，晉不能救，乃來降。三月，大舉攻晉。氏叔琮出太行，取澤、潞。葛從周、張存敬、侯言、張歸厚及鎮、定之兵，皆會于太原，圍之，不克，遇雨而還。五月，天子以王兼河中尹、護國軍節度使。六月，晉取慈、隰。

context.beforeSource: 進攻定州，王郜奔于晉，其將王處直以定州降。
context.afterSource: 自劉季述等已誅，宰相崔胤外與梁交，欲假梁兵盡誅宦者。

context.afterLocal: 自劉季述等已誅，宰相崔胤外與梁交，欲假梁兵盡誅宦者。

manualTranslations.zh: 唐宦者劉季述作亂，天子幽于東宮。
manualTranslations.literal: The Tang eunuch Liu Jishu made disorder, and the Son of Heaven was confined in the Eastern Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Tang eunuch Liu Jishu staged a coup and imprisoned the emperor in the Eastern Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 天復元年正月，護駕都頭孫德昭誅季述，天子復位。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of Tianfu 1, Sun Dezhao, commander of the imperial escort, executed Jishu, and the Son of Heaven was restored to the throne.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month, Tianfu 1, Sun Dezhao, commander of the imperial escort, killed Liu Jishu and restored the emperor.

manualTranslations.zh: 封王為梁王。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was made Prince of Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣張存敬攻王珂于河中，出含山，下晉、絳二州。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent Zhang Cunjing to attack Wang Ke at Hezhong; Cunjing went out by Hanshan and took Jin and Jiang prefectures.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Cunjing to attack Wang Ke at Hezhong. Zhang advanced through Hanshan and captured Jinzhou and Jiangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 王珂求救于晉，晉不能救，乃來降。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Ke sought rescue from Jin; Jin could not save him, so he came and surrendered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ke appealed to Jin for help, but Jin could not rescue him, so he surrendered.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月，大舉攻晉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month, he launched a major attack on Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month he mounted a major offensive against Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 氏叔琮出太行，取澤、潞。
manualTranslations.literal: Shi Shucung went out through the Taihang and took Ze and Lu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shi Shucung came through the Taihang and captured Zezhou and Luzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 葛從周、張存敬、侯言、張歸厚及鎮、定之兵，皆會于太原，圍之，不克，遇雨而還。
manualTranslations.literal: Ge Congzhou, Zhang Cunjing, Hou Yan, Zhang Guihou, and the troops of Zhen and Ding all assembled at Taiyuan and besieged it; they could not take it, encountered rain, and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou, Zhang Cunjing, Hou Yan, Zhang Guihou, and troops from Zhen and Ding converged on Taiyuan and besieged it, but rain forced them to withdraw without taking the city.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月，天子以王兼河中尹、護國軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month, the Son of Heaven made the Prince concurrently Governor of Hezhong and military governor of the Huguo army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor appointed the Prince concurrently governor of Hezhong and military governor of Huguo.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，晉取慈、隰。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month, Jin took Ci and Xi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Jin captured Cizhou and Xizhou.

sourceRange.text: 甲天子出幸梁軍。

context.beforeSource: 三年正月，茂貞殺韓全誨等二十人，囊其首，示梁軍，約出天子以為解。
context.afterSource: 遣使者馳召崔胤，胤託疾不至。
context.beforeLocal: 三年正月，茂貞殺韓全誨等二十人，囊其首，示梁軍，約出天子以為解。
context.afterLocal: 遣使者馳召崔胤，胤托疾不至。

sourceRange.text: 乾寧元年二月，王及朱宣戰于漁山，大敗之。二年八月，又敗宣于梁山。十一月，又敗之于鉅野。兗、鄆求救于河東，李克用發兵救之，假道于魏。既而魏人擊之，克用怒，大舉攻魏。羅弘信來求救，遣葛從周救魏。是歲，李克用封晉王。三年五月，戰于洹水，擒克用子落落，送于魏，殺之。七月，鳳翔李茂貞犯京師，天子出居于華州。王請以兵赴難，天子優詔止之。又請遷都洛陽，不許。四年正月，龐師古克鄆州，王如鄆州，以朱友裕為留後。遂攻兗州。朱瑾奔于淮南，以葛從周為兗州留後。九月，攻淮南，龐師古出清口，葛從周出安豐，王軍屯于宿州。楊行密遣朱瑾先擊清口，師古敗死。從周亟返兵，至于渒河，瑾又敗之。王懼，馳歸。

context.beforeSource: 王如徐州，以師古為留後，遂攻兗、鄆。
context.afterSource: 光化元年三月，天子以王兼天平軍節度使。
context.beforeLocal: 王如徐州，以師古為留後，遂攻兗、鄆。
context.afterLocal: 光化元年三月，天子以王兼天平軍節度使。

manualTranslations.zh: 乾寧元年二月，王及朱宣戰于漁山，大敗之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of Qianing 1, the Prince fought Zhu Xuan at Yushan and badly defeated him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month, Qianing 1, the Prince met Zhu Xuan at Yushan and routed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年八月，又敗宣于梁山。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year, he again defeated Xuan at Liangshan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year he defeated Xuan again at Liangshan.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一月，又敗之于鉅野。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month, he again defeated him at Juye.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he defeated him yet again at Juye.

manualTranslations.zh: 兗、鄆求救于河東，李克用發兵救之，假道于魏。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan and Yun sought rescue from Hedong. Li Keyong sent troops to save them, requesting passage through Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan and Yun appealed to Hedong for help. Li Keyong sent troops to relieve them and asked to pass through Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 既而魏人擊之，克用怒，大舉攻魏。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon the men of Wei attacked them; Keyong was angry and launched a major attack on Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wei forces attacked them, Li Keyong grew furious and mounted a major attack on Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 羅弘信來求救，遣葛從周救魏。
manualTranslations.literal: Luo Hongxin came to seek rescue, and he sent Ge Congzhou to save Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxin appealed for help, and the Prince sent Ge Congzhou to relieve Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲，李克用封晉王。
manualTranslations.literal: That year, Li Keyong was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year Li Keyong was made Prince of Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年五月，戰于洹水，擒克用子落落，送于魏，殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, they fought at the Huan River, captured Keyong’s son Luoluo, sent him to Wei, and killed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, at the Huan River, they captured Li Keyong’s son Luoluo, sent him to Wei, and had him killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，鳳翔李茂貞犯京師，天子出居于華州。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, Li Maozhen of Fengxiang threatened the capital, and the Son of Heaven went out to reside at Hua Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Li Maozhen of Fengxiang menaced the capital, and the emperor withdrew to Huazhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 王請以兵赴難，天子優詔止之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince requested to bring troops to the crisis, but the Son of Heaven issued a gracious edict stopping him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Prince asked to lead troops to the emperor’s aid, but the emperor politely ordered him not to come.

manualTranslations.zh: 又請遷都洛陽，不許。
manualTranslations.literal: He also requested that the capital be moved to Luoyang, but this was not permitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also asked to move the capital to Luoyang, but permission was refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年正月，龐師古克鄆州，王如鄆州，以朱友裕為留後。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Pang Shigu took Yun Prefecture. The Prince went to Yun Prefecture and made Zhu Youyu acting governor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Pang Shigu captured Yunzhou. The Prince went there and appointed Zhu Youyu acting governor.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂攻兗州。
manualTranslations.literal: He then attacked Yan Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then attacked Yanzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 朱瑾奔于淮南，以葛從周為兗州留後。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu Jin fled to Huainan, and Ge Congzhou was made acting governor of Yan Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin fled to Huainan, and Ge Congzhou was installed as acting governor of Yanzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，攻淮南，龐師古出清口，葛從周出安豐，王軍屯于宿州。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month, he attacked Huainan: Pang Shigu went out through Qingkou, Ge Congzhou through Anfeng, and the Prince’s army encamped at Suzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he attacked Huainan. Pang Shigu advanced by Qingkou, Ge Congzhou by Anfeng, and the Prince’s own army camped at Suzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊行密遣朱瑾先擊清口，師古敗死。
manualTranslations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent Zhu Jin to strike Qingkou first; Shigu was defeated and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent Zhu Jin to hit Qingkou first, and Pang Shigu was defeated and killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 從周亟返兵，至于渒河，瑾又敗之。
manualTranslations.literal: Congzhou hurriedly turned his troops back; when he reached the Pi River, Jin defeated him as well.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou hastened back, but when he reached the Pi River Zhu Jin defeated him too.

manualTranslations.zh: 王懼，馳歸。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince was afraid and galloped back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the Prince raced home.

sourceRange.text: 濬挾汴力，請益堅。

context.beforeSource: 唐諸大臣皆以為不可興師。
context.afterSource: 天子不得已，許之。

sourceRange.text: 曾三異校定曰：三異案，唐書地理志：唐州，天祐三年朱全忠徙治泌陽，表更名泌州。則是天祐二年唐州舊名猶在，至三年始更為泌。光化之初，未當有泌州之名。今書為泌，則誤也。

context.beforeSource: 七月，遣氏叔琮、康懷英攻匡凝，取其泌、隨、鄧三州。
context.afterSource: 匡凝請和乃止。

manualTranslations.zh: 曾三異校定曰：三異案，唐書地理志：唐州，天祐三年朱全忠徙治泌陽，表更名泌州。
manualTranslations.literal: Zeng Sanyi’s collation says: Sanyi notes that according to the Geography Treatise of the Tang History, in Tianyou 3 Zhu Quanzhong moved Tang Prefecture’s seat to Biyang and submitted a memorial changing its name to Mi Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zeng Sanyi’s collation says: Sanyi observes that the Geography Treatise of the Tang History records Zhu Quanzhong moving Tangzhou’s seat to Biyang in Tianyou 3 and petitioning to rename it Mizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 則是天祐二年唐州舊名猶在，至三年始更為泌。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus in Tianyou 2 the old name Tang Prefecture still remained, and only in the third year was it changed to Mi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus in Tianyou 2 the old name Tangzhou was still in use; it was only in the third year that it became Mizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 光化之初，未當有泌州之名。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua, there should not yet have been the name Mi Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guanghua, the name Mizhou should not yet have existed.

manualTranslations.zh: 今書為泌，則誤也。
manualTranslations.literal: If the present text writes it as Mi, then that is an error.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: So when the present text writes Mizhou, it is mistaken.

sourceRange.text: 淮南節度使高駢死，楊行密入揚州。天子以王兼淮南節度使。王乃表行密為副使，以行軍司馬李璠為留後。璠之揚州，行密不納。文德元年正月，王如淮南，至宋州而還。是時，秦宗權陷襄州，以趙德諲為節度使。德諲叛于宗權以來附。天子因以王為蔡州四面行營都統，以德諲為副。

context.beforeSource: 十二月，天子使來，賜王鐵券及德政碑。

manualTranslations.zh: 淮南節度使高駢死，楊行密入揚州。
manualTranslations.literal: Gao Pian, military governor of Huainan, died, and Yang Xingmi entered Yangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gao Pian, military governor of Huainan, died, and Yang Xingmi entered Yangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 天子以王兼淮南節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: The Son of Heaven made the Prince concurrently military governor of Huainan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed the Prince concurrently military governor of Huainan.

manualTranslations.zh: 王乃表行密為副使，以行軍司馬李璠為留後。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince then submitted a memorial making Xingmi deputy commissioner and Li Fan, army marching marshal, acting governor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Prince then memorialized to make Yang Xingmi deputy commissioner and his campaign marshal Li Fan acting governor.

manualTranslations.zh: 璠之揚州，行密不納。
manualTranslations.literal: When Fan went to Yangzhou, Xingmi would not admit him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Fan went to Yangzhou, Yang Xingmi refused to admit him.

manualTranslations.zh: 文德元年正月，王如淮南，至宋州而還。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of Wende 1, the Prince went toward Huainan, reached Song Prefecture, and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month, Wende 1, the Prince set out for Huainan but turned back after reaching Songzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，秦宗權陷襄州，以趙德諲為節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time Qin Zongquan captured Xiang Prefecture and made Zhao Deyin military governor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time Qin Zongquan had taken Xiangzhou and appointed Zhao Deyin military governor.

manualTranslations.zh: 德諲叛于宗權以來附。
manualTranslations.literal: Deyin rebelled against Zongquan and came to attach himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Deyin broke with Zongquan and came over to Quanzhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 天子因以王為蔡州四面行營都統，以德諲為副。
manualTranslations.literal: The Son of Heaven therefore made the Prince overall commander of the four-sided campaign headquarters against Cai Prefecture, with Deyin as deputy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore made the Prince supreme commander of the campaign against Caizhou, with Zhao Deyin as his deputy.

manualTranslations.zh: 始而稱名，既而稱爵，既而稱帝，漸也。
manualTranslations.literal: At first he is called by name, then by title, and then as emperor; this is gradual progression.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: First the text names him personally, then gives his noble title, then calls him emperor: the progression is deliberate.

manualTranslations.zh: 爵至王而後稱，著其逼者。
manualTranslations.literal: Only when his rank reached prince does the text use the title, showing his pressure toward it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only after his rank reached prince does the text use the title, marking how near he had pressed to the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃遣朱珍募兵於東方，而求救于兗、鄆。
manualTranslations.literal: He then sent Zhu Zhen to recruit troops in the east and sought rescue from Yan and Yun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then sent Zhu Zhen east to raise men and appealed to Yan and Yun for help.

sourceRange.text: 是時，晉王李克用、岐王李茂貞、楚王趙匡凝、蜀王王建、吳王楊行密曾三異校定曰：三異案，克用本紀及茂貞傳，建、行密世家，皆書其在唐所授，獨匡凝不書其在唐，此乃闕文。聞梁遷天子洛陽，皆欲舉兵討梁，王大懼。

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，晉王李克用、岐王李茂貞、楚王趙匡凝、蜀王王建、吳王楊行密曾三異校定曰：三異案，克用本紀及茂貞傳，建、行密世家，皆書其在唐所授，獨匡凝不書其在唐，此乃闕文。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time there were Prince of Jin Li Keyong, Prince of Qi Li Maozhen, Prince of Chu Zhao Kuangning, Prince of Shu Wang Jian, and Prince of Wu Yang Xingmi. Zeng Sanyi’s collation says: Sanyi notes that Keyong’s Basic Annals, Maozhen’s Biography, and the Hereditary Accounts of Jian and Xingmi all record the titles they received under Tang; only Kuangning is not recorded with what he held under Tang, and this is omitted text.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At this time Li Keyong was Prince of Jin, Li Maozhen Prince of Qi, Zhao Kuangning Prince of Chu, Wang Jian Prince of Shu, and Yang Xingmi Prince of Wu. Zeng Sanyi’s collation says: Sanyi observes that the annals of Keyong, the biography of Maozhen, and the hereditary accounts of Jian and Xingmi all state their Tang-granted titles; only Kuangning’s Tang title is missing, so this is a textual omission.

manualTranslations.zh: 聞梁遷天子洛陽，皆欲舉兵討梁，王大懼。
manualTranslations.literal: When they heard that Liang had moved the Son of Heaven to Luoyang, all wanted to raise troops to punish Liang, and the Prince was greatly afraid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When they heard that Liang had moved the emperor to Luoyang, they all talked of raising armies to punish Liang, and the Prince was terrified.

sourceRange.text: 王乃留子友倫為護駕指揮使，曾三異校定曰：三異案，家人傳友倫乃王兄存之子，其後中書上議，亦皆謂之皇姪。以為天子衞，引兵東歸。

sourceRange.text: 夷狄君臣姓名、官爵，或書或否，不必備，或因其舊史之詳略，但書其來以示意爾。乙酉，兄全昱為廣王，子友文博王，友文非子而書子，語在家人傳。友珪郢王，友璋福王，友貞均王，友徽建王，姪友諒衡王，友能惠王，友誨邵王。甲午，改樞密院為崇政院，太府卿敬翔為使。是月，潞州行營都指揮使李思安及晉人戰，敗績。我敗曰敗績，彼敗曰敗之，文理宜然。已見行營，故戰不言地。六月甲寅，平盧軍節度使韓建守司徒，同中書門下平章事。

manualTranslations.literal: If not these five, then they are not recorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Events outside these five categories are not recorded.

manualTranslations.zh: 戊辰，大赦，赦文皆曰大赦天下，此書大，見其志之欲遠及也，不曰天下，實有所不及也。
manualTranslations.literal: On wuchen there was a great amnesty. Amnesty texts all say great amnesty under Heaven; here writing great shows his intent that it reach far, and not saying under Heaven shows that in fact there were places it did not reach.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the day wuchen there was a general amnesty. Amnesty proclamations all say "general amnesty under Heaven"; writing only "general" here shows his wish that it reach widely, while not saying "under Heaven" reflects that in fact it did not reach everywhere.

manualTranslations.zh: 改元，國號梁。
manualTranslations.literal: The reign title was changed, and the state was named Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He adopted a new reign title and named the dynasty Liang.

sourceRange.text: 戊寅，大閱于興安鞠場。九月辛巳朔，御文明殿，入閤。御殿而云入閤，錄其本語。事在李琪列傳。此禮，其後屢行，皆不書，一書以見其失足矣。

manualTranslations.literal: His wisdom was not enough to protect himself and his talent not enough to govern the multitude, and he was killed; the text does not write died for it, but phrases it as was killed, showing that dying the death one should is a great principle for a gentleman and is not rashly granted to people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His judgment was insufficient to protect himself and his ability insufficient to govern the troops, and so he was killed. The text does not write that he "died for it," but phrases it as "was killed," showing that dying a worthy death is a great principle for a gentleman and is not lightly granted to anyone.

sourceRange.text: 五代亂世，兵無虛日，不可悉書。故用兵無勝敗，攻城無得失，皆不書。其命大將與天子有所如，自著大事爾。此如懷、澤者，以兵方攻潞州也。丁丑，如澤州。戊寅，封鴻臚卿李崧萊國公，為二王後。梁嘗更「戊」曰「武」，而舊史悉復為「戊」。

localRange.text: 丁丑，如泽州。戊寅，封鸿胪卿李崧介国公，为二王后。

manualTranslations.zh: 五代亂世，兵無虛日，不可悉書。
manualTranslations.literal: In the disorderly age of the Five Dynasties, there was no empty day from war, and it could not all be written.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the chaotic age of the Five Dynasties, hardly a day passed without warfare, and it could not all be recorded.

manualTranslations.zh: 故用兵無勝敗，攻城無得失，皆不書。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore, troop use without victory or defeat and attacks on cities without gain or loss are all not recorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore troop deployments with no victory or defeat, and attacks on cities with no gain or loss, are not recorded.

manualTranslations.zh: 其命大將與天子有所如，自著大事爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Appointments of great generals and places to which the Son of Heaven went naturally mark major events.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The appointment of a great general, and places to which the Son of Heaven went, naturally mark major events.

manualTranslations.zh: 此如懷、澤者，以兵方攻潞州也。
manualTranslations.literal: This going to Huai and Ze was because the armies were then attacking Luzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This journey to Huai and Ze was because the armies were then attacking Luzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁丑，如澤州。
manualTranslations.literal: On dingchou, he went to Zezhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou he went to Zezhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 戊寅，封鴻臚卿李崧萊國公，為二王後。
manualTranslations.literal: On wuyin, he enfeoffed Li Song, Chamberlain for Ceremonials, as Duke of Lai to be successor to the two royal houses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the day wuyin Li Song, Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was made Duke of Lai and successor to the two royal houses.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁嘗更「戊」曰「武」，而舊史悉復為「戊」。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang once changed wu 戊 to wu 武, but the old histories all restored it as 戊.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang once changed the character wu 戊 to wu 武, but the old histories uniformly restored it as 戊.

manualTranslations.literal: Lighting lamps was a custom transmitted by popular practice; from Son of Heaven down to commoners, the whole realm shared its extravagance and pleasure, and it was a great corruption of customs, so recording the intent of the edict makes its fault knowable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lighting lamps was a transmitted custom; from the Son of Heaven down to commoners, the whole realm indulged in its extravagance and pleasure, a major corruption of custom. Recording the edict's intent therefore makes the fault clear.

sourceRange.text: 年六十一。不書崩處，以異於得其終者。乾化二年十一月，友珪葬之河南伊闕縣，號宣陵。以不得其死，故不書葬。嗚呼，天下之惡梁久矣！自後唐以來，皆以為偽也。至予論次五代，獨不偽梁，而議者或譏予大失春秋之旨，以謂：「梁負大惡，當加誅絕，而反進之，是奬篡也，非春秋之志也。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Delun could not be accused as the chief instigator, but he could be blamed for failing to die loyal and instead defecting.

manualTranslations.zh: 張彥實首惡，而略不書，彥，微者，德倫可以誅而不誅，故以德倫獨任其責。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Yanshi was the chief culprit, but he is omitted and not written; Yan was a minor man, while Delun could have executed him and did not, so Delun alone is made to bear the responsibility.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshi was the chief culprit, but he is omitted because he was a minor figure. Delun could have executed him and failed to do so, so Delun alone is made to bear the blame.

sourceRange.text: 冬十二月庚子朔，賀瓌殺其將謝彥章、孟審澄、侯溫裕。癸亥，瓌及晉人戰于胡柳，敗績。是歲，泰寧軍節度使張守進叛附于晉，亳州團練使劉鄩為兗州安撫制置使以討之。舊史不書，亡其月日，故書于歲末，為明年克兗州張本。五年春正月，晉軍于德勝。用兵無勝敗不書，此梁、晉得失所繫，故書也。秋八月乙未朔，開封尹王瓚為北面行營招討使。冬十月，劉鄩克兗州，張守進伏誅。十二月，晉人取濮陽。

sourceRange.text: 比至封丘，又敗之，巢脫身走，克用追之，一日夜馳二百里，至于冤朐，不及而還。過汴州，休軍封禪寺，朱全忠饗克用於上源驛，夜，酒罷，克用醉臥，伏兵發，火起，侍者郭景銖滅燭，匿克用牀下，以水醒面而告以難。會天大雨滅火，克用得從者薛鐵山、賀回鶻等，隨電光，縋尉氏門出還軍中。

localRange.text: 比至封丘，又败之，巢脱身走，克用追之，一日夜驰三百里，至于冤朐，不及而还。洺、磁孟氏据之，故当时有两昭义。过汴州，休军封禅寺，朱全忠飨克用于上源驿。夜，酒罢，克用醉卧，伏兵发，火起，侍者郭景铢灭烛，匿克用床下，以水醒面而告以难。会天大雨灭火，克用得从者薛铁山、贺回鹘等，随电光，缒尉氏门出，还军中。

sourceRange.text: 懿宗咸通十年，神策大將軍康承訓統十八將討龐勛於徐州，以朱邪赤心為太原行營招討沙陀三部落軍使。以從破勛功，拜單于大都護、振武軍節度使，賜姓名曰李國昌，以之屬籍。沙陀素彊，而國昌恃功益橫恣，懿宗患之。十三年，徙國昌雲州刺史、大同軍防禦使，國昌稱疾拒命。國昌子克用，尤善騎射，能仰中雙鳧，為雲州守捉使。國昌已拒命，克用乃殺大同軍防禦使段文楚，據雲州，自稱留後。唐以太僕卿盧簡方為振武節度使，會幽、并兵討之。簡方行至嵐州，軍潰，由是沙陀侵掠代北為邊患矣。明年，僖宗即位，以謂前太原節度使李業遇沙陀有恩，而業已死，乃以其子鈞為靈武節度使、宣慰沙陀六州三部落使，六州三部落，皆不見其名處，據唐書除使有此語爾。以招緝之。拜克用大同軍防禦使。居久之，國昌出擊党項，吐渾赫連鐸襲破振武。克用聞之，自雲州往迎國昌，而雲州人亦閉關拒之。

localRange.text: 懿宗咸通十年，神策大将军康承训统十八将讨庞勋于徐州，以朱邪赤心为太原行营招讨沙、陀三部落军使。以从破勋功，拜单于大都护、振武军节度使，赐姓名曰李国昌，以之属籍。居久之，国昌出击党项，吐浑赫连铎袭破振武。克用闻之，自云州往迎国昌，而云州人亦闭关拒之。

manualTranslations.zh: 沙陀素彊，而國昌恃功益橫恣，懿宗患之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Shatuo had long been formidable, and Guochang, trusting in his merit, grew ever more arrogant and unrestrained; Yizong was troubled by it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shatuo were already a fierce power, and Guochang’s battlefield triumphs made him increasingly overbearing. Yizong grew alarmed.

manualTranslations.zh: 十三年，徙國昌雲州刺史、大同軍防禦使，國昌稱疾拒命。
manualTranslations.literal: In the thirteenth year Guochang was transferred to be prefect of Yunzhou and defender of the Datong army; Guochang claimed illness and refused the order.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the court moved Guochang to Yunzhou as prefect and defender of Datong. He pleaded illness and defied the transfer.

manualTranslations.zh: 國昌子克用，尤善騎射，能仰中雙鳧，為雲州守捉使。
manualTranslations.literal: Guochang’s son Keyong was especially skilled in mounted archery and could shoot down paired ducks while looking upward; he served as Yunzhou garrison commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guochang’s son Keyong was a master of horseback archery, famed for shooting down paired ducks on the wing. He held the Yunzhou garrison post.

manualTranslations.zh: 國昌已拒命，克用乃殺大同軍防禦使段文楚，據雲州，自稱留後。
manualTranslations.literal: After Guochang had refused the order, Keyong killed Duan Wenchu, defender of the Datong army, seized Yunzhou, and styled himself acting military governor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Guochang refused the transfer, Keyong killed Duan Wenchu, defender of Datong, took Yunzhou, and proclaimed himself acting governor.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐以太僕卿盧簡方為振武節度使，會幽、并兵討之。
manualTranslations.literal: Tang appointed Minister of the Imperial Stud Lu Jianfang military governor of Zhenwu and joined You and Bing armies to punish them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Tang court named Lu Jianfang, Minister of the Imperial Stud, military governor of Zhenwu and sent allied armies from You and Bing against them.

manualTranslations.zh: 簡方行至嵐州，軍潰，由是沙陀侵掠代北為邊患矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Jianfang marched as far as Lan Prefecture and his army collapsed; from this the Shatuo raided northern Dai and became a border scourge.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jianfang reached Lanzhou before his army broke apart. From then on the Shatuo preyed on northern Dai and became the frontier’s chief menace.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，僖宗即位，以謂前太原節度使李業遇沙陀有恩，而業已死，乃以其子鈞為靈武節度使、宣慰沙陀六州三部落使，六州三部落，皆不見其名處，據唐書除使有此語爾。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year Xizong took the throne. The court held that the former Taiyuan military governor Li Ye had once shown the Shatuo favor, and though Ye was now dead, his son Jun was made military governor of Lingwu and commissioner to pacify the Shatuo of six prefectures and three tribes—the names of those six prefectures and three tribes are nowhere recorded; only the Tang Annals’ appointment edict preserves this phrase.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year Xizong succeeded to the throne. Remembering that the former Taiyuan governor Li Ye had once dealt kindly with the Shatuo, and that Ye was now dead, the court appointed his son Jun military governor of Lingwu and commissioner to pacify the Shatuo across six prefectures and three tribes—whose names are not recorded anywhere except in the appointment language of the Tang Annals.

manualTranslations.zh: 以招緝之。
manualTranslations.literal: This was done to win them back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The appointment was meant to win them back.

manualTranslations.zh: 拜克用大同軍防禦使。
manualTranslations.literal: Keyong was appointed defender of the Datong army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Keyong was named defender of Datong.

sourceRange.text: 率蕃漢萬人出石嶺關，過太原，求發軍錢。節度使鄭從讜與之錢千緡、米千石，克用怒，縱兵大掠而還。

localRange.text: 率蕃汉万人出石岭关，过太原，求发军钱。节度使郑从谠与之钱千缗、米千石，克用怒，纵兵大掠而还。

context.beforeSource: 景思念沙陀非克用不可將，乃以詔書召克用於達靼，承制以為代州刺史、鴈門以北行營節度使。
context.afterSource: 二年十一月，景思、克用復以步騎萬七千赴京師。
context.beforeLocal: 景思念沙陀非克用不可将，乃以诏书召克用于达靼，承制以为代州刺史、雁门以北行营节度使。
context.afterLocal: 二年十一月，景思、克用复以步骑万七千赴京师。

sourceRange.text: 莊宗光聖神閔孝皇帝，其先本號朱邪，蓋出於西突厥，至其後世，別自號曰沙陀，而以朱邪為姓。

localRange.text: 卷四唐本纪第四庄宗光圣神闵孝皇帝，其先本号朱邪，盖出于西突厥，至其后世，别自号曰沙陀，而朱邪为姓。

context.afterSource: 唐德宗時，有朱邪盡忠者，居於北庭之金滿州。
context.afterLocal: 唐德宗时，有朱邪尽忠者，居于北庭之金满州。

manualTranslations.zh: 庄宗光圣神闵孝皇帝，其先本号朱邪，盖出于西突厥，至其后世，别自号曰沙陀，而以朱邪为姓。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong, posthumously titled Luminous, Sagely, Divine, Compassionate, and Filial, traced his line to the clan originally called Zhuye, which had sprung from the Western Turks; in later generations they took the separate name Shatuo, with Zhuye as their surname.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong—the emperor honored as Luminous, Sagely, Divine, Compassionate, and Filial—came of stock first known as the Zhuye, a line said to descend from the Western Turks. His forebears later styled themselves Shatuo while keeping Zhuye as their clan name.

sourceRange.text: 十一月，遣其弟克脩攻昭義孟方立，取其澤、潞二州。方立走山東，以邢、洺、磁三州自別為昭義軍。昭義軍在唐時跨山東、西，管五州，至是澤、潞入于晉，邢、洺、磁孟氏據之，故當時有兩昭義。

localRange.text: 十一月，遣其弟克修攻昭义孟方立，取其泽、潞二州。方立走山东，以邢、洺、磁三州自别为昭义军。

context.beforeSource: 十月，國昌卒。
context.afterSource: 黃巢南走至蔡州，降秦宗權，遂攻陳州。
context.beforeLocal: 十月，国昌卒。
context.afterLocal: 黄巢南走至蔡州，降秦宗权，遂攻陈州。

manualTranslations.zh: 十一月，遣其弟克脩攻昭義孟方立，取其澤、潞二州。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month he sent his younger brother Kexiu to attack Zhaoyi’s Meng Fangli and took his Ze and Lu prefectures.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent his brother Kexiu against Meng Fangli of Zhaoyi and seized Ze and Lu.

manualTranslations.zh: 方立走山東，以邢、洺、磁三州自別為昭義軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Fangli fled to Shandong; he set apart Xing, Ming, and Ci as a separate Zhaoyi command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fangli fled east into Shandong and carved out Xing, Ming, and Ci as his own Zhaoyi command.

manualTranslations.zh: 昭義軍在唐時跨山東、西，管五州，至是澤、潞入于晉，邢、洺、磁孟氏據之，故當時有兩昭義。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zhaoyi command in Tang had spanned east and west Shandong, administering five prefectures; now Ze and Lu passed to Jin, while Xing, Ming, and Ci were held by the Meng clan, so at the time there were two Zhaoyi commands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Tang the Zhaoyi command had straddled the eastern and western Shanxi passes and governed five prefectures. Now Ze and Lu fell to Jin while the Meng family held Xing, Ming, and Ci—so for a time two rival Zhaoyi commands existed.

sourceRange.text: 李匡威救鎔，克用還軍邢州。景福元年，王鎔攻邢州，李存信、李嗣勳等敗鎔于堯山。二月，會王處存攻鎔，戰于新市，為鎔所敗。八月，李匡威攻雲州，以牽克用之兵，克用潛入于雲州，返出擊匡威，匡威敗走。

localRange.text: 李匡威救镕，克用还军邢州。景福元年，王镕攻邢州，李存信、李嗣勋等败镕于尧山。二月，会王处存攻镕，战于新市，为镕所败。八月，李匡威攻云州，以牵克用之兵，克用潜入于云州，返出击匡威，匡威败走。

context.beforeSource: 前軍李存孝取臨城，進攻元氏。
context.afterSource: 十月，李存孝以邢州叛。
context.beforeLocal: 前军李存孝取临城，进攻元氏。
context.afterLocal: 十月，李存孝以邢州叛。

manualTranslations.zh: 凡書過惡辭無譏貶者，直書其實而自見也。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever the text records faults and evil deeds without words of censure, it simply records the facts and lets them show for themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When faults or evil deeds are written without explicit censure, the facts are being recorded plainly so that the judgment appears on its own.

manualTranslations.zh: 庚戌，新羅國王金朴英及其泉州節度使王逢規皆遣使者來。
manualTranslations.literal: On gengxu, King Kim Pak-yeong of Silla and Wang Fenggui, military governor of Quanzhou, both sent envoys.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengxu, King Kim Pak-yeong of Silla and Wang Fenggui, military governor of Quanzhou, each sent envoys.

manualTranslations.zh: 繼儔以被殺書，非不予其死，蓋繼達殺兄，自當著其罪爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Jichou is recorded as having been killed; this is not because his death is denied recognition, but because Jida killed his elder brother and his crime therefore had to be made clear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jichou is written as having been killed not because his death is denied honor, but because Jida murdered his elder brother and the crime had to be exposed.

manualTranslations.zh: 與書弒君者同。
manualTranslations.literal: It is the same as entries that record killing a ruler.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It follows the same rule as entries that record regicide.

manualTranslations.zh: 樞密使，唐故以宦者為之，其職甚微，至此始參用士人，而與宰相權任鈞矣，故與宰相並書。
manualTranslations.literal: For privy commissioners, under the Tang eunuchs had formerly held the post and its duties were very minor. At this point literati-officials first began to be used in it, and its authority and responsibility became equal to those of chancellors, so it is written together with the chancellors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The office of privy commissioner had previously been held by eunuchs under the Tang and had been a minor post. From this point, scholar-officials were first appointed to it, and its authority came to equal that of the chancellors, so it is recorded alongside them.

manualTranslations.literal: On jiyou, Wang Yan surrendered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Wang Yan surrendered.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐兵入蜀，不攻不戰，君臣迎降，故直書其實，以見下書「殺衍」為殺降。
manualTranslations.literal: Tang troops entered Shu; without attack or battle, ruler and ministers came out to surrender. Therefore the facts are written directly, to show that the later entry “killed Yan” means killing a surrendered man.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Tang army entered Shu without assault or battle, and the ruler and his ministers came out to submit. The facts are therefore written plainly to show that the later phrase “killed Yan” means killing a man who had surrendered.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was Lady Cao, Zhuangzong’s mother.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong took the throne, he sent Lu Cheng to present the investiture register naming her Empress Dowager.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Neither the Old History nor the Veritable Records preserves the month or day of that ceremony, so it is not entered here.

sourceRange.text: 五代十三君，立后者七，辭有不同：立得其正者，曰「以某妃、夫人某氏為皇后」，其不正者，直曰「立某氏為皇后」。嫌與得正同爾，無褒貶也。

manualTranslations.zh: 五代十三君，立后者七，辭有不同：立得其正者，曰「以某妃、夫人某氏為皇后」，其不正者，直曰「立某氏為皇后」。
manualTranslations.literal: Among the thirteen rulers of the Five Dynasties, seven established empresses, and the wording differs: for one whose establishment was proper, it says “made such-and-such consort or madam, Lady X, empress”; for one whose establishment was improper, it simply says “established Lady X as empress.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Of the thirteen rulers of the Five Dynasties, seven named empresses, and the phrasing varies. When the act was proper, the text says that a certain consort or lady was made empress; when it was not, it simply says that a certain woman was established as empress.

manualTranslations.zh: 嫌與得正同爾，無褒貶也。
manualTranslations.literal: This only avoids making it seem the same as a proper establishment; there is no praise or blame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The difference only keeps the improper case from looking like a proper one; it carries no extra praise or blame.

manualTranslations.zh: 反者皆不書日，獨在禮書日，推迹其心可知爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who rebel are generally not recorded with the day; only Zaili is recorded with the day, and by tracing his intentions one can understand why.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rebels are usually not dated by day; Zhao Zaili alone is, and his motives explain why.

manualTranslations.zh: 其事具本傳。
manualTranslations.literal: The affair is fully set out in his biography.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The affair is told in full in his biography.

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋在禮初無亂心，以是日見迫而反爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Zaili initially had no rebellious intent and rebelled only because he was pressured on that day.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first he had no intent to rebel, and only rose because he was forced on that day.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖加以大惡之名，猶原其本心而異於他反者。
manualTranslations.literal: Although the name of a great evil is applied to him, his original intention is still considered and he is distinguished from other rebels.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though he is still given the grave name of rebel, his original state of mind is considered, setting him apart from other rebels.

manualTranslations.zh: 於此見凡書人善惡，不妄加之也如此。
manualTranslations.literal: From this one can see that whenever the text records people’s good and evil, it does not falsely impose them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This shows how carefully the text avoids falsely assigning good or evil to people.

manualTranslations.zh: 後唐太祖置義兒軍如李嗣昭等甚眾，初皆賜姓名，而不全若子，故書李嗣源者，書其所賜姓名爾，不以子書也，與友文、從珂異。
manualTranslations.literal: The Later Tang Taizu established an army of adopted sons, with many men such as Li Sizhao. At first all were granted surnames and names, but they were not fully treated as sons. Therefore when the text writes “Li Siyuan,” it records only the surname and name bestowed on him and does not write him as a son; this differs from Youwen and Congke.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Tang Taizu created an “adopted-sons army,” including many men such as Li Sizhao. They were originally granted surnames and personal names, but were not all sons in the full sense. Thus “Li Siyuan” records only the bestowed name, not a filial status, unlike Youwen and Congke.

manualTranslations.zh: 實皇后劉氏作教與繼岌使殺崇韜，而書「繼岌殺」者，繼岌將兵在外，后教非天子命，可止而不止。
manualTranslations.literal: In fact, Empress Liu issued an instruction to Jiji, sending him to kill Chongtao; but the text writes “Jiji killed” because Jiji was commanding troops away from court, and the empress’s instruction was not the Son of Heaven’s command, so he could have stopped it and did not.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In reality Empress Liu ordered Jiji to kill Chongtao. The text says “Jiji killed” because Jiji was commanding troops outside the court, and the empress’s order was not an imperial command; he could have refused, but did not.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋八月，梁人克澤州，唐末，澤、潞皆屬晉，梁初已得澤州，至此又屬晉，而梁克之，中間不見晉得澤州年月，蓋舊史闕不書。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, the Liang men took Ze Prefecture. At the end of Tang, Ze and Lu both belonged to Jin; at the beginning of Liang, Liang had already obtained Ze Prefecture; by this point it again belonged to Jin, and Liang took it. In between, no year or month is seen when Jin obtained Ze Prefecture, probably because the old history omitted it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In autumn’s eighth month Liang took Ze Prefecture. At the end of Tang, Ze and Lu had both belonged to Jin; early in Liang, Liang had already obtained Ze. By this point it again belonged to Jin, and Liang captured it. The intervening date when Jin recovered Ze is not found, probably because the old history failed to record it.

manualTranslations.zh: 五代之亂，戰爭攻取，彼此得失不常，多類此也。
manualTranslations.literal: In the disorder of the Five Dynasties, warfare and conquest brought gains and losses on both sides without constancy; many cases were like this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Amid the chaos of the Five Dynasties, war and seizure made territory change hands constantly; many cases were like this.

manualTranslations.zh: 守將裴約死之。

manualTranslations.zh: 君病不侍疾，以兵求立，罪當誅，故書「伏誅」。
manualTranslations.literal: His ruler was ill, and he did not attend on the illness; he sought enthronement with troops, and his crime deserved execution, so the text writes “was executed.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His lord lay ill, yet he did not attend him; instead he used troops to seek the succession. His crime deserved execution, so the text says “was executed.”

manualTranslations.zh: 其意以謂帝崩矣，懼不得立，而舉兵自助，非反，故不書反。
manualTranslations.literal: His intention was that he thought the emperor had died; fearing he would not be established, he raised troops to help himself. It was not rebellion, so it does not write “rebelled.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He acted because he believed the emperor had died and feared he would not be enthroned, so he raised troops in his own support. Since this was not rebellion, the text does not call it rebellion.

manualTranslations.zh: 乙未，侍衞親軍都指揮使康義誠殺三司使孫岳。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Kang Yicheng, commander of the imperial guards, killed Sun Yue, commissioner of the Three Fiscal Agencies.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，荊南自絕於中國而附吳，不足以有罪，不書討而書「伐」，見非內臣，不責其叛。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time Jingnan had cut itself off from the Central States and attached itself to Wu. It was not enough to constitute guilt, so the text does not write “punitive campaign” but writes “campaign,” showing that it was not an inner minister and was not held responsible as a rebel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At this time Jingnan had severed itself from the central realm and attached itself to Wu. That was not enough to make it guilty as an internal rebel, so the text says “campaign against” rather than “punish,” showing that it was not being treated as an inner subject whose rebellion was being condemned.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月壬子朔，幸會節園，羣臣買宴。
manualTranslations.literal: On the renzi new moon of the third month, he visited Huijie Garden, and the assembled ministers purchased a banquet.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the renzi new moon of the third month, he visited Huijie Garden, where the officials bought a banquet.

manualTranslations.zh: 遊幸若不過度，則小事也，皆不書。
manualTranslations.literal: If outings and visits are not excessive, they are minor matters and are all left unrecorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Imperial outings, when not excessive, are small matters and normally go unrecorded.

manualTranslations.zh: 惟莊宗及晉出帝之世則書者，著其過度耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Only in the reigns of Zhuangzong and the Later Jin’s Deposed Emperor are they recorded, merely to show their excess.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They are recorded only under Zhuangzong and the Later Jin’s Deposed Emperor, to mark their excess.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗於五代為勤儉之君，遊幸無過度，此書以著買宴，見君臣之失矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong was a diligent and frugal ruler among the Five Dynasties, and his outings were not excessive. This is written to mark the purchased banquet and show the fault of ruler and ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among the Five Dynasties rulers, Mingzong was diligent and frugal, and his outings were not excessive. This entry is written because of the purchased banquet, exposing the lapse by ruler and ministers alike.

manualTranslations.zh: 盧臺亂，殺其將烏震。
manualTranslations.literal: Lutai mutinied and killed its general Wu Zhen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lutai fell into mutiny and killed its commander Wu Zhen.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Congqian had murdered his ruler; because he was appointed to office rather than punished, the text records it.

manualTranslations.zh: 與在禮同罪宜誅，而書「殺」者，明宗亦同罪，不得行誅，故以兩相殺書之。
manualTranslations.literal: He had the same guilt as Zaili and deserved execution, yet the text writes “killed” because Mingzong shared the same guilt and could not carry out execution; therefore it records the two as killing one another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He shared Zhao Zaili’s guilt and deserved execution, but the text says “killed” because Mingzong was guilty in the same way and had no standing to execute him. The wording treats it as one guilty party killing another.

manualTranslations.zh: 十國外而不書，此書者，知祥本唐臣而反，至此改過自歸，絕之則嫌不許其自新，錄之則尚冀其遷善，然其來也，臣禮不備，故如夷狄書之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Ten Kingdoms are outside and are not recorded; this is recorded because Zhixiang was originally a Tang minister who rebelled, and at this point corrected his fault and returned of himself. To cut him off would risk seeming not to permit him to renew himself; to record him still hopes that he may move toward goodness. Yet when he came, the rites of a minister were not complete, so it records him like the barbarians.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Ten Kingdoms are normally outside the record, but this is entered because Meng Zhixiang had once been a Tang minister, rebelled, and now corrected his fault by returning on his own. To exclude him would seem to deny him a chance to reform; to record him leaves hope that he might turn toward good. But since his submission lacked the full rites of a minister, he is recorded in the manner of foreign peoples.

manualTranslations.zh: 實安重誨矯詔殺之，不書重誨殺者，明宗知而不責，又下詔書誣圜以罪，故以明宗自殺書之。
manualTranslations.literal: In fact, An Chonghui falsely issued an edict and killed him. The text does not write that Chonghui killed him because Mingzong knew and did not hold him responsible, and also issued an edict falsely accusing Huan of crimes; therefore it records him as killed by Mingzong himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In reality An Chonghui forged an edict and killed him. The text does not attribute the killing to Chonghui because Mingzong knew of it and did not punish him, and then issued an edict falsely charging Huan with crimes; it therefore records the killing as Mingzong’s own act.

manualTranslations.zh: 干戈之世，王道息而禮義亡，民猶有自知孝悌，而時君旌表，猶有勸民之意，故兩善而書之。
manualTranslations.literal: In an age of arms, the kingly way rested and ritual and righteousness disappeared, yet among the people there were still those who knew filiality and brotherly respect of themselves; and when the ruler of the time commended them, there was still an intention to encourage the people. Therefore both were good, and it is recorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In an age of war, the royal way had fallen silent and ritual principle had vanished, yet common people could still know filial and fraternal duty on their own. The ruler’s public commendation still aimed to encourage the people. Since both were good, the text records it.

sourceRange.text: 四月丁亥，莊宗崩。己丑，入洛陽。甲午，監國，朝羣臣于興聖宮。乙未，中門使安重誨為樞密使。殺元行欽及租庸使孔謙。壬寅，左驍衞大將軍孔循為樞密使。丙午，始奠于西宮，曰「始奠」，見其緩也。自己丑入洛，至此二十日矣。皇帝即位于柩前，柩前即位，嗣君之禮也。反逆之臣自立，而用嗣君之禮，書從其實而不變文者，蓋先已書反，正其罪矣。此書其實者，見其猶有自愧之心，而欲逃大惡之名也。易斬縗以衮冕。既用嗣君之禮矣，遽釋縗而服冕，故書以見其情詐。壬子，魏王繼岌薨。諸王薨不書，此書者，見明宗舉兵實反，會從謙弒逆，遂託赴難為名。及即位時，莊宗元子猶在，則其辭屈矣。甲寅，大赦，改元。渤海國王大諲譔使大陳林來。是月，張居翰罷。五月丙辰朔，太子賓客鄭珏工部尚書任圜為中書侍郎：同中書門下平章事。

manualTranslations.zh: 殺元行欽及租庸使孔謙。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingqin and Kong Qian, commissioner of grain and corvée, were put to death.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renyin Kong Xun, great general of the Left Valiant Guard, was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙午，始奠于西宮，曰「始奠」，見其緩也。
manualTranslations.literal: On bingwu the first offering was made at the Western Palace; it is written “first offering” to show how slow it was.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingwu the first offering was made at the Western Palace. The text says “first offering” to show how slow the rites were.

manualTranslations.zh: 自己丑入洛，至此二十日矣。
manualTranslations.literal: From jichou, when he entered Luoyang, to this point had been twenty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From jichou, when he entered Luoyang, twenty days had already passed.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇帝即位于柩前，柩前即位，嗣君之禮也。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor took the throne before the coffin; enthronement before the coffin is the rite of a successor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor took the throne before the coffin—enthronement before the bier is the rite of a legitimate successor.

manualTranslations.zh: 反逆之臣自立，而用嗣君之禮，書從其實而不變文者，蓋先已書反，正其罪矣。
manualTranslations.literal: A rebellious minister set himself up, yet used the rites of a successor. The text follows the fact without changing the wording because rebellion had already been written and his crime fixed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A rebel had set himself up, yet used a successor’s rites. The text records what happened without changing the wording because rebellion had already been written and his crime established.

manualTranslations.zh: 此書其實者，見其猶有自愧之心，而欲逃大惡之名也。
manualTranslations.literal: That the fact is written here shows that he still had a heart of self-reproach and wished to escape the name of great evil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Writing the fact here shows that he still felt shame and wished to escape the name of great villainy.

manualTranslations.zh: 易斬縗以衮冕。
manualTranslations.literal: He exchanged hemp mourning for imperial robes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He exchanged hemp mourning garb for imperial robes.

manualTranslations.zh: 既用嗣君之禮矣，遽釋縗而服冕，故書以見其情詐。
manualTranslations.literal: Having already used the rites of a successor, he suddenly cast off mourning and donned the crown robes; it is written thus to show his deceit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Having already used a successor’s rites, he suddenly cast off mourning and put on the crown robes; the text records this to expose his duplicity.

manualTranslations.zh: 壬子，魏王繼岌薨。
manualTranslations.literal: On renzi Prince of Wei Jiji died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renzi Prince Jiji of Wei died.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸王薨不書，此書者，見明宗舉兵實反，會從謙弒逆，遂託赴難為名。
manualTranslations.literal: When princes die it is not written; this is written to show that Mingzong’s raising of troops was in fact rebellion. When Congqian committed regicide he took the name of rushing to the rescue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Princes’ deaths are usually not recorded; this entry is written because Mingzong’s campaign was in fact rebellion. When Congqian committed regicide, he took refuge in the name of rushing to the rescue.

manualTranslations.zh: 及即位時，莊宗元子猶在，則其辭屈矣。
manualTranslations.literal: When he took the throne Zhuangzong’s eldest son was still alive, and his case was thereby weakened.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he took the throne Zhuangzong’s eldest son was still alive, which left his position indefensible.

manualTranslations.zh: 甲寅，大赦，改元。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiayin there was a general amnesty and a change of era name.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiayin there was a general amnesty and the era name was changed.

manualTranslations.zh: 渤海國王大諲譔使大陳林來。
manualTranslations.literal: Da Yinshen, king of Bohai, sent his envoy Da Chenlin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Da Chenlin arrived as envoy from Da Yinshen, king of Bohai.

manualTranslations.zh: 是月，張居翰罷。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: That month Zhang Juhun left office.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月丙辰朔，太子賓客鄭珏工部尚書任圜為中書侍郎：同中書門下平章事。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the bingchen new moon of the fifth month, Zheng Jue, guest of the heir apparent, and Ren Huan, minister of works, became vice directors of the Department of State Affairs and co-grand councilors.

sourceRange.text: 天成元年，實同光四年，而書「天成元年」者，大赦改元文見下可知。莊宗本紀自書「同光四年」，各從其所稱，既曰改元，不嫌二號也。郭崇韜、朱友謙皆以讒死，嗣源以名位高，亦見疑忌。趙在禮反於魏，大臣皆請遣嗣源討賊，莊宗不許，羣臣屢請，莊宗不得已，遣之。

manualTranslations.zh: 天成元年，實同光四年，而書「天成元年」者，大赦改元文見下可知。
manualTranslations.literal: The first year of Tiancheng was in fact the fourth year of Tongguang; that the text writes “first year of Tiancheng” can be understood from the amnesty and change-of-era text seen below.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tiancheng 1 was actually Tongguang 4; the reason the text writes “Tiancheng 1” becomes clear below, where the amnesty and era change are recorded.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗本紀自書「同光四年」，各從其所稱，既曰改元，不嫌二號也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong’s Basic Annals themselves write “fourth year of Tongguang”; each follows the designation it used, and since the era was changed, there is no objection to the two names.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong’s own annals write “Tongguang 4”; each annal follows the title used by its subject, and once an era change is stated, the two designations cause no problem.

manualTranslations.zh: 郭崇韜、朱友謙皆以讒死，嗣源以名位高，亦見疑忌。
manualTranslations.literal: Guo Chongtao and Zhu Youqian both died because of slander; Siyuan, because his reputation and position were high, was also viewed with suspicion and jealousy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao and Zhu Youqian both died through slander; Li Siyuan too, with his high reputation and rank, came under suspicion.

manualTranslations.zh: 趙在禮反於魏，大臣皆請遣嗣源討賊，莊宗不許，羣臣屢請，莊宗不得已，遣之。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao Zaili rebelled at Wei. The great ministers all asked that Siyuan be sent to punish the rebels; Zhuangzong would not permit it. The assembled ministers repeatedly requested it, and Zhuangzong, having no choice, sent him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili rebelled at Wei, the chief ministers all urged that Siyuan be sent against the rebels. Zhuangzong refused, but after repeated pleas from the court he had no choice and dispatched him.

sourceRange.text: 辛亥，幸康義誠第。四年春正月壬辰，回鶻使掣撥都督來。二月癸卯，王晏球克定州。王都自焚，故不書伏誅。辛酉，晏球獻馘俘。趙敬怡薨。丁卯，崔協薨。庚午，至自汴州。三月丙戌，殺姪從璨。夏四月，契丹寇雲州。癸丑，契丹使撩括梅里來求禿餒，殺之。甲寅，端明殿學士、尚書兵部侍郎趙鳳為門下侍郎兼工部尚書、同中書門下平章事。五月己巳，朝羣臣，賀朔。不曰視朝，而曰「賀朔」，著非禮。視朝常事，自不書爾。五月賀朔，出於道家之說，自唐以來用之，書之見亂世舉非禮之不急者。此禮其後屢行，皆不復書者，與入閤同。乙酉，追謚少帝曰昭宣光烈孝皇帝。契丹寇雲州。秋七月壬申，殺右金吾衞上將軍毛璋。八月乙巳，黑水使骨至來。丁未，吐渾首領念公山來。乙卯，党項折遇明來，己未，高麗王建使張彬來。九月癸巳，殺供奉官烏昭遇。冬十二月辛丑，殺西平縣令李商。

context.beforeSource: 十二月，李敬周克慶州，竇廷琬伏誅。
context.afterSource: 長興元年春正月丁卯，閱馬于苑。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: In spring of the fourth year, on renchen of the first month, the Uyghur envoy Chebo, military commissioner, arrived.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guimao of the second month Wang Yanqiu took Ding.

manualTranslations.zh: 王都自焚，故不書伏誅。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Du burned himself to death, so the text does not say he was executed after surrender.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛酉，晏球獻馘俘。
manualTranslations.literal: On xinyou Yanqiu presented severed ears and captives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On xinyou Yanqiu presented severed ears and captives.

manualTranslations.zh: 趙敬怡薨。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao Jingyi died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Jingyi died.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁卯，崔協薨。
manualTranslations.literal: On dingmao Cui Xie died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingmao Cui Xie died.

manualTranslations.zh: 庚午，至自汴州。
manualTranslations.literal: On gengwu he returned from Bianzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengwu he returned from Bian.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月丙戌，殺姪從璨。
manualTranslations.literal: On the third month, day bingxu, his nephew Cong Can was killed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingxu of the third month his nephew Cong Can was put to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏四月，契丹寇雲州。
manualTranslations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, the Khitan raided Yunzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In summer’s fourth month the Khitan raided Yun.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸丑，契丹使撩括梅里來求禿餒，殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: On guichou the Khitan envoy Liaokuo Meili came seeking Tuyi; he was killed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guichou the Khitan envoy Liaokuo Meili came seeking Tuyi and was put to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 甲寅，端明殿學士、尚書兵部侍郎趙鳳為門下侍郎兼工部尚書、同中書門下平章事。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiayin Zhao Feng, academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of War in the Ministry of War, was made Vice Director of the Chancellery, concurrently Minister of Works, and Co-Grand Councilor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiayin Zhao Feng, Duanming academician and vice minister of war, became vice director of the Chancellery, concurrently minister of works, and co-grand councilor.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月己巳，朝羣臣，賀朔。
manualTranslations.literal: On the fifth month, day jisi, he held court with the assembled ministers and celebrated the new moon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jisi of the fifth month he held court with the ministers and celebrated the new moon.

manualTranslations.zh: 不曰視朝，而曰「賀朔」，著非禮。
manualTranslations.literal: It does not say “audience at court” but says “celebrate the new moon,” marking it as contrary to ritual.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The text does not say “audience at court” but says “celebrate the new moon,” marking the act as unorthodox.

manualTranslations.zh: 視朝常事，自不書爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Audiences at court are routine affairs and are not written of themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Routine court audiences are not normally recorded at all.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月賀朔，出於道家之說，自唐以來用之，書之見亂世舉非禮之不急者。
manualTranslations.literal: Celebrating the new moon in the fifth month comes from Daoist teaching and has been used since Tang; writing it here shows a troubled age undertaking unorthodox matters that are not urgent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fifth-month new-moon celebration comes from Daoist teaching and had been used since Tang times. Recording it here shows a troubled age pursuing unorthodox and inessential rites.

manualTranslations.zh: 此禮其後屢行，皆不復書者，與入閤同。
manualTranslations.literal: This rite was performed repeatedly afterward and was no longer written of, the same as entering the inner hall.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This rite was performed repeatedly afterward without further record, as with entering the inner hall.

manualTranslations.zh: 乙酉，追謚少帝曰昭宣光烈孝皇帝。
manualTranslations.literal: On yiyou the late emperor was posthumously titled “Brilliant, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On yiyou the late emperor was posthumously titled “Brilliant, Propagating, Radiant, and Filial Emperor.”

manualTranslations.zh: 契丹寇雲州。
manualTranslations.literal: The Khitan raided Yunzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Khitan raided Yun.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋七月壬申，殺右金吾衞上將軍毛璋。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on renshen, the Right Golden Crow Guard general Mao Zhang was killed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renshen of autumn’s seventh month Mao Zhang, general of the Right Golden Crow Guard, was put to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月乙巳，黑水使骨至來。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, on yisi, the Heishui envoy Guzhi came.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On yisi of the eighth month the Heishui envoy Guzhi arrived.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁未，吐渾首領念公山來。
manualTranslations.literal: On dingwei the Tuhun chief Nian Gongshan came.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingwei the Tuhun chief Nian Gongshan arrived.

manualTranslations.zh: 乙卯，党項折遇明來，己未，高麗王建使張彬來。
manualTranslations.literal: On yimao the Tangut Zhe Yuming came; on jiwei Wang Jian of Goryeo sent Zhang Bin as envoy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On yimao the Tangut leader Zhe Yuming arrived; on jiwei Zhang Bin came as envoy from Wang Jian of Goryeo.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月癸巳，殺供奉官烏昭遇。
manualTranslations.literal: On the ninth month, day guisi, the palace attendant Wu Zhaoyu was killed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guisi of the ninth month the palace attendant Wu Zhaoyu was put to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬十二月辛丑，殺西平縣令李商。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter, in the twelfth month, on xinchou, Li Shang, magistrate of Xiping County, was killed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On xinchou of winter’s twelfth month Li Shang, magistrate of Xiping County, was put to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 敬達不書死之而書「殺」者，敬達大將，宜以義責光遠而誅之，雖不果而見殺，猶為得死，乃諷光遠殺己以叛，故書之如其志。
manualTranslations.literal: That Jingda is not written as dying for it but as “killed” is because Jingda was a great general and should have rebuked Guangyuan with righteousness and executed him; even if he failed and was killed, he would still have obtained a proper death, but instead he urged Guangyuan to kill him and rebel, so the text writes it according to his intention.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda is not said to have died for the cause but to have been “killed.” As a senior general, he should have rebuked Yang Guangyuan on grounds of duty and executed him; even if he had failed and been killed, that would still have been an honorable death. Instead he urged Guangyuan to kill him and rebel, so the text records the death according to his own intention.

manualTranslations.zh: 許御署官選。
manualTranslations.literal: The selection of yushu officials was permitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court permitted the selection of yushu officials.

manualTranslations.zh: 「御署官」，疑是廢帝初舉兵時所置之官，以其非吏部正授，故須有旨方得選。
manualTranslations.literal: “Yushu officials” were probably officials established when Feidi first raised troops; because they were not regular appointments by the Ministry of Personnel, an imperial order was required before they could be selected.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The “yushu officials” were probably offices created when Feidi first raised troops. Since they were not regular Ministry of Personnel appointments, they required an imperial order before they could be selected.

manualTranslations.zh: 此於事無勸戒，不必書，以舊史不詳，故存所不知，慎傳疑也。
manualTranslations.literal: This has no encouragement or warning in the matter and need not have been written; because the old history is unclear, it preserves what is not known, cautiously transmitting doubt.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The matter carries no lesson of praise or warning and did not need to be recorded; because the old history is unclear, the text preserves the uncertainty and carefully transmits the doubt.

sourceRange.text: __TOC__愍皇帝，明宗第五子從厚也。為人形質豐厚，寡言好禮，明宗以其貌類己，特愛之。天成二年，以檢校司徒拜河南尹、判六軍諸衞事，加檢校太保、同中書門下平章事。從厚妃，孔循女也，安重誨怒循以女妻從厚，三年，罷循樞密使，出從厚為宣武軍節度使。明年，徙鎮河東。長興元年，封從厚宋王，徙鎮成德。二年，徙鎮天雄，累加兼中書令。四年十一月，秦王從榮伏誅。明宗病甚，遣宦者孟漢瓊召王于鄴，而明宗崩，祕其喪六日。十二月癸卯朔，發喪于西宮，皇帝即位于柩前，羣臣見於東階，復于喪位。丙午，成服于西宮。二代五君，於此始見嗣君即位服喪之事，先君得其終，嗣君得其始，而免禍亂於臣民，於篡亂之世，稀見之事也，故特詳言之。庚戌，登光政門樓，存問軍民。辛亥，殺司衣王氏。癸丑，始聽政。乙卯，殺司儀康氏。丁巳，馮道為大行皇帝山陵使，戶部尚書韓彥惲為副，中書舍人王延為判官，禮部尚書王權為禮儀使，兵部尚書李鏻為鹵簿使，御史中丞龍敏為儀仗使，左僕射權判河南府盧質為橋道頓遞使。丁卯，禫。

items.sourceTextOverride: 愍皇帝，明宗第五子從厚也。為人形質豐厚，寡言好禮，明宗以其貌類己，特愛之。天成二年，以檢校司徒拜河南尹、判六軍諸衞事，加檢校太保、同中書門下平章事。從厚妃，孔循女也，安重誨怒循以女妻從厚，三年，罷循樞密使，出從厚為宣武軍節度使。明年，徙鎮河東。長興元年，封從厚宋王，徙鎮成德。二年，徙鎮天雄，累加兼中書令。四年十一月，秦王從榮伏誅。明宗病甚，遣宦者孟漢瓊召王于鄴，而明宗崩，祕其喪六日。十二月癸卯朔，發喪于西宮，皇帝即位于柩前，羣臣見於東階，復于喪位。丙午，成服于西宮。二代五君，於此始見嗣君即位服喪之事，先君得其終，嗣君得其始，而免禍亂於臣民，於篡亂之世，稀見之事也，故特詳言之。庚戌，登光政門樓，存問軍民。辛亥，殺司衣王氏。癸丑，始聽政。乙卯，殺司儀康氏。丁巳，馮道為大行皇帝山陵使，戶部尚書韓彥惲為副，中書舍人王延為判官，禮部尚書王權為禮儀使，兵部尚書李鏻為鹵簿使，御史中丞龍敏為儀仗使，左僕射權判河南府盧質為橋道頓遞使。丁卯，禫。

manualTranslations.zh: 愍皇帝，明宗第五子從厚也。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Min was Mingzong’s fifth son, Conghou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Min was Conghou, the fifth son of Mingzong.

manualTranslations.zh: 為人形質豐厚，寡言好禮，明宗以其貌類己，特愛之。
manualTranslations.literal: As a man he was broad and substantial in build, sparing of speech, and fond of ritual; Mingzong especially loved him because his appearance resembled his own.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was broad and solid in build, quiet, and fond of ritual. Mingzong loved him especially because he looked like him.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成二年，以檢校司徒拜河南尹、判六軍諸衞事，加檢校太保、同中書門下平章事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng, as acting Minister over the Masses he was appointed governor of Henan and supervisor of the Six Armies and the various Guards, and was additionally made acting Grand Guardian and joint manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng 2, with the title acting Minister over the Masses, he was appointed governor of Henan and supervisor of the Six Armies and the Guards; he was also given the titles acting Grand Guardian and joint manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

manualTranslations.zh: 從厚妃，孔循女也，安重誨怒循以女妻從厚，三年，罷循樞密使，出從厚為宣武軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Conghou’s consort was the daughter of Kong Xun; An Chonghui was angry that Xun had married his daughter to Conghou, and in the third year dismissed Xun as privy commissioner and sent Conghou out as military governor of Xuanwu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Conghou’s consort was Kong Xun’s daughter. An Chonghui was angered that Kong Xun had married her to Conghou; in the third year, Xun was removed as privy commissioner and Conghou was sent out as military governor of Xuanwu.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，徙鎮河東。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year, he was transferred to guard Hedong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year, he was transferred to the Hedong command.

manualTranslations.zh: 長興元年，封從厚宋王，徙鎮成德。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Changxing, Conghou was enfeoffed as Prince of Song and transferred to guard Chengde.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Changxing 1, Conghou was made Prince of Song and transferred to the Chengde command.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年，徙鎮天雄，累加兼中書令。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to guard Tianxiong and was repeatedly promoted up to concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was transferred to Tianxiong and eventually given the additional title concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年十一月，秦王從榮伏誅。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, Congrong, Prince of Qin, was executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, Congrong, Prince of Qin, was put to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗病甚，遣宦者孟漢瓊召王于鄴，而明宗崩，祕其喪六日。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong was gravely ill and sent the eunuch Meng Hanqiong to summon the prince from Ye, but Mingzong died, and his death was kept secret for six days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong became gravely ill, he sent the eunuch Meng Hanqiong to summon the prince from Ye. Mingzong then died, and his death was kept secret for six days.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月癸卯朔，發喪于西宮，皇帝即位于柩前，羣臣見於東階，復于喪位。
manualTranslations.literal: On the guimao new moon of the twelfth month, the mourning was announced in the Western Palace; the emperor took the throne before the coffin, the assembled ministers appeared at the eastern steps, and then returned to their mourning places.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the guimao new moon of the twelfth month, the death was announced in the Western Palace. The emperor ascended before the coffin; the assembled ministers presented themselves at the eastern steps and then returned to their mourning positions.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙午，成服于西宮。
manualTranslations.literal: On bingwu, mourning dress was completed in the Western Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the court formally assumed mourning dress in the Western Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 二代五君，於此始見嗣君即位服喪之事，先君得其終，嗣君得其始，而免禍亂於臣民，於篡亂之世，稀見之事也，故特詳言之。
manualTranslations.literal: In two dynasties and five rulers, only here is there first seen the matter of a successor ruler taking the throne and wearing mourning, with the former ruler obtaining his end and the successor ruler obtaining his beginning, and disaster and disorder being avoided among ministers and people; in an age of usurpation and disorder, this was a rarely seen affair, and therefore it is spoken of in special detail.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Across two dynasties and five rulers, this is the first case in which a successor took the throne and observed mourning: the former ruler had a proper end, the successor a proper beginning, and ministers and people were spared disaster. In an age of usurpation and disorder, this was rare, so the text records it in special detail.

manualTranslations.zh: 庚戌，登光政門樓，存問軍民。
manualTranslations.literal: On gengxu, he ascended the Guangzheng gate tower and inquired after the soldiers and people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengxu, he mounted the Guangzheng Gate tower and addressed the soldiers and people.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛亥，殺司衣王氏。
manualTranslations.literal: On xinhai, he killed the Wardrobe Attendant Lady Wang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On xinhai, he killed Lady Wang, the Wardrobe Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸丑，始聽政。
manualTranslations.literal: On guichou, he first heard government affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guichou, he first attended to government business.

manualTranslations.zh: 乙卯，殺司儀康氏。
manualTranslations.literal: On yimao, he killed the Ceremonial Attendant Lady Kang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On yimao, he killed Lady Kang, the Ceremonial Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁巳，馮道為大行皇帝山陵使，戶部尚書韓彥惲為副，中書舍人王延為判官，禮部尚書王權為禮儀使，兵部尚書李鏻為鹵簿使，御史中丞龍敏為儀仗使，左僕射權判河南府盧質為橋道頓遞使。
manualTranslations.literal: On dingsi, Feng Dao was made commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum, Minister of Revenue Han Yanyun was deputy, Secretariat Drafter Wang Yan was administrative judge, Minister of Rites Wang Quan was rites commissioner, Minister of War Li Lin was procession commissioner, Censor-in-chief Long Min was honor-guard commissioner, and Left Vice Director Lu Zhi, acting administrator of Henan prefecture, was commissioner for bridges, roads, stops, and relays.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Feng Dao was appointed commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum, with Minister of Revenue Han Yanyun as deputy. Wang Yan served as administrative judge, Wang Quan oversaw the rites, Li Lin the procession, Long Min the honor guard, and Lu Zhi the bridges, roads, lodging, and relays.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁卯，禫。
manualTranslations.literal: On dingmao, the dan sacrifice was performed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the concluding mourning sacrifice was performed.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Min had been buried in the precinct of Mingzong's Huiling and had no separate mausoleum name, so the text says "tomb." After Gaozu of Jin took the throne, he gave him the posthumous title Emperor Min.

manualTranslations.zh: 五代諸帝謚號不可為法，皆不足道，惟愍帝宜書者，嫌嘗降為鄂王也。
manualTranslations.literal: The posthumous titles of the Five Dynasties emperors cannot serve as models and are not worth speaking of; only Emperor Min ought to be written, because there is concern that he had once been demoted to Prince of E.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The posthumous titles of the Five Dynasties rulers are not models and generally need not be discussed. Emperor Min alone should be named, since he had once been demoted to Prince of E and that could cause ambiguity.

manualTranslations.zh: 而國亡禮闕，舊史、實錄皆無奏謚上冊月日，故雖當書而不得，因事而見於此爾。
manualTranslations.literal: But because the state had perished and the rites were deficient, the old history and the Veritable Records both lacked the month and day when the posthumous title was memorialized and the ce was presented; therefore, although it ought to have been written, it could not be, and it is merely shown here because of the event.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But the state had fallen and the rites were incomplete: neither the old history nor the Veritable Records gave the date when the posthumous title was proposed and the formal ce presented. So although it should have been recorded directly, it could not be; it appears here only because this incident brings it up.

manualTranslations.zh: 至此始見子得葬其父，故并祔廟詳書之。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only here do we first see a son able to bury his father; therefore the text records both the burial and the temple enshrinement in detail.

manualTranslations.literal: When Chudi came to the throne, envoys crossed back and forth without cease and could not be counted, so those of low office were all abbreviated and not written; Ban is written because he could not advance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Chudi took the throne, envoys came and went incessantly, too many to count, so those of low rank are generally omitted. Wang Ban is recorded because he was unable to proceed.

manualTranslations.zh: 古謂歲之一月，亦不云一，而曰正月。
manualTranslations.literal: In antiquity, the first month of the year was likewise not called the first month, but the correct month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In ancient usage, the first month of the year was not called “first month” either; it was called the first, or correct, month.

manualTranslations.zh: 國語言六呂曰元間大呂，周易列六爻曰初九。
manualTranslations.literal: The Discourses of the States, speaking of the six pitch-pipes, says yuan comes between and dalu; the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says initial nine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Guoyu, in discussing the six pitch-pipes, uses yuan in relation to Dalu, and the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says “initial nine.”

manualTranslations.zh: 大抵古人言數多不云一，不獨謂年為元也。
manualTranslations.literal: In general, when ancient people spoke of numbers, they often did not say one; it was not only that they called the year yuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, ancient writers often avoided saying “one” in numbering; calling the year yuan was not unique.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時天下無主，得其主則往歸之，與乎叛于彼而來於此者異矣。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time the realm had no ruler; when they found their ruler, they went and returned to him, which differs from rebelling from one side and coming to another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time the realm had no master. When people found one, they went over to him; that was different from defecting from one side to another.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢高祖非有德之君，惶惶斯人之無所歸者，猶得而歸也，故曰「歸」。
manualTranslations.literal: Gaozu of Han was not a ruler possessed of virtue, but these anxious people with nowhere to turn still found someone to return to; therefore it says “returned.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Han was no virtuous ruler, yet anxious people with no one to turn to could still find him and return; therefore the text says “returned.”

manualTranslations.idiomatic: On wuchen the state name was changed to Han. When Gaozu first founded the regime, it apparently had no declared dynastic name; the edicts gave no clear wording, so the text omitted it.

manualTranslations.zh: 然稱天福十二年，則國仍號晉可知，但無明據，故慎於所疑爾。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since the year was still called Tianfu 12, the state evidently still used the Jin name, but without explicit proof the text is cautious about the doubtful point.

manualTranslations.zh: 此書「改國號漢」，則未改之前宜有所稱，此可以推知也。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because this entry says “changed the state name to Han,” there must have been some prior designation; that much can be inferred.

manualTranslations.zh: 自隱帝崩後四十二日，周太祖始即位，而斷自帝崩書「漢亡」者，見帝而漢崩亡矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Forty-two days after Yindi died, Taizu of Zhou finally took the throne; yet cutting it off at the emperor’s death and writing “Han perished” shows that with the emperor Han had collapsed and perished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu of Zhou did not take the throne until forty-two days after Yindi died, but the text marks “Han perished” at the emperor’s death to show that Han fell with him.

manualTranslations.zh: 其太后臨朝，湘陰公嗣立，皆周所假託，非誠實，所以破其姦，故書曰「漢亡」，見周之立遲也，遲而難於自立，則猶有自媿之心焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The empress dowager’s holding court and the succession of the Duke of Xiangyin were both pretexts used by Zhou and were not sincere; to expose this deceit, it therefore writes “Han perished,” showing that Zhou’s establishment was delayed, and that in being delayed and finding it hard to establish itself, it still had some sense of shame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The empress dowager’s regency and the Duke of Xiangyin’s succession were Zhou pretexts, not realities. To expose that deceit, the text says “Han perished,” showing how slowly Zhou dared to establish itself; that delay shows it still felt some shame.

items.sourceTextOverride: 與晉高祖俱事明宗為偏將，明宗及梁人戰德勝，晉高祖馬甲斷，梁兵幾及，知遠以所乘馬授之，復取高祖馬殿而還，高祖德之。高祖留守北京，知遠為押衙。潞王從珂反，愍帝出奔，高祖自鎮州朝京師，遇愍帝于衞州，止傳舍，知遠遣勇士石敢袖鐵槌侍高祖以虞變。高祖與愍帝議事未決，左右欲兵之，知遠擁高祖入室，敢與左右格鬬而死，知遠即率兵盡殺愍帝左右，留帝傳舍而去。廢帝入立，高祖復鎮河東，已而有隙，高祖將舉兵，知遠與桑維翰密為高祖謀畫，贊成之。高祖即位於太原，以知遠為侍衞親軍都虞候，領保義軍節度使。契丹耶律德光送高祖至潞州，臨決，指知遠曰：「此都軍甚操剌」，世俗謂勇猛為「操剌」，錄其本語，「無大故勿棄之。」

manualTranslations.zh: 與晉高祖俱事明宗為偏將，明宗及梁人戰德勝，晉高祖馬甲斷，梁兵幾及，知遠以所乘馬授之，復取高祖馬殿而還，高祖德之。
manualTranslations.literal: He served Mingzong together with Gaozu of Jin as subordinate generals. When Mingzong fought the Liang at Desheng, Gaozu of Jin’s horse armor broke and Liang troops nearly reached him; Zhiyuan gave him the horse he was riding, then took Gaozu’s horse and covered the rear as they returned, and Gaozu was grateful to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He and Gaozu of Jin served Mingzong as subordinate commanders. At Desheng, Gaozu’s horse armor broke and Liang soldiers nearly reached him; Zhiyuan gave Gaozu his own mount, then took Gaozu’s horse and guarded the rear. Gaozu was grateful.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖留守北京，知遠為押衙。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu stayed behind to guard the Northern Capital, Zhiyuan served as chief adjutant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu held the Northern Capital, Zhiyuan was his chief adjutant.

manualTranslations.zh: 潞王從珂反，愍帝出奔，高祖自鎮州朝京師，遇愍帝于衞州，止傳舍，知遠遣勇士石敢袖鐵槌侍高祖以虞變。
manualTranslations.literal: When Congke, Prince of Lu, rebelled and Mindi fled, Gaozu came from Zhenzhou to court at the capital, met Mindi at Weizhou, and stopped at the courier lodge. Zhiyuan sent the brave man Shi Gan to hide an iron mallet in his sleeve and attend Gaozu in case of trouble.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Prince Congke of Lu rebelled and Mindi fled, Gaozu came from Zhenzhou toward the capital and met Mindi at Weizhou, where they stopped at the courier lodge. Zhiyuan sent the warrior Shi Gan to wait on Gaozu with an iron mallet hidden in his sleeve in case matters turned dangerous.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖與愍帝議事未決，左右欲兵之，知遠擁高祖入室，敢與左右格鬬而死，知遠即率兵盡殺愍帝左右，留帝傳舍而去。
manualTranslations.literal: Gaozu and Mindi discussed affairs without reaching a decision, and the attendants wanted to use force against him. Zhiyuan embraced Gaozu and took him into a room; Gan fought with the attendants and died, and Zhiyuan immediately led troops to kill all of Mindi’s attendants, left the emperor at the courier lodge, and departed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu and Mindi could not settle matters, the emperor’s attendants moved to seize Gaozu. Zhiyuan bundled Gaozu into an inner room. Shi Gan fought the attendants and died, and Zhiyuan then led troops in, killed all of Mindi’s attendants, left the emperor at the lodge, and went away.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝入立，高祖復鎮河東，已而有隙，高祖將舉兵，知遠與桑維翰密為高祖謀畫，贊成之。
manualTranslations.literal: After the Deposed Emperor entered and took the throne, Gaozu again governed Hedong. Before long there was a rift, and when Gaozu was about to raise troops, Zhiyuan and Sang Weihan secretly made plans for Gaozu and helped bring it about.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Gaozu returned to Hedong. A rift soon opened; when Gaozu prepared to raise troops, Zhiyuan and Sang Weihan secretly planned for him and helped make the revolt happen.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖即位於太原，以知遠為侍衞親軍都虞候，領保義軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne at Taiyuan, he made Zhiyuan chief aide of the Palace Guard and acting military governor of Baoyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu proclaimed himself emperor at Taiyuan, he appointed Zhiyuan chief aide of the Palace Guard and military governor of Baoyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 契丹耶律德光送高祖至潞州，臨決，指知遠曰：「此都軍甚操剌」，世俗謂勇猛為「操剌」，錄其本語，「無大故勿棄之。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Khitan Yelü Deguang escorted Gaozu to Luzhou, and at parting pointed to Zhiyuan and said, “This commander is very caola”; in common speech bravery was called “caola,” and the original wording is recorded; “Do not abandon him without a major reason.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yelü Deguang of the Khitan escorted Gaozu to Luzhou. As they parted, he pointed at Zhiyuan and said, “This commander is very caola”; common speech used caola for bravery, and the text preserves the original word; “Do not abandon him without serious cause.”

manualTranslations.literal: On renyin, the Khitan withdrew. They heard that Han had risen at Taiyuan, were afraid, and left; therefore the wording differs from simply leaving on their own. Dun is a term for retreating to avoid danger.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renyin the Khitan withdrew. Since they left out of fear after hearing that Han had risen at Taiyuan, the wording differs from ordinary departure: dun means a retreat or withdrawal.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozu loved him and intended to make him heir, but Chengxun died. Gaozu fell ill, grief worsened the sickness, and he entrusted Chengyou to the generals and ministers.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chancellor Su Fengji said, “The imperial son Chengyou has not yet been made a prince. Please enfeoff him immediately.”

manualTranslations.zh: 不書子者，榮於禮不得為子，不書子則當書其本姓，又不書者，周人所共諱。
manualTranslations.literal: It does not write “son” because according to ritual Rong could not be a son; if it did not write “son,” it ought to write his original surname, but that too is not written because it was what the Zhou people all avoided saying.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The text does not call Rong a son because ritually he could not be one. If it avoided “son,” it should have given his original surname, but it omits that too because the people of Zhou collectively tabooed it.
