manualTranslations.zh: 冬十月丙午，漢人來討，討加有罪，漢之於周，義所得誅。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on bingwu, the Han people came to punish. “Punish” means imposing punishment on guilt; as between Han and Zhou, Han had the righteous ground to execute them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingwu of winter’s tenth month, Han came on a punitive campaign. “Punish” is used for applying penalty to the guilty; in relation to Zhou, Han had the moral claim to execute them.

manualTranslations.zh: 攻自晉州。
manualTranslations.literal: They attacked from Jin Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The attack came from Jinzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 云「自晉州」者，見漢兵當誅罪人于京師，自晉州而入耳。
manualTranslations.literal: It says “from Jin Prefecture” to show that the Han troops ought to have executed the guilty men at the capital, and merely entered from Jin Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The phrase “from Jinzhou” shows that Han’s troops should have punished the guilty at the capital itself, and that Jinzhou was only their route of entry.

manualTranslations.zh: 攻城無得失不書，此書者，許漢來討。
manualTranslations.literal: When an attack on a city has no gain or loss, it is not recorded; this is recorded because the text approves Han’s coming to punish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An attack on a city is normally omitted if nothing is gained or lost; this one is written because the text recognizes Han’s punitive claim.

manualTranslations.zh: 在郑州新郑县。
manualTranslations.literal: At Xinzheng County in Zheng Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The tomb lay at Xinzheng County in Zheng Prefecture.

sourceRange.text: 顯德元年正月丙子，郊，僅而成禮，即以王判內外兵馬事。壬辰，太祖崩，祕不發喪。丙申，發喪，皇帝即位于柩前。於書封晉王，正其非子矣。其餘假竊嗣君之禮，不待譏貶而可知，故皆無異辭。右監門衞大將軍魏仁浦為樞密副使。二月庚戌，回鶻遣使者來。丁卯，馮道為大行皇帝山陵使，太常卿田敏為禮儀使。兵部尚書張昭為鹵簿使，御史中丞張煦為儀仗使，開封少尹權判府事王敏為橋道頓遞使，漢人來討，攻自潞州。

localRange.text: 显德元年正月丙子，郊，仅而成礼，即以王判内外兵马事。壬辰，太祖崩，秘不发丧。丙申，发丧，皇帝即位于柩前。右监门卫大将军魏仁浦为枢密副使。二月庚戌，回鹘遣使者来。丁卯，冯道为大行皇帝山陵使，太常卿田敏为礼仪使，兵部尚书张昭为卤簿使，御史中丞张煦为仪仗使，开封少尹权判府事王敏为桥道顿递使。汉人来讨，攻自潞州。

context.beforeSource: 是冬，卜以來年正月朔旦有事于南郊，而太祖遇疾，不能視朝者久之。
context.afterSource: 三月辛巳，大赦。
context.beforeLocal: 是冬，卜以来年正月朔旦有事于南郊，而太祖遇疾，不能视朝者久之。
context.afterLocal: 三月辛巳，大赦。

manualTranslations.zh: 于书封晋王，正其非子矣。其余假窃嗣君之礼，不待讥贬而可知，故皆无异辞。
manualTranslations.literal: In recording the enfeoffment as Prince of Jin, the annals correct the false claim of true sonship. The other usurped rites of a succeeding sovereign need no explicit censure or praise—the facts themselves make the impropriety plain, and so the text records them without further comment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By recording the enfeoffment as Prince of Jin, the annals expose the fiction that he was a true son. The other stolen rites of succession need no added rebuke or praise; the facts speak for themselves, and the text therefore gives them without comment.

sourceRange.text: 及北取三關，遇疾還京師，始封宗訓梁王，時年七歲。顯德六年六月癸巳，世宗崩。甲午，皇帝即位于柩前。癸卯，范質為大行皇帝山陵使，翰林學士竇儼為禮儀使，兵部尚書張昭為鹵簿使，御史中丞邊歸讜為儀仗使，宣徽南院使、判開封府事昝居潤為橋道頓遞使。秋七月丁未，戶部尚書李濤為山陵副使，度支郎中盧億為判官。八月庚寅，封弟熙讓為曹王，熙謹紀王，熙誨蘄王。壬寅，高麗遣使者來。九月丙寅，左驍衞大將軍戴交使于高麗。冬十一月壬寅，葬睿武孝文皇帝于慶陵。在鄭州管城縣。高麗遣使者來。

localRange.text: 及北取三关，遇疾还京师，始封宗训梁王，时年七岁。

context.beforeSource: 世宗即位，大臣請封皇子為王，世宗謙抑久之。
context.afterSource: 七年春正月甲辰，遜于位。
context.beforeLocal: 世宗即位，大臣请封皇子为王，世宗谦抑久之。
context.afterLocal: 七年春正月甲辰，逊于位。

manualTranslations.zh: 显德六年六月癸巳，世宗崩。
manualTranslations.literal: On guisi in the sixth month of Xiande 6 Shizong died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guisi in the sixth month of Xiande 6 Shizong died.

manualTranslations.zh: 甲午，皇帝即位于柩前。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiawu the emperor acceded before the coffin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiawu the new emperor took the throne before the bier.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸卯，范质为大行皇帝山陵使，翰林学士窦俨为礼仪使，兵部尚书张昭为卤簿使，御史中丞边归谠为仪仗使，宣徽南院使、判开封府事昝居润为桥道顿递使。
manualTranslations.literal: On guimao Fan Zhi was made commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum; Hanlin academician Dou Yan, commissioner of ritual; Minister of War Zhang Zhao, commissioner of insignia; Vice Censor-in-Chief Bian Guidang, commissioner of ceremonial guards; and Southern Court Privy Commissioner and acting Mayor of Kaifeng Zan Jurun, commissioner of bridges, roads, and relay stations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guimao Fan Zhi was named mausoleum commissioner for the late emperor; Dou Yan, Hanlin academician, oversaw ritual; Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, insignia; Bian Guidang, Vice Censor-in-Chief, ceremonial guards; and Zan Jurun, Southern Court privy commissioner acting as mayor of Kaifeng, bridges, roads, and relays.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋七月丁未，户部尚书李涛为山陵副使，度支郎中卢億为判官。
manualTranslations.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn Li Tao, Minister of Revenue, was made vice commissioner for the mausoleum, and Lu Yi, outer office director of the expenditure bureau, was made adjutant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the seventh month Li Tao, Minister of Revenue, became vice mausoleum commissioner, and Lu Yi of the expenditure bureau served as adjutant.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月庚寅，封弟熙让为曹王，熙谨纪王，熙诲蕲王。
manualTranslations.literal: On gengyin younger brothers Xi Rang were enfeoffed as Prince of Cao, Xi Jin as Prince of Ji, and Xi Hui as Prince of Qi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengyin his younger brothers Xi Rang, Xi Jin, and Xi Hui were enfeoffed as Princes of Cao, Ji, and Qi.

manualTranslations.zh: 壬寅，高丽遣使者来。
manualTranslations.literal: On renyin Goryeo sent envoys.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renyin envoys arrived from Goryeo.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月丙寅，左骁卫大将军戴交使于高丽。
manualTranslations.literal: On bingyin in the ninth month Dai Jiao, Grand General of the Left Tiger Guard, was sent as envoy to Goryeo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the ninth month Dai Jiao, Grand General of the Left Tiger Guard, was dispatched to Goryeo.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬十一月壬寅，葬睿武孝文皇帝于庆陵。
manualTranslations.literal: On renyin in the eleventh month of winter the Sagacious Martial Filial Civil Emperor was buried at Qingling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renyin in the eleventh month Shizong, the Sagacious Martial Filial Civil Emperor, was interred at Qingling.

manualTranslations.zh: 在郑州管城县。
manualTranslations.literal: At Guancheng County in Zheng Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The tomb lay at Guancheng County in Zheng Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 高丽遣使者来。
manualTranslations.literal: Goryeo sent envoys.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent envoys again.

sourceRange.text: 十二月丙戌，罷州縣課戶、俸戶。六年春正月，高麗王昭遣使者來。辛酉，女真使阿辨來。三月己酉，甘州回鶻來獻玉，却之。庚申，王朴薨。丙寅，宣徽南院使吳延祚留守東京。癸酉，停給銅魚。甲戌，北征。是月，吳延祚為左驍衞上將軍、樞密使。夏四月壬辰，取乾寧軍。辛丑，取益津關，以為霸州。癸卯，取瓦橋關，以為雄州。州縣廢置不書，此書，重復中國故地。世宗下三關，瓦橋、益津以建州及見，淤口關止置寨，故舊史、實錄皆闕不書，遂不見其取得時日，今信安軍是也。五月乙巳朔，取瀛州。復中國故地，故不書「契丹」。甲戌，至自雄州。六月癸未，立皇后符氏，符氏無國爵，不曰立符氏為皇后，嫌同於不正也。蓋其位先定而後娶，故書曰「立皇后符氏」，文理宜然，無褒貶也。封子宗訓為梁王、宗讓燕國公。戊子，占城使莆訶散來。己丑，范質、王溥參知樞密院事，魏仁浦同中書門下平章事。癸巳，皇帝崩于滋德殿。年三十九。恭皇帝，世宗第四子宗訓也。

localRange.text: 十二月丙戌，罢州县课户、俸户。恭皇帝，世宗第四子宗训也。

context.beforeSource: 十一月庚戌，作通禮、正樂。
context.afterSource: 世宗即位，大臣請封皇子為王，世宗謙抑久之。
context.beforeLocal: 十一月庚戌，作《通礼》、《正乐》。
context.afterLocal: 世宗即位，大臣请封皇子为王，世宗谦抑久之。

manualTranslations.zh: 六年春正月，高丽王昭遣使者来。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of spring in the sixth year King Zhao of Goryeo sent envoys.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xiande 6 King Zhao of Goryeo sent envoys.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛酉，女真使阿辨来。
manualTranslations.literal: On xinyou the Jurchen envoy A Bian came.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Jurchen envoy A Bian arrived.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月己酉，甘州回鹘来献玉，却之。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiyou in the third month the Ganzhou Uyghurs came to present jade; it was refused.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the third month the Ganzhou Uyghurs offered jade; the court declined it.

manualTranslations.zh: 庚申，王朴薨。
manualTranslations.literal: On gengshen Wang Pu died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengshen Wang Pu died.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙寅，宣徽南院使吴延祚留守东京。
manualTranslations.literal: On bingyin Wu Yanzuo, Southern Court privy commissioner, was left to guard the Eastern Capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingyin Wu Yanzuo, Southern Court privy commissioner, was posted to guard the Eastern Capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸酉，停给铜鱼。
manualTranslations.literal: On guiyou the issuance of bronze tally-fish was halted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guiyou the court stopped issuing bronze tally-fish.

manualTranslations.zh: 甲戌，北征。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiaxu the northern campaign began.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the emperor launched the northern campaign.

manualTranslations.zh: 是月，吴延祚为左骁卫上将军、枢密使。
manualTranslations.literal: That month Wu Yanzuo was made Grand General of the Upper Left Tiger Guard and privy commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That month Wu Yanzuo became Grand General of the Upper Left Tiger Guard and privy commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏四月壬辰，取乾宁军。
manualTranslations.literal: On renchen in the fourth month of summer Qianning command was taken.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renchen in the fourth month Qianning command fell.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛丑，取益津关，以为霸州。
manualTranslations.literal: On xinchou Yijin Pass was taken and made Ba Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On xinchou Yijin Pass was captured and established as Ba Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸卯，取瓦桥关，以为雄州。
manualTranslations.literal: On guimao Waqiao Pass was taken and made Xiong Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guimao Waqiao Pass was captured and established as Xiong Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 州县废置不书，此书，重复中国故地。世宗下三关，瓦桥、益津以建州及见，淤口关止置寨，故旧史、实录皆阙不书，遂不见其取得时日，今信安军是也。
manualTranslations.literal: The abolition and establishment of prefectures and counties is normally not recorded; here it is recorded because Chinese territory was recovered. Shizong took the Three Passes—Waqiao and Yijin were made prefectures and noted as such, while Yankou Pass was only garrisoned—so the old histories and veritable records all omit the record and the dates of capture cannot be seen; present-day Xin’an command is the case.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Changes to prefectures and counties are usually omitted; here they are recorded because old Chinese lands were recovered. Shizong took the Three Passes: Waqiao and Yijin were made prefectures and noted, but Yankou was only fortified, so earlier histories and veritable records left the captures undated—today’s Xin’an command is an example.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月乙巳朔，取瀛州。
manualTranslations.literal: On the new-year day yisi in the fifth month Ying Prefecture was taken.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the new-year day yisi in the fifth month Ying Prefecture fell.

manualTranslations.zh: 复中国故地，故不书「契丹」。
manualTranslations.literal: Chinese territory was recovered, and so the text does not say “Khitan.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because this was recovery of Chinese territory, the text does not say “Khitan.”

manualTranslations.zh: 甲戌，至自雄州。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiaxu the emperor returned from Xiong Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he returned from the Xiongzhou campaign.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月癸未，立皇后符氏，符氏无国爵，不曰立符氏为皇后，嫌同于不正也。盖其位先定而后娶，故书曰「立皇后符氏」，文理宜然，无褒贬也。
manualTranslations.literal: On guiwei in the sixth month Lady Fu was installed as empress. Because Lady Fu had no state enfeoffment, the text does not say “installed Lady Fu as empress,” avoiding the appearance of impropriety. Her rank had been fixed before the marriage, and so the wording “installed Empress Lady Fu” is fitting in form and carries no praise or blame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the sixth month Empress Lady Fu was enthroned. She held no state title, so the annals avoid saying “installed Lady Fu as empress” lest it seem irregular. Her status had been settled before the wedding, so the phrasing “installed Empress Lady Fu” is formally correct and carries no judgment.

manualTranslations.zh: 封子宗训为梁王、宗让燕国公。
manualTranslations.literal: His sons Zongxun and Zongrang were enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and Duke of Yan respectively.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Zongxun as Prince of Liang and Zongrang as Duke of Yan.

manualTranslations.zh: 戊子，占城使莆诃散来。
manualTranslations.literal: On wuzi the Champa envoy Puhesan came.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On wuzi the Champa envoy Puhesan arrived.

manualTranslations.zh: 己丑，范质、王溥参知枢密院事，魏仁浦同中书门下平章事。
manualTranslations.literal: On jichou Fan Zhi and Wang Pu were made participants in Privy Council affairs, and Wei Renpu became associate grand councilor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jichou Fan Zhi and Wang Pu joined Privy Council affairs, and Wei Renpu became associate grand councilor.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸巳，皇帝崩于滋德殿。
manualTranslations.literal: On guisi the emperor died in Zide Hall.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guisi the emperor died in Zide Hall.

manualTranslations.zh: 年三十九。
manualTranslations.literal: He was thirty-nine years old.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was thirty-nine.

sourceRange.text: 庚申，濠州團練使郭廷謂以其州來降。身居其地而來降者書「附」，再遇、廷謂雖以地降，既降而不居其地，故不書「附」而書「降」。廷謂不書「叛」，事見南唐世家。

localRange.text: 庚申，濠州团练使郭廷谓以其州来降。

manualTranslations.zh: 身居其地而来降者书「附」，再遇、廷谓虽以地降，既降而不居其地，故不书「附」而书「降」。廷谓不书「叛」，事见南唐世家。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who lived in the territory and came to submit are recorded with “attached.” Although Zaiyu and Tingwei surrendered their prefectures, once they surrendered they did not remain in their territory, and so the text does not say “attached” but says “surrendered.” Tingwei is not recorded as “rebelled”; the matter is treated in the Southern Tang house chronicle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Defectors who still held their posts are recorded as “attached.” Zaiyu and Tingwei surrendered territory but did not stay to hold it, so the text says “surrendered” rather than “attached.” Tingwei is not called a “rebel”; see the Southern Tang house chronicle.

sourceRange.text: 不書劉仁贍降，事見死節傳。蓋仁贍實不降，故書周自克之爾。「克」者，難取之名也，壽難取，則見仁贍之節著，不書「死之」者，仁贍自以病死，以其至死守節，故列之死節傳。

manualTranslations.zh: 不书刘仁赡降，事见死节传。盖仁赡实不降，故书周自克之尔。「克」者，难取之名也，寿难取，则见仁赡之节著，不书「死之」者，仁赡自以病死，以其至死守节，故列之死节传。
manualTranslations.literal: The text does not record Liu Renzan’s surrender; the matter appears in the Biographies of Those Who Died for Principle. Renzan in fact did not surrender, and so the annals say Zhou took the city by force. “Took by force” is the term for what is hard to capture; that Shou was hard to capture shows Renzan’s integrity. It does not say “died in the fighting” because Renzan died of illness; because he held the city to the end and kept his integrity, he is listed among those who died for principle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Renzan’s surrender is not recorded; see the Biographies of Those Who Died for Principle. Renzan never truly surrendered, so the annals say Zhou “took” the city—the word for a hard-won capture. Shouzhou’s difficulty shows Renzan’s steadfastness. The text does not say he “died in battle” because he died of illness; having held firm to the end, he belongs in the martyrs’ biographies.

manualTranslations.literal: The assault began on xinyou in the twelfth month of the fourth year; Yanqing and the others held firm for more than forty days before the city fell—clearly they neither fled nor surrendered, and so the text grants them “died in the fighting.” What matters is death itself; the annals need only record their great integrity.

Yanqing and the others held out more than forty days before the city fell—they plainly neither fled nor surrendered, so the text records their deaths. What counts is dying in place; the annals need only note their steadfastness.

sourceRange.text: 二年五代亂世，以嗣君即位者五，而改元不依古者四，梁末帝、晉出帝即位踰年，宜改元而不改，又明年然後改，漢隱帝、周世宗皆仍稱先帝年號，終其世不改，而本紀無譏者，但書其實，自見其失也。春二月，御札求直言。夏五月辛未，宣徽南院使向訓、鳳翔節度使王景伐蜀。甲戌，大毀佛寺，禁民親無侍養而為僧尼及私自度者。秋九月丙寅朔，頒銅禁。閏月癸丑，向訓克秦州。冬十月辛未，取成州。戊寅，高麗使王子太相融來。取階州。十一月乙未朔，李穀為淮南道行營都部署以伐唐。戊申，王景克鳳州。十二月丙戌，鄭仁誨薨。三年春正月，增築京城。庚子，向訓留守東京。

manualTranslations.zh: 二年五代乱世，以嗣君即位者五，而改元不依古者四，梁末帝、晋出帝即位逾年，宜改元而不改，又明年然后改，汉隐帝、周世宗皆仍称先帝年号，终其世不改，而本纪无讥者，但书其实，自见其失也。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year: in the chaotic age of the Five Dynasties, five successors took the throne, yet four did not change the reign title according to ancient practice. The Last Emperor of Liang and the Deposed Emperor of Jin, more than a year after accession, ought to have changed the era name but did not, changing only the following year. The Hidden Emperor of Han and Shizong of Zhou both kept their predecessors’ era names to the end without change, and the annals offer no censure—they simply record the facts, and the fault shows itself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Year two opens with Ouyang Xiu’s note: in the Five Dynasties’ chaos five heirs took throne, yet four broke ancient practice on era names. Liang’s last emperor and Jin’s deposed emperor waited more than a year; Han’s Hidden Emperor and Zhou’s Shizong kept prior reign titles for life. The annals do not rebuke them—they record facts, and the fault is plain.

sourceRange.text: 五代之亡，所書不同，隨事為文爾。「梁亡」見唐之速，「漢亡」見周之遲也。唐欺天下以討賊，周欺天下以立贇。故書「梁亡」，見唐之立速，則知其志不在討賊也；「漢亡」見周之立遲，則知立贇者偽也。唐亡無辭，莊宗之弒，唐已亡矣，而明宗又稱唐，愍帝之奔，唐又亡矣，而廢帝又稱唐，其亡也不可以屢書，故不書也。晉亡曰「契丹滅晉」，明言以深戒。周曰「遜于位」，遜，順也，能順乎天命也。嗚呼，五代本紀備矣！備，謂喪亂之事，無所不有。君臣之際，可勝道哉。

manualTranslations.zh: 五代之亡，所书不同，随事为文尔。「梁亡」见唐之速，「汉亡」见周之迟也。
manualTranslations.literal: The endings of the Five Dynasties are written differently, phrased according to the circumstances. “The Liang perished” shows how swiftly Tang arose; “Han perished” shows how slowly Zhou came.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each dynasty’s fall is worded differently as the facts require. “The Liang perished” shows Tang’s swift rise; “Han perished” shows Zhou’s delay.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐欺天下以讨贼，周欺天下以立贇。
manualTranslations.literal: Tang deceived the realm under the pretense of punishing rebels; Zhou deceived the realm under the pretense of enthroning Yun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tang fooled the empire with talk of punishing rebels; Zhou fooled it with talk of enthroning Yun.

manualTranslations.zh: 故书「梁亡」，见唐之立速，则知其志不在讨贼也；「汉亡」见周之立迟，则知立贇者伪也。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore “the Liang perished” shows Tang’s swift establishment and reveals that its aim was not to punish rebels; “Han perished” shows Zhou’s slow establishment and reveals that enthroning Yun was a sham.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: So “the Liang perished” exposes Tang’s haste and its sham crusade; “Han perished” exposes Zhou’s delay and the fraud of enthroning Yun.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐亡无辞，庄宗之弑，唐已亡矣，而明宗又称唐，愍帝之奔，唐又亡矣，而废帝又称唐，其亡也不可以屡书，故不书也。
manualTranslations.literal: Tang’s fall has no wording: Zhuangzong was assassinated and Tang was already dead, yet Mingzong still called himself Tang; Min-di fled and Tang died again, yet the Deposed Emperor still called himself Tang. Its deaths cannot be written again and again, and so they are not written.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Tang’s end cannot be repeated: after Zhuangzong’s murder Mingzong still claimed Tang; after Min-di’s flight the deposed emperor did too. The annals cannot record every death, so they omit them.

manualTranslations.zh: 晋亡曰「契丹灭晋」，明言以深戒。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin’s fall is written as “the Khitan destroyed Jin,” stating it plainly as a stern warning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin’s end reads “the Khitan destroyed Jin”—stated plainly as warning.

manualTranslations.zh: 周曰「逊于位」，逊，顺也，能顺乎天命也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou is written as “abdicated the throne”; to abdicate is to yield, to yield to Heaven’s mandate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou is written as “abdicated the throne”—yielding, obeying Heaven’s mandate.

manualTranslations.zh: 呜呼，五代本纪备矣！备，谓丧乱之事，无所不有。
manualTranslations.literal: Alas! The annals of the Five Dynasties are complete—complete in the sense that nothing of disorder and ruin is missing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas! The Five Dynasties annals stand complete—complete meaning that every calamity of the age is recorded.

manualTranslations.zh: 君臣之际，可胜道哉。
manualTranslations.literal: How much can be told of what passed between ruler and subject!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What can fully be told of the bond between ruler and subject!

manualTranslations.zh: 友珪以裀裖裹之寢中，祕喪四日。
manualTranslations.literal: Yougui wrapped him in bedding in the chamber and concealed the death for four days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yougui swaddled the corpse in the bedchamber and hid the death for four days.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃出府庫，大賚羣臣及諸軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Then he opened the treasury and gave great rewards to the ministers and the armies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then he opened the vaults and lavished gifts on court and camp.

sourceRange.text: 庶人友珪者，太祖初鎮宣武，略地宋，亳間，與逆旅婦人野合而生也。長而辯黠多智。博王友文多材藝，太祖愛之，而年又長，太祖即位，嫡嗣未立，心嘗獨屬友文。太祖自張皇后崩，無繼室，諸子在鎮，皆邀其婦入侍。友文妻王氏有色，尤寵之。太祖病久，王氏與友珪妻張氏，常專房侍疾。太祖病少間，謂王氏曰：「吾知終不起，汝之東都，召友文來，吾與之決。」蓋心欲以後事屬之。乃謂敬翔曰：「友珪可與一郡，趣使之任。」乃以友珪為萊州刺史。

context.beforeSource: 太祖幸西都，友文留守東京。
context.afterSource: 太祖素剛暴，既病而喜怒難測，是時左降者，必有後命，友珪大懼。

manualTranslations.zh: 庶人友珪者，太祖初鎮宣武，略地宋，亳間，與逆旅婦人野合而生也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yougui the Deposed: when Taizu first held Xuanwu and raided the lands between Song and Bo, he was born of a chance union with an innkeeper’s wife.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yougui, later the Deposed, was born when Taizu first governed Xuanwu and raided the lands between Song and Bo, of a chance union with an innkeeper’s wife.

manualTranslations.zh: 長而辯黠多智。
manualTranslations.literal: Grown, he was eloquent, cunning, and resourceful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As he grew he proved eloquent, shrewd, and resourceful.

manualTranslations.zh: 博王友文多材藝，太祖愛之，而年又長，太祖即位，嫡嗣未立，心嘗獨屬友文。
manualTranslations.literal: Youwen, Prince of Bo, had many talents; Taizu loved him, and he was the elder; when Taizu took the throne and no heir had been named, Taizu’s heart leaned to Youwen alone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Youwen, Prince of Bo, was gifted in many arts and Taizu loved him; he was also the elder son. When Taizu took the throne and no heir had been named, Taizu’s heart leaned to Youwen alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖自張皇后崩，無繼室，諸子在鎮，皆邀其婦入侍。
manualTranslations.literal: After Empress Zhang died and Taizu took no new empress, sons posted to commands each invited their wives to attend the court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Empress Zhang died and Taizu took no new empress, each son posted to a command invited his wife to attend at court.

manualTranslations.zh: 友文妻王氏有色，尤寵之。
manualTranslations.literal: Youwen’s wife, Lady Wang, was beautiful and Taizu favored her above all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Youwen’s wife, Lady Wang, was beautiful, and Taizu favored her above all.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖病久，王氏與友珪妻張氏，常專房侍疾。
manualTranslations.literal: In Taizu’s long illness, Lady Wang and Yougui’s wife Zhang attended him alone in his chambers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Taizu’s long illness, Lady Wang and Yougui’s wife Zhang attended him alone in his chambers.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖病少間，謂王氏曰：「吾知終不起，汝之東都，召友文來，吾與之決。」
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu briefly rallied, he told Lady Wang: “I know I will not recover. Go to the eastern capital, summon Youwen, and I will settle matters with him.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu briefly rallied, he told Lady Wang: “I know I will not recover. Go to the eastern capital, summon Youwen, and I will settle matters with him.”

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋心欲以後事屬之。
manualTranslations.literal: His heart intended to entrust the succession to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His heart intended to entrust the succession to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃謂敬翔曰：「友珪可與一郡，趣使之任。」
manualTranslations.literal: He then told Jing Xiang: “Give Yougui a prefecture and hurry him to his post.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then told Jing Xiang: “Give Yougui a prefecture and hurry him to his post.”

manualTranslations.zh: 乃以友珪為萊州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He then made Yougui prefect of Laizhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then made Yougui prefect of Laizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞明元年，妃病甚，帝遽冊為德妃，其夕薨，年二十四。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming the consort fell gravely ill; the emperor hastily created her Virtuous Consort; that very night she died, aged twenty-four.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 1 she fell mortally ill; the emperor rushed her creation as Virtuous Consort, and she died that night at twenty-four.

sourceRange.text: 郴王友裕字端夫，幼善騎射，從太祖征伐，能以寬厚得士卒心。太祖與晉圍黃鄴於西華，鄴卒荷矟登城罵敵，晉王使胡騎連射不能中。太祖顧友裕，一發中之，軍中皆大讙呼，晉王喜，遺友裕良弓百矢。太祖鎮宣武，以為衙內都指揮使。景福元年，太祖攻鄆，友裕以先鋒次斗門，鄆兵夜擊之，友裕敗走。太祖從後來，不知友裕之敗也，前軍遇敵多死。太祖至村落間，始與友裕相得。是時，朱宣在濮州，太祖乃遣友裕先以二百騎前，太祖後至，與友裕相失。太祖卒與敵遇，敗而走。敵兵追之甚急，前至大溝，幾不免，賴溝中有積薪，馬乃得過，梁將李璠等死者十餘人。

context.beforeSource: 於是追封存朗王、友寧安王、友倫密王。
context.afterSource: 冬，友裕取濮州，遂圍時溥於徐州。

manualTranslations.zh: 郴王友裕字端夫，幼善騎射，從太祖征伐，能以寬厚得士卒心。
manualTranslations.literal: Youyu, Prince of Chen, courtesy name Duanfu, was skilled at horsemanship and archery from youth; he followed Taizu on campaigns and could win soldiers’ hearts through generous forbearance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Youyu, Prince of Chen, styled Duanfu, was skilled at riding and archery from boyhood; on Taizu’s campaigns he won the troops through generous forbearance.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖與晉圍黃鄴於西華，鄴卒荷矟登城罵敵，晉王使胡騎連射不能中。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu and Jin besieged Huang Ye at Xihua; Ye’s soldiers shouldered spears, climbed the walls, and cursed the enemy; the Prince of Jin sent Mongolian riders to shoot in succession but none hit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu and Jin invested Huang Ye at Xihua. Ye’s men shouldered spears, scaled the walls, and hurled abuse; the Prince of Jin sent Mongolian archers to shoot in volleys, but none struck home.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖顧友裕，一發中之，軍中皆大讙呼，晉王喜，遺友裕良弓百矢。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu turned to Youyu; with one shot he hit; the whole army cheered; the Prince of Jin was pleased and sent Youyu a fine bow and a hundred arrows.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu looked to Youyu, who hit with a single shot. The army roared; the Prince of Jin was delighted and sent him a fine bow and a hundred arrows.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖鎮宣武，以為衙內都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu held Xuanwu, he made Youyu commander of the inner guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu governed Xuanwu, he made Youyu commander of the inner guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 景福元年，太祖攻鄆，友裕以先鋒次斗門，鄆兵夜擊之，友裕敗走。
manualTranslations.literal: In Jingfu 1, Taizu attacked Yun; Youyu led the vanguard and camped at Doumen; Yun troops struck by night and Youyu fled in defeat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jingfu 1 Taizu attacked Yun. Youyu led the vanguard and halted at Doumen; Yun forces struck by night and Youyu fled in defeat.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖從後來，不知友裕之敗也，前軍遇敵多死。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu came from behind, unaware of Youyu’s defeat; the forward units met the enemy and many died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu followed behind, unaware that Youyu had been beaten; the van met the enemy and many were killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖至村落間，始與友裕相得。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu reached a village and at last reunited with Youyu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu reached a village and at last found Youyu.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，朱宣在濮州，太祖乃遣友裕先以二百騎前，太祖後至，與友裕相失。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Zhu Xuan was at Puzhou; Taizu sent Youyu ahead with two hundred riders; Taizu followed but lost contact with Youyu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan was then at Puzhou. Taizu sent Youyu ahead with two hundred horsemen; Taizu came after and lost contact with him.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖卒與敵遇，敗而走。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu at last met the enemy, was defeated, and fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu at last met the enemy, was routed, and fled.

manualTranslations.zh: 敵兵追之甚急，前至大溝，幾不免，賴溝中有積薪，馬乃得過，梁將李璠等死者十餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: The enemy pursued hotly; reaching Dagou he was nearly caught, but firewood piled in the ditch let his horse pass; Li Fan and more than ten other Liang generals died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The pursuers pressed hard. At Dagou he was nearly taken, but firewood heaped in the ditch let his horse cross. Li Fan and more than ten other Liang officers died.

manualTranslations.literal: Yougui then changed clothes, went incognito into the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and met the commander Han Qing to plan the matter; that night Qing took five hundred personal troops to follow Yougui, mingled them with the Control Crane guards, and entered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yougui changed clothes, slipped into the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and plotted with its commander Han Qing. That night Han Qing brought five hundred personal guards with Yougui, mixed them among the Control Crane guards, and entered the palace.

sourceRange.text: 乾化元年，升宋州為宣武軍，以友諒為節度使。友諒進瑞麥一莖三穗，太祖怒曰：「今年宋州大水，何用此為！」乃罷友諒，居京師。太祖臥病，全昱來視疾，與太祖相持慟哭；太祖為釋友諒，使與東歸。貞明二年，全昱以疾薨。徙衡王友諒嗣封廣王。

manualTranslations.zh: 乾化元年，升宋州為宣武軍，以友諒為節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: In Qianhua 1, Songzhou was promoted to the Xuanwu army; Youliang was made its military commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Qianhua 1, Songzhou was raised to the Xuanwu army, and Youliang was made its military commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 友諒進瑞麥一莖三穗，太祖怒曰：「今年宋州大水，何用此為！」
manualTranslations.literal: Youliang presented an auspicious wheat stalk with three ears; Taizu raged: “Songzhou had great floods this year—what use is this!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Youliang presented an auspicious wheat stalk with three ears. Taizu raged: “Songzhou suffered great floods this year—what use is this!”

manualTranslations.zh: 乃罷友諒，居京師。
manualTranslations.literal: Youliang was dismissed and lived in the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Youliang was dismissed and remained in the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖臥病，全昱來視疾，與太祖相持慟哭；
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu lay ill, Quanyu came to see him; they clung to each other weeping;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu lay ill, Quanyu came to visit; they embraced and wept together;

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖為釋友諒，使與東歸。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu released Youliang and let him return east with Quanyu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu released Youliang and let him return east with Quanyu.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞明二年，全昱以疾薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In Zhenming 2, Quanyu died of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 2, Quanyu died of illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 徙衡王友諒嗣封廣王。
manualTranslations.literal: Youliang, Prince of Heng, was transferred to succeed the title Prince of Guang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Youliang, Prince of Heng, was transferred to succeed as Prince of Guang.

sourceRange.text: 曹氏封晉國夫人，後生子，是謂莊宗，太祖奇之，曹氏由是專寵。太祖性暴，怒多殺人，左右無敢言者，惟曹氏從容諫譬，往往見聽。及莊宗立，事曹氏尤謹，其救趙破燕取魏博，與梁戰河上十餘歲，歲嘗馳省其母至三四，人皆稱其孝。莊宗即位，冊尊曹氏為皇太后，而以嫡母劉氏為皇太妃。太妃往謝太后，太后有慚色。太妃曰：「願吾兒享國無窮，使吾獲沒于地以從先君，幸矣，復何言哉！」莊宗滅梁入汴，使人迎太后歸洛，居長壽宮，而太妃獨留晉陽。同光三年五月，太妃薨。七月，太后薨，謚曰貞簡，葬于坤陵。而太妃無謚，葬魏縣。太妃與太后甚相愛，其送太后于洛也，涕泣而別，歸而相思慕，遂至不起。太后聞之，欲馳至晉陽視疾，及其卒也，又欲自往葬之，莊宗泣諫，羣臣交章請留，乃止。而太后自太妃卒，悲哀不飲食，逾月亦崩。莊宗神閔敬皇后劉氏，魏州成安人也。莊宗正室曰衞國夫人韓氏，其次燕國夫人伊氏，其次后也，初封魏國夫人。后父劉叟，黃鬚，善醫卜，自號劉山人。后生五六歲，晉王攻魏，掠成安，裨將袁建豐得后，納之晉宮，貞簡太后教以吹笙歌舞。既筓，甚有色，莊宗見而悅之。莊宗已為晉王，太后幸其宮，置酒為壽，自起歌舞，太后歡甚，命劉氏吹笙佐酒，酒罷去，留劉氏以賜莊宗。先時，莊宗攻梁軍於夾城，得符道昭妻侯氏，寵專諸宮，宮中謂之「夾寨夫人」。莊宗出兵四方，常以侯氏從軍。其後，劉氏生子繼岌，莊宗以為類己，愛之，由是劉氏寵益專，自下魏博、戰河上十餘年，獨以劉氏從。劉氏多智，善迎意承旨，其佗嬪御莫得進見。

context.beforeSource: 」而曹氏亦自謙退，因相得甚歡。
context.afterSource: 其父聞劉氏已貴，詣魏宮上謁。

manualTranslations.zh: 曹氏封晉國夫人，後生子，是謂莊宗，太祖奇之，曹氏由是專寵。
manualTranslations.literal: Lady Cao was created Lady of Jin; later she bore a son—this was Zhuangzong. Taizu marveled at him, and from this Lady Cao enjoyed exclusive favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady Cao was titled Lady of Jin and later bore Zhuangzong. Taizu was delighted, and she became his favorite.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖性暴，怒多殺人，左右無敢言者，惟曹氏從容諫譬，往往見聽。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu was by nature violent; in anger he often killed people, and none at his side dared speak—only Lady Cao calmly admonished and persuaded, and was often heeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu was violent and killed in anger; no one dared speak except Lady Cao, who calmly remonstrated and was often heard.

manualTranslations.zh: 及莊宗立，事曹氏尤謹，其救趙破燕取魏博，與梁戰河上十餘歲，歲嘗馳省其母至三四，人皆稱其孝。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong came to power he served Lady Cao with especial care; rescuing Zhao, crushing Yan, and taking Weibo, he fought Liang on the Yellow River for more than ten years, each year galloping to visit his mother three or four times—everyone praised his filial piety.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As ruler Zhuangzong treated Lady Cao with great devotion. Through campaigns in Zhao, Yan, and Weibo and more than ten years of war with Liang on the river, he rode to see her three or four times a year, and all called him filial.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗即位，冊尊曹氏為皇太后，而以嫡母劉氏為皇太妃。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he invested Lady Cao as empress dowager and made his principal mother, Lady Liu, grand consort.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At his accession he made Lady Cao empress dowager and his chief mother, Lady Liu, grand consort.

manualTranslations.zh: 太妃往謝太后，太后有慚色。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand consort went to thank the empress dowager; the dowager showed shame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand consort came to pay respects; the dowager looked ashamed.

manualTranslations.zh: 太妃曰：「願吾兒享國無窮，使吾獲沒于地以從先君，幸矣，復何言哉！」
manualTranslations.literal: The grand consort said: “May my son enjoy the realm without end; that I may die and follow the late lord—this is fortune enough. What more is there to say!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand consort said: “May my son reign forever; if I may die and join my late husband, that is blessing enough—what more can I ask?”

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗滅梁入汴，使人迎太后歸洛，居長壽宮，而太妃獨留晉陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and entered Bian; he sent men to welcome the empress dowager to Luoyang, where she lived in Changshou Palace, while the grand consort alone remained at Jinyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After destroying Liang and entering Bian, Zhuangzong brought the dowager to Luoyang’s Changshou Palace; the grand consort stayed at Jinyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 同光三年五月，太妃薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Tongguang the grand consort died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tongguang 3 the grand consort died.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月，太后薨，謚曰貞簡，葬于坤陵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month the empress dowager died; her posthumous title was Zhenjian, and she was buried at Kunling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the dowager died, posthumously titled Zhenjian, and was buried at Kunling.

manualTranslations.zh: 而太妃無謚，葬魏縣。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand consort received no posthumous title and was buried in Wei County.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand consort had no posthumous title and was buried in Wei County.

manualTranslations.zh: 太妃與太后甚相愛，其送太后于洛也，涕泣而別，歸而相思慕，遂至不起。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand consort and the empress dowager loved each other deeply; when she saw the dowager off to Luoyang she wept in parting, and returning home she pined with longing until she fell ill and could not rise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The two women were deeply attached. Seeing the dowager off to Luoyang, the grand consort wept; home again, she pined until she took to her bed.

manualTranslations.zh: 太后聞之，欲馳至晉陽視疾，及其卒也，又欲自往葬之，莊宗泣諫，羣臣交章請留，乃止。
manualTranslations.literal: When the dowager heard, she wished to gallop to Jinyang to visit her in illness; when she died she wished to go herself to bury her. Zhuangzong wept and remonstrated, and officials submitted memorial after memorial asking her to stay, so she stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearing of her illness, the dowager wanted to ride to Jinyang; when she died, she wished to attend the burial. Zhuangzong wept and pleaded, and officials begged her to stay—so she did not go.

manualTranslations.zh: 而太后自太妃卒，悲哀不飲食，逾月亦崩。
manualTranslations.literal: From the grand consort’s death the empress dowager grieved and would not eat or drink; after more than a month she too died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the grand consort’s death the dowager grieved without eating; within a month she too was gone.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗神閔敬皇后劉氏，魏州成安人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong’s Empress Jing Shenmin, the Liu clan, was a native of Cheng’an in Weizhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong’s Empress Jing Shenmin, Lady Liu, came from Cheng’an in Weizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗正室曰衞國夫人韓氏，其次燕國夫人伊氏，其次后也，初封魏國夫人。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong’s principal wife was Lady Han of Weiguo; next was Lady Yi of Yanguo; the empress came after them and was first created Lady of Weiguo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His chief wife was Lady Han of Weiguo, then Lady Yi of Yanguo; the empress ranked after them and was first titled Lady of Weiguo.

manualTranslations.zh: 后父劉叟，黃鬚，善醫卜，自號劉山人。
manualTranslations.literal: The empress’s father, Old Liu, had yellow whiskers, was skilled in medicine and divination, and styled himself the Mountain Man Liu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her father, Old Liu, had a yellow beard, practiced medicine and divination, and called himself the Mountain Man Liu.

manualTranslations.zh: 后生五六歲，晉王攻魏，掠成安，裨將袁建豐得后，納之晉宮，貞簡太后教以吹笙歌舞。
manualTranslations.literal: When the empress was five or six, the Prince of Jin attacked Wei and raided Cheng’an; the lieutenant Yuan Jianfeng took her and brought her into the Jin palace, where Empress Dowager Zhenjian taught her to play the sheng and to sing and dance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At five or six she was taken when the Prince of Jin raided Cheng’an; Yuan Jianfeng brought her to the Jin palace, where Dowager Zhenjian taught her music and dance.

manualTranslations.zh: 既筓，甚有色，莊宗見而悅之。
manualTranslations.literal: After she put up her hair she was very beautiful; Zhuangzong saw her and was pleased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When she came of age she was strikingly beautiful, and Zhuangzong was taken with her.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗已為晉王，太后幸其宮，置酒為壽，自起歌舞，太后歡甚，命劉氏吹笙佐酒，酒罷去，留劉氏以賜莊宗。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong was already Prince of Jin when the empress dowager visited his palace, set out wine for his birthday, and rose herself to sing and dance. The dowager was greatly pleased, ordered Lady Liu to play the sheng to accompany the wine, and when the wine ended and she departed, she left Lady Liu to be given to Zhuangzong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong was Prince of Jin, the dowager visited his palace for his birthday feast and danced for joy. She had Lady Liu play the sheng, and when she left she gave Liu to Zhuangzong.

manualTranslations.zh: 先時，莊宗攻梁軍於夾城，得符道昭妻侯氏，寵專諸宮，宮中謂之「夾寨夫人」。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, when Zhuangzong attacked Liang forces at Jiacheng, he obtained Fu Daozhao’s wife, Lady Hou, who monopolized favor in all the palaces; within the palace she was called the Jiazai Lady.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, at Jiacheng, Zhuangzong took Fu Daozhao’s wife Lady Hou, who dominated the inner quarters; the palace called her the Jiazai Lady.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗出兵四方，常以侯氏從軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong marched in all directions he often took Lady Hou with the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On campaign he often took Lady Hou with him.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後，劉氏生子繼岌，莊宗以為類己，愛之，由是劉氏寵益專，自下魏博、戰河上十餘年，獨以劉氏從。
manualTranslations.literal: Later Lady Liu bore Jiji; Zhuangzong thought the child resembled himself and loved him, and from this Lady Liu’s favor grew ever more exclusive; from the descent on Weibo and more than ten years of war on the river, only Lady Liu accompanied him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Liu bore Jiji. Zhuangzong thought the boy resembled him and loved him; from then Liu alone shared his campaigns for more than ten years on the river.

manualTranslations.zh: 劉氏多智，善迎意承旨，其佗嬪御莫得進見。
manualTranslations.literal: Lady Liu was very clever and skilled at reading his wishes; the other consorts could not gain audience.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu was clever and adept at pleasing him; the other consorts could not approach.

manualTranslations.zh: 湣帝哀皇后孔氏，父循，橫海軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: The Last Emperor's Empress Ai, Lady Kong—her father Xun was military governor of the Henghai army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Ai of the Last Emperor, Lady Kong, was daughter of Xun, military governor of Henghai.

manualTranslations.zh: 后有賢行，生四子。
manualTranslations.literal: The empress had virtuous conduct and bore four sons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The empress was known for virtue and bore four sons.

manualTranslations.zh: 湣帝即位，立為皇后，未及冊命而難作。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne she was made empress, but before the enthronement rites could be completed calamity arose.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor succeeded she was named empress, but before the enthronement rites were finished disaster struck.

manualTranslations.zh: 湣帝出奔，后病子幼，皆不能從。
manualTranslations.literal: The Last Emperor fled; the empress was ill and the children young—none could follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor fled; the empress was sick and the children too young to follow.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝入立，后及四子皆見殺。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor entered and took the throne, the empress and all four sons were killed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor seized the throne, the empress and all four sons were put to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉高祖立，追謚曰哀。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he posthumously gave her the name Ai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu rose he posthumously named her Ai.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong's Sons

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Congmin, styled Shuda, was grave, quiet, and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

manualTranslations.zh: 初從莊宗為馬步軍都指揮使兼行軍司馬，明宗入立，遷皇城使、保義軍節度使，與討王都。
manualTranslations.literal: At first he followed Zhuangzong as commander of horse and foot armies and concurrent army marshal; when Mingzong took the throne he was made imperial city envoy and military governor of Baoyi and joined the campaign against Wang Du.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He first served Zhuangzong as commander of horse and foot and army marshal; when Mingzong succeeded he became imperial city envoy and governor of Baoyi and joined the campaign against Wang Du.

manualTranslations.zh: 歷鎮橫海、義武、成德、歸德、保義、昭義、河陽，封涇王。
manualTranslations.literal: He governed in succession Henghai, Yiwu, Chengde, Guide, Baoyi, Zhaoyi, and Heyang, and was enfeoffed Prince of Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He governed Henghai, Yiwu, Chengde, Guide, Baoyi, Zhaoyi, and Heyang in turn and was enfeoffed Prince of Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢高祖時，為西京留守，封秦國公。
manualTranslations.literal: Under Han Gaozu he was Western Capital regent and enfeoffed Duke of Qin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Han Gaozu he was regent of the Western Capital and made Duke of Qin.

manualTranslations.zh: 周廣順元年卒，贈中書令，謚曰恭惠。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in Guangshun 1 of Zhou; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat with posthumous name Gonghui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Zhou's first year Guangshun; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat and named Gonghui.

sourceRange.text: 從璋字子良，少善騎射。莊宗時，將兵戍常山，聞明宗兵變于魏，乃亦起兵據邢州。明宗即位，以為捧聖左廂都指揮使，改皇城使，領饒州刺史，拜彰國軍節度使，徙鎮義成。明宗幸汴州，從璋欲率民為貢獻，其從事諫以為不可，從璋怒，引弓欲射之，坐罷為右驍衞上將軍。居久之，出鎮保義，徙河中。長興四年夏，封洋王。晉高祖立，徙鎮威勝，降封隴西郡公。從璋為人貪鄙，自鎮保義，始折節自脩，在南陽頗有遺愛。天福二年卒，年五十一。

manualTranslations.zh: 從璋字子良，少善騎射。
manualTranslations.literal: Congzhang, style Ziliang, was skilled in horsemanship and archery from youth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Congzhang, styled Ziliang, was skilled in horsemanship and archery from youth.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗時，將兵戍常山，聞明宗兵變于魏，乃亦起兵據邢州。
manualTranslations.literal: Under Zhuangzong he commanded troops garrisoning Changshan; hearing Mingzong's troops mutiny at Wei, he too raised troops and seized Xingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong he garrisoned Changshan; hearing of Mingzong's mutiny at Wei, he too raised troops and seized Xingzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗即位，以為捧聖左廂都指揮使，改皇城使，領饒州刺史，拜彰國軍節度使，徙鎮義成。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was made commander of the left wing of the Sacred Guard, then grand envoy of the imperial city, prefect of Raozhou, military governor of Zhangguo, and transferred to govern Yicheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong succeeded he was made commander of the Sacred Guard's left wing, then imperial city envoy, prefect of Raozhou, governor of Zhangguo, and later transferred to Yicheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗幸汴州，從璋欲率民為貢獻，其從事諫以為不可，從璋怒，引弓欲射之，坐罷為右驍衞上將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong visited Bianzhou, Congzhang wished to lead the people in tribute; his staff officer remonstrated that it was improper; Congzhang in anger drew his bow to shoot him and was demoted to senior general of the Right Martial Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong visited Bian, Congzhang meant to lead the people in tribute; his aide protested; Congzhang drew his bow in rage and was demoted to senior general of the Right Martial Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 居久之，出鎮保義，徙河中。
manualTranslations.literal: After a long while he was sent out to govern Baoyi and then transferred to Hezhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After a time he was sent to govern Baoyi, then transferred to Hezhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 長興四年夏，封洋王。
manualTranslations.literal: In summer of Changxing 4 he was enfeoffed Prince of Yang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Changxing 4 he was made Prince of Yang.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉高祖立，徙鎮威勝，降封隴西郡公。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he was transferred to govern Weisheng and demoted to Duke of Longxi commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu rose he was moved to Weisheng and demoted to Duke of Longxi.

manualTranslations.zh: 從璋為人貪鄙，自鎮保義，始折節自脩，在南陽頗有遺愛。
manualTranslations.literal: Congzhang was greedy and base by nature; from his governorship of Baoyi he began to restrain himself and cultivate virtue, and at Nanyang left considerable goodwill.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Congzhang was greedy and coarse; from his time at Baoyi he began to reform himself and won goodwill at Nanyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 天福二年卒，年五十一。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in Tianfu 2 at fifty-one.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Tianfu 2 at the age of fifty-one.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗三后一妃：和武憲皇后曹氏生晉國公主；昭懿皇后夏氏生秦王從榮、湣帝；宣憲皇后魏氏，潞王從珂母也；淑妃王氏，許王從益之慈母也。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong had three empresses and one consort: Empress Wuhe, Lady Cao, bore the Jin State Princess; Empress Zhaoyi, Lady Xia, bore the Prince of Qin Congrong and the Last Emperor; Empress Xuanxian, Lady Wei, was mother of the Prince of Lu Congke; Chaste Consort Lady Wang was foster mother of Xu Wang Congyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong had three empresses and one consort: Empress Wuhe, Lady Cao, bore the Jin State Princess; Empress Zhaoyi, Lady Xia, bore Congrong, Prince of Qin, and the Last Emperor; Empress Xuanxian, Lady Wei, was mother of Congke, Prince of Lu; Chaste Consort Lady Wang was foster mother to Congyi, Xu Wang.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹氏、夏氏皆不見其世家。
manualTranslations.literal: Lady Cao and Lady Xia do not appear in the genealogies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Neither Lady Cao nor Lady Xia appears in the genealogies.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏氏無封爵，明宗未即位前卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Lady Xia held no enfeoffed title; she died before Mingzong took the throne.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady Xia bore no noble title and died before Mingzong ascended.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗天成元年，封楚國夫人曹氏為淑妃，追封夏氏晉國夫人。
manualTranslations.literal: In Tiancheng 1 of Mingzong, Lady Cao of Chu was made Chaste Consort and Lady Xia was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Mingzong's first year Tiancheng, Lady Cao of Chu was made Chaste Consort and Lady Xia was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 長興元年，立淑妃為皇后，而夏氏所生二子皆已王，乃追冊為皇后，謚曰昭懿。
manualTranslations.literal: In Changxing 1 the Chaste Consort was enthroned empress; both sons born of Lady Xia were already princes, so she was posthumously made empress with posthumous name Zhaoyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Changxing 1 the Chaste Consort was enthroned as empress; as both of Lady Xia's sons were already princes, Xia was posthumously canonized empress with the temple name Zhaoyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏氏，鎮州平山人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Lady Wei was a native of Pingshan in Zhenzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lady Wei came from Pingshan in Zhenzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 初適平山民王氏，生子十歲矣。
manualTranslations.literal: She first married a commoner of Pingshan named Wang and had borne a son of ten years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She had first married a commoner of Pingshan named Wang and bore a son who was ten years old.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗為騎將，掠平山，得其子母以歸。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong was a cavalry commander he raided Pingshan and took the mother and child home.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a cavalry commander Mingzong raided Pingshan and brought the mother and child away.

manualTranslations.zh: 居數年，魏氏卒，葬太原。
manualTranslations.literal: After several years Lady Wei died and was buried at Taiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Several years later Lady Wei died and was buried at Taiyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 其子是為潞王從珂。
manualTranslations.literal: Her son was Congke, Prince of Lu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her son was Congke, Prince of Lu.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗時，從珂已王，乃追封魏氏為魯國夫人。
manualTranslations.literal: In Mingzong's time, when Congke was already a prince, Lady Wei was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Lu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Congke was already a prince under Mingzong, Lady Wei was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Lu.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝即位，追尊魏氏為皇太后，議建陵寢，而太原石敬瑭反，乃於京師河南府東立寢宮。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne Lady Wei was posthumously honored as empress dowager; they planned to build a mausoleum, but when Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan they erected a resting palace east of Henan prefecture in the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor posthumously honored her as empress dowager and planned a mausoleum, but when Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan they built a resting palace east of Henan in the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 清泰三年六月丙寅，遣工部尚書崔儉奉上皇太后寶冊，謚曰宣憲。
manualTranslations.literal: On bingyin of the sixth month, Qingtai 3, Minister of Works Cui Jian was sent to present the empress dowager's seals and patent; her posthumous name was Xuanxian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the sixth month of Qingtai 3 the Minister of Works Cui Jian presented the empress dowager's seals and patent; she was posthumously named Xuanxian.

sourceRange.text: 秦王從榮，天成元年，以檢校司徒兼御史大夫，拜天雄軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。三年，徙鎮河東。長興元年，拜河南尹，兼判六軍諸衞事。從璟死，從榮於諸皇子次最長，又握兵柄。然其為人輕雋而鷹視，頗喜儒，學為歌詩，多招文學之士，賦詩飲酒，故後生浮薄之徒，日進諛佞以驕其心。自將相大臣皆患之，明宗頗知其非而不能裁制。從榮嘗侍側，明宗問曰：「爾軍政之餘，習何事業？」對曰：「有暇讀書，與諸儒講論經義爾。」明宗曰：「經有君臣父子之道，然須碩儒端士，乃可親之。吾見先帝好作歌詩，甚無謂也。汝將家子，文章非素習，必不能工，傳於人口，徒取笑也。吾老矣，於經義雖不能曉，然尚喜屢聞之，其餘不足學也。

manualTranslations.zh: 秦王從榮，天成元年，以檢校司徒兼御史大夫，拜天雄軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。
manualTranslations.literal: Congrong, Prince of Qin—in Tiancheng 1 was made Acting Minister of Education and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, appointed military governor of the Tianxiong army and Chief Minister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Congrong, Prince of Qin—in Tiancheng 1 he was made Acting Minister of Education and Censor-in-Chief, military governor of Tianxiong, and Chief Minister.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，徙鎮河東。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to govern Hedong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Hedong.

manualTranslations.zh: 長興元年，拜河南尹，兼判六軍諸衞事。
manualTranslations.literal: In Changxing 1 he was made Governor of Henan and concurrently judged the affairs of the Six Armies and palace guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Changxing 1 he was made Governor of Henan and given charge of the Six Armies and palace guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 從璟死，從榮於諸皇子次最長，又握兵柄。
manualTranslations.literal: When Congjing died, Congrong was eldest among the princes in order of birth and also held military power.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Congjing's death Congrong was eldest among the princes and held the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 然其為人輕雋而鷹視，頗喜儒，學為歌詩，多招文學之士，賦詩飲酒，故後生浮薄之徒，日進諛佞以驕其心。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet he was light and sharp in manner with a hawk's gaze; he delighted in Confucian learning, composed songs and poems, and gathered many literary men to versify and drink, so frivolous young men daily advanced flattery to swell his pride.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet he was quick-witted and sharp-eyed, fond of letters; he wrote verse, gathered scholars to drink and compose, and frivolous youths daily flattered him to feed his pride.

manualTranslations.zh: 自將相大臣皆患之，明宗頗知其非而不能裁制。
manualTranslations.literal: From generals and chancellors downward all were troubled; Mingzong knew well his faults but could not restrain him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Generals and ministers alike were alarmed; Mingzong knew his faults but could not check him.

manualTranslations.zh: 從榮嘗侍側，明宗問曰：「爾軍政之餘，習何事業？」
manualTranslations.literal: Once while Congrong attended at his side, Mingzong asked: "Besides military affairs, what studies do you pursue?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once while Congrong stood beside him, Mingzong asked: "Apart from military duties, what do you study?"

manualTranslations.zh: 對曰：「有暇讀書，與諸儒講論經義爾。」
manualTranslations.literal: He answered: "When I have leisure I read books and discuss the classics with scholars."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He answered: "When I have time I read and debate the classics with scholars."

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗曰：「經有君臣父子之道，然須碩儒端士，乃可親之。吾見先帝好作歌詩，甚無謂也。汝將家子，文章非素習，必不能工，傳於人口，徒取笑也。吾老矣，於經義雖不能曉，然尚喜屢聞之，其餘不足學也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong said: "The classics hold the way of lord and subject, father and son, yet only great and upright scholars should be approached. I saw the late emperor fond of composing songs and poems—quite pointless. You are a general's son; writing is not your training and you cannot master it; spread by word of mouth it would only invite mockery. I am old; though I cannot grasp the classics, I still like to hear them often—the rest is not worth learning."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong said: "The classics teach the bonds of lord and subject, father and son, but only great upright scholars are fit company. I saw the late emperor dote on verse—to no purpose. You are a soldier's son; letters are not your trade and you will not excel; let them circulate and you become a laughingstock. I am old; I may not grasp the classics, yet I still like to hear them—the rest is not worth your time."

sourceRange.text: __TOC__廢帝皇后劉氏，父茂威，應州渾元人也。后為人彊悍，廢帝素憚之。初封沛國夫人，廢帝即位，立為皇后。其弟延皓，少事廢帝為牙將，廢帝即位，拜宮苑使、宣徽南院使。清泰二年，為樞密使、天雄軍節度使。延皓為人素謹厚，及貴而改節，以后故用事，受賕，掠人園宅，在鄴下不恤軍士，軍士皆怨。捧聖都虞候張令昭以其屯駐兵逐延皓，延皓走相州。是時，石敬瑭已反，方用兵，而令昭之亂作。令昭乃閉城，遣其副使邊仁嗣請己為節度使。廢帝以令昭為右千牛衞將軍，權知天雄軍府事。已而遣范延光討之，令昭敗走邢州，追至沙河，斬之，屯駐諸軍亂者三千餘人皆死。有司請以延皓行軍法，廢帝以后故，削其官爵而已。

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝皇后劉氏，父茂威，應州渾元人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Liu of the Deposed Emperor—her father was Maowei, a man of Hunyuan in Yingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Liu, wife of the deposed emperor, was the daughter of Maowei of Hunyuan in Ying Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 后為人彊悍，廢帝素憚之。
manualTranslations.literal: The empress was by nature fierce and overbearing, and the Deposed Emperor had long feared her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She was fierce and domineering by nature, and the deposed emperor had always been afraid of her.

manualTranslations.zh: 初封沛國夫人，廢帝即位，立為皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: At first she was enfeoffed as Lady of Pei; when the Deposed Emperor took the throne, she was made empress.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She was first created Lady of Pei; when the deposed emperor acceded, she was enthroned as empress.

manualTranslations.zh: 其弟延皓，少事廢帝為牙將，廢帝即位，拜宮苑使、宣徽南院使。
manualTranslations.literal: Her younger brother Yanhao had served the Deposed Emperor in youth as a guards officer; when the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Yanhao was appointed Commissioner of the Palace Parks and Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Bureau of Palace Attendants.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her brother Yanhao had served the deposed emperor as a guards officer in his youth; on his accession Yanhao was made commissioner of the palace parks and of the southern court of the Bureau of Palace Attendants.

manualTranslations.zh: 清泰二年，為樞密使、天雄軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: In Qingtai 2 he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of the Tianxiong Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Qingtai 2 he was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of the Tianxiong Army.

manualTranslations.zh: 延皓為人素謹厚，及貴而改節，以后故用事，受賕，掠人園宅，在鄴下不恤軍士，軍士皆怨。
manualTranslations.literal: Yanhao had been plain and honest in character, but once elevated he changed his ways; because of his sister he wielded power, accepted bribes, seized others’ gardens and houses, and at Ye showed no care for the soldiers, so the troops all resented him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yanhao had been modest and honest, but once he rose in rank he changed his conduct; relying on his sister’s position he took power, accepted bribes, seized gardens and residences, and at Ye neglected the troops, who came to hate him.

manualTranslations.zh: 捧聖都虞候張令昭以其屯駐兵逐延皓，延皓走相州。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Lingzhao, chief inspector of the Pingsheng command, drove Yanhao out with the garrison troops under his command, and Yanhao fled to Xiangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Lingzhao, chief inspector of the Pingsheng command, expelled Yanhao with the troops stationed under him, and Yanhao fled to Xiangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，石敬瑭已反，方用兵，而令昭之亂作。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Shi Jingtang had already rebelled and war was underway when Lingzhao’s mutiny broke out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang had already rebelled and fighting was under way when Lingzhao’s revolt erupted.

manualTranslations.zh: 令昭乃閉城，遣其副使邊仁嗣請己為節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Lingzhao then shut the city gates and sent his deputy Bian Rensi to request that he himself be made military governor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lingzhao closed the city and sent his deputy Bian Rensi to ask that he be appointed military governor.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝以令昭為右千牛衞將軍，權知天雄軍府事。
manualTranslations.literal: The Deposed Emperor made Lingzhao General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guards and acting administrator of the Tianxiong headquarters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor appointed Lingzhao general of the Right Thousand-Bull Guards and acting administrator of the Tianxiong headquarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 已而遣范延光討之，令昭敗走邢州，追至沙河，斬之，屯駐諸軍亂者三千餘人皆死。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon afterward he sent Fan Yanguang to attack him; Lingzhao was defeated and fled to Xingzhou, was pursued to Shahe and beheaded, and more than three thousand mutinous garrison troops were put to death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then sent Fan Yanguang against him; Lingzhao was defeated, fled to Xingzhou, was pursued to Shahe and executed, and more than three thousand mutinous garrison soldiers were killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 有司請以延皓行軍法，廢帝以后故，削其官爵而已。
manualTranslations.literal: The authorities asked that Yanhao be dealt with under military law, but because of the empress the Deposed Emperor merely stripped him of office and rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Officials asked that Yanhao be punished under military law, but because of the empress the deposed emperor only removed his offices and titles.

sourceRange.text: 廢帝鎮鳳翔，重吉為控鶴指揮使，與尼俱留京師。控鶴，親兵也。愍帝即位，不欲重吉掌親兵，乃出重吉為亳州團練使，居幼澄於禁中，又徙廢帝北京。廢帝自疑，乃反。愍帝遣人殺重吉于宋州，幼澄亦死。重美，幼而明敏如成人。廢帝即位，自左衞上將軍領成德軍節度使、兼河南尹、判六軍諸衞事，改領天雄軍節度使、同中書門下平章事，封雍王。石敬瑭反，廢帝欲北征，重美謂宜持重，固請毋行。廢帝心憚敬瑭，初不欲往，聞重美言，以為然，而劉延皓與劉延朗等迫之不已，廢帝遂如河陽，留重美守京師。京師震恐，居民皆出城以藏竄，門者禁止之。重美曰：「國家多難，不能與民為主，而欲禁其避禍，可乎？」因縱民出。及晉兵將至，劉皇后積薪于地，將焚其宮室，重美曰：「新天子至，必不露坐，但佗日重勞民力，取怨身後耳！」后以為然。廢帝自焚，后及重美與俱死。

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝鎮鳳翔，重吉為控鶴指揮使，與尼俱留京師。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor held Fengxiang, Chongji was commander of the Crane-Controlled Guard and remained in the capital together with the nun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While the deposed emperor governed Fengxiang, Chongji served as commander of the Crane-Controlled Guard and stayed in the capital with the nun.

manualTranslations.zh: 控鶴，親兵也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Crane-Controlled were the emperor’s personal troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Crane-Controlled were the sovereign’s personal guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 愍帝即位，不欲重吉掌親兵，乃出重吉為亳州團練使，居幼澄於禁中，又徙廢帝北京。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Min Emperor took the throne, he did not wish Chongji to command the personal guard, so he sent Chongji out as regimental commissioner of Bozhou, kept Youcheng within the palace, and also moved the Deposed Emperor to the northern capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Min emperor acceded, unwilling to let Chongji command the personal guard, he posted Chongji to Bozhou as regimental commissioner, kept Youcheng in the inner palace, and transferred the deposed emperor to the northern capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝自疑，乃反。
manualTranslations.literal: The Deposed Emperor grew suspicious and rebelled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor grew suspicious and rose in revolt.

manualTranslations.zh: 愍帝遣人殺重吉于宋州，幼澄亦死。
manualTranslations.literal: The Min Emperor sent men to kill Chongji at Songzhou, and Youcheng also died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Min emperor sent agents to kill Chongji at Songzhou, and Youcheng died as well.

manualTranslations.zh: 重美，幼而明敏如成人。
manualTranslations.literal: Chongmei from childhood was bright and keen like an adult.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chongmei had been clever and quick-witted from childhood, like a grown man.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝即位，自左衞上將軍領成德軍節度使、兼河南尹、判六軍諸衞事，改領天雄軍節度使、同中書門下平章事，封雍王。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Chongmei rose from General of the Left Guard to military governor of the Chengde Army, concurrently Grand Guardian of Henan and overseer of the Six Armies and all guards; he was then transferred to military governor of the Tianxiong Army, made Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor acceded, Chongmei advanced from general of the Left Guard to military governor of the Chengde Army, concurrently grand guardian of Henan and overseer of the Six Armies and all guards; he was then transferred to military governor of the Tianxiong Army, made grand councilor, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.

manualTranslations.zh: 石敬瑭反，廢帝欲北征，重美謂宜持重，固請毋行。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shi Jingtang rebelled, the Deposed Emperor wished to campaign north; Chongmei said he should act with restraint and firmly begged him not to go.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang rebelled, the deposed emperor wanted to march north; Chongmei urged caution and firmly pleaded that he not go.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝心憚敬瑭，初不欲往，聞重美言，以為然，而劉延皓與劉延朗等迫之不已，廢帝遂如河陽，留重美守京師。
manualTranslations.literal: The Deposed Emperor inwardly feared Jingtang and at first did not wish to go; hearing Chongmei’s words, he thought them right, but Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang, and others pressed him without cease, so the Deposed Emperor went on to Heyang and left Chongmei to guard the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor feared Jingtang and at first did not want to march; hearing Chongmei, he agreed, but Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang, and others kept pressing him, so he proceeded to Heyang and left Chongmei to hold the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 京師震恐，居民皆出城以藏竄，門者禁止之。
manualTranslations.literal: The capital was shaken with terror; residents all left the city to hide, and the gatekeepers forbade it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The capital was gripped by panic; residents fled the city to hide, and gatekeepers tried to stop them.

manualTranslations.zh: 重美曰：「國家多難，不能與民為主，而欲禁其避禍，可乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: Chongmei said: “The state is in great difficulty; we cannot act as masters for the people, yet would forbid them to flee harm—can that be right?”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chongmei said, “The realm is in grave trouble; we cannot protect the people, yet would forbid them to escape disaster—how can that be right?”

manualTranslations.zh: 因縱民出。
manualTranslations.literal: He therefore let the people leave.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He therefore allowed the people to go out.

manualTranslations.zh: 及晉兵將至，劉皇后積薪于地，將焚其宮室，重美曰：「新天子至，必不露坐，但佗日重勞民力，取怨身後耳！」
manualTranslations.literal: When the Jin army was about to arrive, Empress Liu piled firewood on the ground and was about to burn the palace halls. Chongmei said: “When the new Son of Heaven comes, he will surely not sit in the open; this would only later overburden the people’s strength and win resentment after death!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As the Jin army neared, Empress Liu heaped firewood to burn the palace. Chongmei said, “When the new emperor arrives he will not sit in the open air; this would only waste the people’s labor later and bring hatred after our deaths!”

manualTranslations.zh: 后以為然。
manualTranslations.literal: The empress thought him right.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The empress agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝自焚，后及重美與俱死。
manualTranslations.literal: The Deposed Emperor burned himself; the empress and Chongmei died with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor set himself afire; the empress and Chongmei perished with him.

items.sourceTextOverride: 壽王重乂字弘理，為人好學，頗知兵法。高祖即位，拜左驍衛大將軍。高祖幸汴州，以為東都留守。張從賓反，攻河南，見殺，時年十九，贈太傅。天福七年正月，加贈太尉，追封壽王。出帝天福八年五月，加贈太師。皆無子。

manualTranslations.zh: 壽王重乂字弘理，為人好學，頗知兵法。
manualTranslations.literal: Prince of Shou Chongyi, styled Hongli, loved learning and was well versed in military arts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prince of Shou Chongyi, styled Hongli, loved learning and knew military affairs well.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖即位，拜左驍衛大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed Grand General of the Left Flying Cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made grand general of the Left Flying Cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖幸汴州，以為東都留守。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu visited Bianzhou, he was made eastern capital commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu visited Bianzhou, he was made eastern capital commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 張從賓反，攻河南，見殺，時年十九，贈太傅。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Congbin rebelled and attacked Henan; he was killed—aged nineteen—and granted Grand Tutor posthumously.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Congbin rebelled and attacked Henan; Chongyi was killed at nineteen and posthumously granted Grand Tutor.

manualTranslations.zh: 天福七年正月，加贈太尉，追封壽王。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of the seventh Tianfu year, he was additionally granted Grand Commandant and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Shou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianfu 7 he was additionally made Grand Commandant and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Shou.

manualTranslations.zh: 出帝天福八年五月，加贈太師。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth Tianfu year under the Fleeing Emperor, he was additionally granted Grand Preceptor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu 8 under the Fleeing Emperor, he was additionally made Grand Preceptor.

manualTranslations.zh: 皆無子。
manualTranslations.literal: He had no sons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sourceRange.text: 敬贇字德和，少無賴，竄身民間。高祖使人求得之，補太原牙將。即位，以為飛龍皇城使，累遷曹州防禦使。天福五年冬，拜河陽三城節度使。敬贇性貪暴，高祖為擇賢佐吏輔之，而敬贇亦憚高祖嚴，未嘗敢犯法。歲餘，徙鎮保義。出帝時，加同中書門下平章事，始漸驕恣。帝嘗遣使者至，必問曰：「小姪安否？」陝人苦其暴虐，召還京師，以其皇叔不能責也，斥其元從都押衙蘇彥存、鄭溫遇以警之。契丹犯邊，敬贇從出帝幸澶淵，使以兵備汶陽，守麻家渡，未嘗見敵，皆無功。開運元年七月，復出為威勝軍節度使。歲餘，出帝以曹州為威信軍，授敬贇節度使。在曹貪暴尤甚，久之，召還。張彥澤兵犯京師，敬贇夜走，踰城東垣，墮沙濠溺死，時年四十九。

localRange.text: 從兄敬赟從弟韓王敬暉

context.beforeSource: 出帝天福八年五月，加贈三皇叔皆為太師，而皇伯敬儒始追封宋王，亦加贈太師。
context.afterSource: 韓王敬暉字德昭，為人厚重剛直，勇而多智，高祖尤愛之。

items.sourceTextOverride: 敬赟字德和，少無賴，竄身民間。高祖使人求得之，補太原牙將。即位，以為飛龍皇城使，累遷曹州防禦使。天福五年冬，拜河陽三城節度使。敬赟性貪暴，高祖為擇賢佐吏輔之，而敬赟亦憚高祖嚴，未嘗敢犯法。歲餘，徙鎮保義。出帝時，加同中書門下平章事，始漸驕恣。帝嘗遣使者至，必問曰：「小姪安否？」陝人苦其暴虐，召還京師，以其皇叔不能責也，斥其元從都押衙蘇彥存、鄭溫遇以警之。契丹犯邊，敬赟從出帝幸澶淵，使以兵備汶陽，守麻家渡，未嘗見敵，皆無功。開運元年七月，復出為威勝軍節度使。歲餘，出帝以曹州為威信軍，授敬赟節度使。在曹貪暴尤甚，久之，召還。張彥澤兵犯京師，敬赟夜走，踰城東垣，墮沙濠溺死，時年四十九。

manualTranslations.zh: 敬赟字德和，少無賴，竄身民間。
manualTranslations.literal: Jingyun, styled Dehe, was dissolute in youth and hid among the common people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingyun, styled Dehe, was unruly in youth and hid among the common people.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖使人求得之，補太原牙將。
manualTranslations.literal: Gaozu sent men to find him and made him a Taiyuan guards officer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent men to find him and appointed him a Taiyuan guards officer.

manualTranslations.zh: 即位，以為飛龍皇城使，累遷曹州防禦使。
manualTranslations.literal: On accession Gaozu made him Flying Dragon imperial-city commissioner; he rose to defense commissioner of Caozhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On accession Gaozu made him Flying Dragon imperial-city commissioner and later raised him to defense commissioner of Caozhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 天福五年冬，拜河陽三城節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the winter of the fifth Tianfu year he was appointed military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the winter of Tianfu 5 he was made military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 敬赟性貪暴，高祖為擇賢佐吏輔之，而敬赟亦憚高祖嚴，未嘗敢犯法。
manualTranslations.literal: Jingyun was greedy and violent; Gaozu chose worthy assistants to aid him, and Jingyun also feared Gaozu's severity and never dared break the law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingyun was greedy and brutal; Gaozu chose worthy aides to assist him, and Jingyun also feared Gaozu's stern rule and never dared violate the law.

manualTranslations.zh: 歲餘，徙鎮保義。
manualTranslations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Baoyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to Baoyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 出帝時，加同中書門下平章事，始漸驕恣。
manualTranslations.literal: Under the Fleeing Emperor he was made Associate Chief Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery and began to grow arrogant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the Fleeing Emperor he was made associate chief councilor and began to grow arrogant and unrestrained.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝嘗遣使者至，必問曰：「小姪安否？」
manualTranslations.literal: When the emperor sent envoys, he always asked: "Is my little nephew well?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor sent envoys, he always asked: "Is my little nephew well?"

manualTranslations.zh: 陝人苦其暴虐，召還京師，以其皇叔不能責也，斥其元從都押衙蘇彥存、鄭溫遇以警之。
manualTranslations.literal: The people of Shaan suffered under his brutality; he was recalled to the capital. Because his imperial uncle could not hold him accountable, his original followers Chief Custodian Su Yancun and Zheng Wenyun were demoted as a warning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people of Shaan suffered under his cruelty; he was recalled to the capital. Because his imperial uncle could not restrain him, his original followers Chief Custodian Su Yancun and Zheng Wenyun were demoted as a warning.

manualTranslations.zh: 契丹犯邊，敬赟從出帝幸澶淵，使以兵備汶陽，守麻家渡，未嘗見敵，皆無功。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Khitan raided the frontier, Jingyun followed the Fleeing Emperor to Chanyuan and was ordered to guard Wenyang and hold Majia Ford; he never met the enemy and achieved nothing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the frontier, Jingyun followed the Fleeing Emperor to Chanyuan and was ordered to secure Wenyang and hold Majia Ford; he never met the enemy and won no success.

manualTranslations.zh: 開運元年七月，復出為威勝軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the first Kaiyun year he was again made military commissioner of Weisheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyun 1 he was again made military commissioner of Weisheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 歲餘，出帝以曹州為威信軍，授敬赟節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: After more than a year the Fleeing Emperor made Caozhou into Weixin Army and appointed Jingyun its commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After more than a year the Fleeing Emperor made Caozhou into Weixin Army and appointed Jingyun its commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 在曹貪暴尤甚，久之，召還。
manualTranslations.literal: At Cao he was greedier and crueler than ever; after a long while he was recalled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Cao he was greedier and more brutal than ever; after a long while he was recalled.

manualTranslations.zh: 張彥澤兵犯京師，敬赟夜走，踰城東垣，墮沙濠溺死，時年四十九。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhang Yanze's troops invaded the capital, Jingyun fled by night, climbed the eastern wall, fell into the sand moat, and drowned—aged forty-nine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yanze's troops invaded the capital, Jingyun fled by night, climbed the eastern wall, fell into the sand moat, and drowned at forty-nine.

context.afterSource: 陳王重杲，高祖幼子也。

manualTranslations.zh: 隱帝，舊史、實錄皆無皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: The Hidden Emperor: the old histories and true records all have no empress.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor: older histories and the Veritable Records record no empress.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝立三年崩，時年二十，蓋未嘗立后也。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor reigned three years and died; he was then twenty years old—apparently he never installed an empress.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He reigned three years and died at twenty—he never seems to have taken an empress.

sourceRange.text: 夫史之闕文，可不慎哉。

context.beforeSource: 當王彥超之攻徐州也，周嘗遣人招庭美等，予得其詔書四，皆言庭美等嘗已送款於周，後懼罪而復叛，然庭美等款狀亦不見，是皆不可知也。
context.afterSource: 其疑以傳疑，則信者信矣。

sourceRange.text: __TOC__高祖皇后李氏，晉陽人也，其父為農。高祖少為軍卒，牧馬晉陽，夜入其家劫取之。高祖已貴，封魏國夫人，生隱帝。開運四年，高祖起兵太原，賞軍士，帑藏不足充，欲斂於民。后諫曰：「方今起事，號為義兵，民未知惠而先奪其財，殆非新天子所以救民之意也。今後宮所有，請悉出之，雖其不足，士亦不以為怨也。」高祖為改容謝之。高祖即位，立為皇后。高祖崩，隱帝冊尊為皇太后。帝年少，數與小人郭允明、後贊、李業等游戲宮中，后數切責之。

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖皇后李氏，晉陽人也，其父為農。
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Li, wife of Gaozu, was from Jinyang; her father was a farmer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Li of Gaozu was a native of Jinyang; her father was a farmer.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖少為軍卒，牧馬晉陽，夜入其家劫取之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu was young he was an army soldier, herding horses at Jinyang; by night he entered her home and carried her off.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozu was once a soldier herding horses at Jinyang; one night he entered her home and abducted her.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖已貴，封魏國夫人，生隱帝。
manualTranslations.literal: After Gaozu had risen high, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Wei and bore the Hidden Emperor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose to power, she was made Lady of Wei and bore the Hidden Emperor.

manualTranslations.zh: 開運四年，高祖起兵太原，賞軍士，帑藏不足充，欲斂於民。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyun, Gaozu raised troops at Taiyuan and rewarded the soldiers; the treasury was insufficient, and he wished to levy upon the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 4, Gaozu rebelled at Taiyuan and meant to reward his troops, but the treasury fell short and he planned to levy the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 后諫曰：「方今起事，號為義兵，民未知惠而先奪其財，殆非新天子所以救民之意也。
manualTranslations.literal: The empress admonished, saying: "Now in raising the affair we call ourselves righteous troops; the people have not yet known kindness when we first seize their goods—this is scarcely what a new Son of Heaven intends in saving the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She admonished him: "We call this a righteous rising, yet we seize people's goods before they know our kindness—is that how a new emperor saves his people?

manualTranslations.zh: 今後宮所有，請悉出之，雖其不足，士亦不以為怨也。」
manualTranslations.literal: What the inner palace now holds, please bring it all forth; though it be insufficient, the soldiers will not regard it as cause for resentment."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Take everything the inner palace holds; even if it is not enough, the soldiers will not resent it."

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖為改容謝之。
manualTranslations.literal: Gaozu changed expression and thanked her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozu softened and thanked her.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖即位，立為皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, she was installed as empress.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu ascended, she was made empress.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖崩，隱帝冊尊為皇太后。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu died, the Hidden Emperor enfeoffed and honored her as empress dowager.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death, the Hidden Emperor made her empress dowager.

sourceRange.text: 」於是遷后於太平宮，上尊號曰昭聖皇太后。

manualTranslations.zh: 於是遷后於太平宮，上尊號曰昭聖皇太后。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon she was moved to the Taiping Palace and honored as Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She was moved to Taiping Palace and titled Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.

sourceRange.text: 蔡王信，高祖之從弟也。高祖鎮太原，以信為興捷軍都指揮使領義成軍節度使，徙領許州。高祖寢疾，隱帝當立為嗣，楊邠等受顧命，不欲信在京師，乃遣信就鎮，信涕泣而去。信所至黷貨，好行殺戮。軍士有犯法者，信召其妻子，對之刲剔支解，使自食其肉，血流盈前，信命樂飲酒自如也。楊邠等死，信大喜，謂其寮佐曰：「吾嘗為天無眼，而使我鬱鬱於此者三年矣！主上孤立，幾落賊手。諸公可以勸我一杯矣。」已而聞難作，信憂不能食。周太祖軍變於澶州，王峻遣前申州刺史馬鐸以兵巡檢許州，信乃自殺。周太祖即位，追封蔡王。傳，先贇而後信，亦便於述事爾。

context.beforeSource: 予固嘉二人之忠而悲其志，然不得列於死節之士者，惜哉！
