manualTranslations.zh: 蔡王信，高祖之從弟也。
manualTranslations.literal: Prince of Cai, Xin, was Gaozu's younger cousin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prince of Cai Xin was Gaozu's younger cousin.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖鎮太原，以信為興捷軍都指揮使領義成軍節度使，徙領許州。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu held Taiyuan, he made Xin commander of the Xingjie Army and military governor of Yicheng, then transferred him to govern Xu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu governed Taiyuan, he made Xin commander of the Xingjie Army and military governor of Yicheng, then moved him to Xu.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖寢疾，隱帝當立為嗣，楊邠等受顧命，不欲信在京師，乃遣信就鎮，信涕泣而去。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu fell gravely ill and the Hidden Emperor was to succeed, Yang Bin and the others received the final charge; not wanting Xin in the capital, they sent him to his command, and Xin wept as he departed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu lay dying and the Hidden Emperor was to succeed, Yang Bin and the others took the deathbed charge; fearing Xin in the capital, they sent him to his post, and he left in tears.

manualTranslations.zh: 信所至黷貨，好行殺戮。
manualTranslations.literal: Wherever Xin went he extorted goods and loved to carry out executions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wherever he went Xin extorted wealth and delighted in killing.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍士有犯法者，信召其妻子，對之刲剔支解，使自食其肉，血流盈前，信命樂飲酒自如也。
manualTranslations.literal: When soldiers broke the law, Xin summoned their wives and children, and before them flayed, dismembered, and cut them apart, making them eat their own flesh; blood flowed before him, yet Xin ordered music and drank as usual.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When soldiers broke the law, he summoned their families and, before their eyes, flayed and dismembered the men, forcing them to eat their own flesh; blood pooled before him while he ordered music and drank as usual.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊邠等死，信大喜，謂其寮佐曰：「吾嘗為天無眼，而使我鬱鬱於此者三年矣！
manualTranslations.literal: When Yang Bin and the others died, Xin rejoiced greatly and told his staff: "I once thought Heaven had no eyes, yet it kept me pent up here for three years!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yang Bin and the others died, Xin rejoiced and told his staff: "I once thought Heaven was blind to keep me pent here three years!

manualTranslations.zh: 主上孤立，幾落賊手。
manualTranslations.literal: The sovereign stood alone and nearly fell into the rebels' hands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor stood alone and nearly fell to rebels.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸公可以勸我一杯矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: Gentlemen, you may urge me to a cup."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gentlemen, toast me a cup!"

manualTranslations.zh: 已而聞難作，信憂不能食。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he heard trouble had arisen, and Xin was so worried he could not eat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he heard trouble had broken out, and worry left him unable to eat.

manualTranslations.zh: 周太祖軍變於澶州，王峻遣前申州刺史馬鐸以兵巡檢許州，信乃自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu of Zhou's army mutinied at Dazhou, Wang Jun sent former prefect of Shenzhou Ma Duo with troops to inspect Xu; Xin then killed himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei's army mutinied at Dazhou, Wang Jun sent the former prefect of Shenzhou, Ma Duo, to inspect Xu with troops; Xin then killed himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 周太祖即位，追封蔡王。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu of Zhou took the throne, Xin was posthumously created Prince of Cai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei took the throne, Xin was posthumously made Prince of Cai.

manualTranslations.zh: 傳，先贇而後信，亦便於述事爾。
manualTranslations.literal: In the biography, Yun is treated before Xin—also for convenience in narration.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The biography treats Yun before Xin, simply for ease of narration.

sourceRange.text: 符道昭，蔡州人也。為秦宗權騎將，宗權敗，道昭流落無所依，後依鳳翔李茂貞，茂貞愛之，養以為子，名繼遠。梁攻茂貞，道昭與梁兵戰，屢敗，乃歸梁，太祖表道昭秦州節度使，以亂不果行。太祖為元帥，初開府，而李周彝以鄜州降，以為左司馬，擇右司馬難其人，及得道昭，乃授之。羅紹威將誅其牙兵，惡魏兵彊，未敢發，求梁為助。太祖乃悉發魏兵使攻燕，而遣馬嗣勳助紹威誅牙兵。牙兵已誅，魏兵在外者聞之皆亂，魏將左行遷據歷亭、史仁遇據高唐以叛，道昭等從太祖悉破之。道昭為將，勇於犯敵而少成筭，每戰先發，多敗，而周彝等繼之乃勝。開平元年與康懷英等攻潞州，築夾城為蚰蜒塹以圍之，逾年不能下，晉兵攻破夾城，道昭戰死。劉捍，開封人也。為人明敏有威儀，善擯贊。太祖初鎮宣武，以為客將，使從朱珍募兵淄青。太祖北攻鎮州，與王鎔和，遣捍見鎔，鎔軍未知梁意，方嚴兵，捍馳一騎入城中，諭鎔以太祖意，鎔乃聽命。梁兵攻定州，降王處直，捍復以一騎入慰城中。太祖圍鳳翔，遣捍入見李茂貞計事。唐昭宗召見，問梁軍中事，稱旨，賜以錦袍，拜登州刺史，賜號「迎鑾毅勇功臣」。梁兵攻淮南，遣捍先之淮口，築馬頭下浮橋以渡梁兵。太祖出光山攻壽州，又使捍作浮橋于淮北，以渡歸師。拜宋州刺史。太祖即位，遷左天武指揮使、元從親軍都虞候、左龍虎統軍，出為佑國軍留後。同州劉知俊反，以賂誘捍將吏，執捍而去，知俊械之，送于李茂貞，見殺。太祖哀之，贈捍太傅。寇彥卿字俊臣，開封人也，世事宣武軍為牙將。

sourceRange.text: 遂從太祖攻鎮州，下臨城，王鎔乞盟，太祖表從周泰寧軍節度使。從氏叔琮攻晉太原，不克。梁兵西攻鳳翔，青州王師範遣其將劉鄩襲兗州，從周家屬為鄩所得，厚遇之而不殺。太祖還自鳳翔，乃遣從周攻鄩，從周卒招降鄩。太祖即位，拜左金吾衞上將軍，以疾致仕，拜右衞上將軍，居于偃師。末帝即位，拜昭義軍節度使、陳留郡王，食其俸于家。卒，贈太尉。

sourceRange.text: 太祖即位，拜彥卿感化軍節度使。歲餘，召為左金吾衞大將軍，充金吾街仗使。彥卿晨朝至天津橋，民梁現不避道，前驅捽現投橋上石欄以死。彥卿見太祖自首，太祖惜之，詔彥卿以錢償現家以贖罪。御史司憲崔沂劾奏彥卿，請論如法，太祖不得已，責授彥卿左衞中郎將。復拜相州防禦使，遷河陽節度使。

context.beforeSource: 」彥卿復馳至華，即日迫昭宗上道。
context.afterSource: 太祖遇弒，彥卿出太祖畫像事之如生，嘗對客語先朝，必涕泗交下。

sourceRange.text: 末帝即位，趙巖等用事，頗離間舊臣，翔愈鬱鬱不得志。其後，梁盡失河北，與晉相拒楊劉，翔曰：「故時河朔半在，以先帝之武，御貔虎之臣，猶不得志於晉。今晉日益彊，梁日益削，陛下處深宮之中，所與計事者，非其近習，則皆親戚之私，而望成事乎？臣聞晉攻楊劉，李亞子負薪渡水，為士卒先。陛下委蛇守文，以儒雅自喜，而遣賀瓌為將，豈足當彼之餘鋒乎？臣雖憊矣，受國恩深，若其乏材，願得自效。」巖等以翔為怨言，遂不用。

context.beforeSource: 翔以友珪畏己，多稱疾，未嘗省事。
context.afterSource: 其後，王彥章敗于中都，末帝懼，召段凝於河上。

sourceRange.text: 使以弓手五百人伏湟中，太祖以騎數百為遊兵，過晊柵，晊出兵追太祖，歸霸發伏，殺晊兵千人，奪馬數十匹。太祖攻蔡州，蔡將蕭顥急擊太祖營，歸霸不暇請，與徐懷玉分出東南壁門，合擊敗之，太祖得拔營去。太祖攻兗、鄆，取曹州，使歸霸以兵數千守之，與朱瑾逆戰金鄉，大敗之。又破濮州。晉人攻魏，歸霸從葛從周救魏，戰洹水，歸霸擒克用子落落以與魏人。又破劉仁恭於內黃，功出諸將右。光化二年，權知邢州。遷萊州刺史，拜左衞上將軍、曹州刺史。開平元年，拜右龍虎統軍、左驍衞上將軍。二年，拜河陽節度使，以疾卒。

manualTranslations.zh: 使以弓手五百人伏湟中，太祖以騎數百為遊兵，過晊柵，晊出兵追太祖，歸霸發伏，殺晊兵千人，奪馬數十匹。
manualTranslations.literal: He had five hundred archers lie in ambush in the Huang; Taizu with several hundred cavalry acted as skirmishers; passing Zhang Zhi's stockade, Zhi sent troops to pursue Taizu; Guiba sprang the ambush, killed a thousand of Zhi's men, and seized dozens of horses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He hid five hundred archers in the Huang reed beds; Taizu rode out with a few hundred cavalry as bait; passing Zhang Zhi's palisade, Zhi sent men after him; Guiba sprung the trap, killed a thousand, and took dozens of horses.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖攻蔡州，蔡將蕭顥急擊太祖營，歸霸不暇請，與徐懷玉分出東南壁門，合擊敗之，太祖得拔營去。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu attacked Cai Prefecture, the Cai commander Xiao Hao struck Taizu's camp in haste; Guiba had no time to request permission; he and Xu Huaiyu sallied through the southeast wall gate, joined in the attack, and defeated them, allowing Taizu to break camp and withdraw.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu attacked Cai Prefecture, the Cai general Xiao Hao rushed Taizu's camp. Guiba had no time to ask leave; he and Xu Huaiyu burst through the southeast gate, struck together, and beat them back so Taizu could break camp and go.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖攻兗、鄆，取曹州，使歸霸以兵數千守之，與朱瑾逆戰金鄉，大敗之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu attacked Yan and Yun and took Cao Prefecture, he left Guiba with several thousand troops to hold it; Guiba met Zhu Jin in battle at Jinxiang and routed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu attacked Yan and Yun and took Cao, he left Guiba with several thousand men to hold it. Guiba met Zhu Jin head-on at Jinxiang and crushed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 又破濮州。
manualTranslations.literal: He also broke Pu Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also took Pu Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉人攻魏，歸霸從葛從周救魏，戰洹水，歸霸擒克用子落落以與魏人。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jin attacked Wei, Guiba followed Ge Congzhou to relieve Wei; they fought at the Huan River; Guiba captured Kkuser's son Luoluo and handed him over to the men of Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jin attacked Wei, Guiba followed Ge Congzhou to the relief; they fought at the Huan River, and Guiba captured Kkuser's son Luoluo and gave him to the Wei garrison.

manualTranslations.zh: 又破劉仁恭於內黃，功出諸將右。
manualTranslations.literal: He also defeated Liu Rengong at Neihuang; his merit outshone the other generals.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also beat Liu Rengong at Neihuang, and his merit stood above the other commanders.

manualTranslations.zh: 光化二年，權知邢州。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Guanghua, he was appointed acting prefect of Xing Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Guanghua 2 he was made acting prefect of Xing.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷萊州刺史，拜左衞上將軍、曹州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Laizhou, enfeoffed as Senior General of the Left Guard, and made prefect of Cao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was moved to Laizhou, made Senior General of the Left Guard, and appointed prefect of Cao.

manualTranslations.zh: 開平元年，拜右龍虎統軍、左驍衞上將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Kaiping, he was made Right Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief and Senior General of the Left Resplendent Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 1 he was made Right Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief and Senior General of the Left Resplendent Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年，拜河陽節度使，以疾卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year, he was made military governor of Heyang and died of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made military governor of Heyang and died of illness.

sourceRange.text: 太祖即位，拜右千牛衞上將軍。從康懷英攻潞州，為行營排陣使。晉兵已破夾城，存節等以餘兵歸，行至天井關，聞晉兵攻澤州，存節顧諸將曰：「吾行雖不受命，然澤州要害，不可失也。」諸將皆不欲救之。存節戒士卒熟息，已而謂曰：「事急不赴，豈曰勇乎！」舉策而先，士卒隨之。比至澤州，州人已焚外城，將降晉，聞存節至，乃稍定。存節入城，助澤人守，晉人穴地道以攻之，存節選勇士數十，亦穴地以應之，戰于隧中，敵不得入，晉人解去。遷左龍虎統軍、六軍都指揮使、絳州刺史，遷鄜州留後。

context.beforeSource: 累拜邢州團練使、元帥府左都押衙。
context.afterSource: 同州劉知俊叛，奔鳳翔，乃遷存節匡國軍節度使。

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖即位，拜右千牛衞上將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Cunjie was appointed Senior General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Cunjie was made Senior General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 從康懷英攻潞州，為行營排陣使。
manualTranslations.literal: He followed Kang Huaiying in the attack on Lu Prefecture and served as campaign formation-deployment commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He followed Kang Huaiying against Lu Prefecture and served as campaign formation commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉兵已破夾城，存節等以餘兵歸，行至天井關，聞晉兵攻澤州，存節顧諸將曰：「吾行雖不受命，然澤州要害，不可失也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Jin troops had already broken Jiacheng; Cunjie and others returned with the remaining troops; reaching Tianjing Pass, they heard Jin was attacking Ze Prefecture; Cunjie turned to the generals and said: "Though my march was not ordered, Ze Prefecture is vital and must not be lost."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin had already broken Jiacheng, and Cunjie and the others were marching home with the survivors. At Tianjing Pass they heard Jin was attacking Ze Prefecture. Cunjie turned to his officers and said: "My march was not ordered, but Ze is vital and cannot be lost."

manualTranslations.zh: 諸將皆不欲救之。
manualTranslations.literal: The generals all did not wish to go to its relief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: None of the generals wanted to go to the rescue.

manualTranslations.zh: 存節戒士卒熟息，已而謂曰：「事急不赴，豈曰勇乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: Cunjie ordered the soldiers to rest and digest, then said: "When affairs are urgent and one does not go—can that be called bravery!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cunjie let the men rest and eat, then said: "When things are urgent and you hold back, can that be called courage!"

manualTranslations.zh: 舉策而先，士卒隨之。
manualTranslations.literal: He raised his whip and took the lead; the soldiers followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He raised his whip and rode ahead; the soldiers followed.

manualTranslations.zh: 比至澤州，州人已焚外城，將降晉，聞存節至，乃稍定。
manualTranslations.literal: By the time they reached Ze Prefecture, the townspeople had burned the outer city and were about to submit to Jin; hearing Cunjie had arrived, they somewhat settled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Ze, the people had burned the outer walls and were ready to surrender to Jin; when they heard Cunjie had come, they steadied a little.

manualTranslations.zh: 存節入城，助澤人守，晉人穴地道以攻之，存節選勇士數十，亦穴地以應之，戰于隧中，敵不得入，晉人解去。
manualTranslations.literal: Cunjie entered the city and helped the people of Ze hold it; the Jin men burrowed a tunnel to attack; Cunjie chose several dozen brave men and tunneled in response; they fought in the tunnel; the enemy could not enter, and the Jin withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cunjie entered the city and helped the Ze garrison hold on. The Jin dug a tunnel assault; Cunjie picked several dozen brave men and tunneled to meet them. They fought underground; the enemy could not break in, and the Jin pulled back.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷左龍虎統軍、六軍都指揮使、絳州刺史，遷鄜州留後。
manualTranslations.literal: He was promoted to Left Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief, Chief Commander of the Six Armies, and prefect of Jiang Prefecture, then transferred to acting military governor of Fu Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief, Chief Commander of the Six Armies, and prefect of Jiang, then made acting military governor of Fu.

manualTranslations.zh: 末帝即位，封師厚鄴王，詔書不名，事無巨細皆以諮之，然心益忌而畏之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne he enfeoffed Shihou as Prince of Ye; edicts did not name him; affairs great and small were all referred to him, yet the emperor grew ever more jealous and fearful of him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor took the throne he enfeoffed Shihou as Prince of Ye. Edicts did not name him; affairs great and small were all referred to him, yet the emperor grew ever more jealous and afraid of him.

manualTranslations.zh: 已而師厚瘍發卒，末帝為之受賀於宮中。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long Shihou died of carbuncle, and the Last Emperor received congratulations for it within the palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before long Shihou died of carbuncle, and the Last Emperor received congratulations for it within the palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 由是始分相、魏為兩鎮。
manualTranslations.literal: From this the division of Xiang and Wei into two commands began.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this Xiang and Wei were first divided into two commands.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏軍亂，以魏博降晉，梁失河北自此始。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei troops mutinied; Weibo surrendered to Jin, and Liang’s loss of Hebei began from this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei troops mutinied; Weibo went over to Jin, and Liang’s loss of Hebei began from this.

sourceRange.text: 貞明元年，魏兵亂，賀德倫降晉，晉王入魏州。劉鄩敗于故元城，走黎陽，貝、衞、洺、磁諸州皆入于晉。晉軍取楊劉，末帝乃以瓌為招討使，與謝彥章等屯于行臺。晉軍迫瓌十里而柵，相持百餘日。瓌與彥章有隙，伏甲殺之，莊宗喜曰：「將帥不和，梁亡無日矣！」乃令軍中歸其老疾於鄴，以輕兵襲濮州。瓌自行臺躡之，戰于胡柳陂，晉人輜重在陣西，瓌軍將薄之，晉軍亂，斬其將周德威，盡取其輜重。軍已勝，陣無石山，日暮，晉兵仰攻之，瓌軍下山擊晉軍，瓌大敗，晉遂取濮州，城德勝，夾河為柵。瓌以舟兵攻南柵，不能得，還軍行臺，以疾卒，年六十二，贈侍中。有子光圖。凡言有子某者，皆仕皇朝有聞。

manualTranslations.zh: 貞明元年，魏兵亂，賀德倫降晉，晉王入魏州。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming Wei troops mutinied; He Delun surrendered to Jin, and the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenming Wei troops mutinied. He Delun went over to Jin, and the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 劉鄩敗于故元城，走黎陽，貝、衞、洺、磁諸州皆入于晉。
manualTranslations.literal: Liu Xun was defeated at former Yuancheng and fled to Liyang; Bei, Wei, Ming, and Ci prefectures all passed to Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Xun was beaten at former Yuancheng and fled to Liyang. Bei, Wei, Ming, and Ci prefectures all passed to Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉軍取楊劉，末帝乃以瓌為招討使，與謝彥章等屯于行臺。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin troops took Yangliu; the Last Emperor then made Gui pacification commissioner and encamped with Xie Yanzhang and others at the field headquarters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin took Yangliu. The Last Emperor then made Gui pacification commissioner and camped with Xie Yanzhang and others at the field headquarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉軍迫瓌十里而柵，相持百餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin troops pressed within ten li of Gui and palisaded; the stalemate lasted more than a hundred days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin pressed within ten li of Gui and fenced in; the standoff lasted more than a hundred days.

manualTranslations.zh: 瓌與彥章有隙，伏甲殺之，莊宗喜曰：「將帥不和，梁亡無日矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: Gui and Yanzhang were at odds; he hid armored men and killed him. Zhuangzong rejoiced and said: “When commanders are not at one, Liang’s fall is near!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gui and Yanzhang were at odds. Gui hid armed men and killed him. Zhuangzong rejoiced and said: “When commanders fall out, Liang’s end is near!”

manualTranslations.zh: 乃令軍中歸其老疾於鄴，以輕兵襲濮州。
manualTranslations.literal: He then ordered the army to send the old and sick back to Ye and struck Pu prefecture with light troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then sent the old and sick back to Ye and struck Pu prefecture with light troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 瓌自行臺躡之，戰于胡柳陂，晉人輜重在陣西，瓌軍將薄之，晉軍亂，斬其將周德威，盡取其輜重。
manualTranslations.literal: Gui pursued from the field headquarters himself and fought at Huliupi. Jin baggage trains were west of the formation; Gui’s army was about to press them when the Jin forces broke in disorder. They beheaded the commander Zhou Dewei and took all the baggage trains.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gui pursued from the field headquarters himself and fought at Huliupi. Jin baggage trains lay west of the formation; as Gui’s army was about to close, the Jin broke in disorder. They beheaded Zhou Dewei and took all the baggage trains.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍已勝，陣無石山，日暮，晉兵仰攻之，瓌軍下山擊晉軍，瓌大敗，晉遂取濮州，城德勝，夾河為柵。
manualTranslations.literal: The army had already won; there was no stony hill in the formation. At dusk Jin troops attacked uphill; Gui’s army went down the hill to strike the Jin forces and Gui suffered great defeat. Jin then took Pu prefecture, fortified Desheng, and fenced both banks of the river.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The army had already won, but there was no stony hill in the formation. At dusk the Jin attacked uphill; Gui’s army went down the hill to strike them and was routed. Jin then took Pu, fortified Desheng, and fenced both banks of the river.

manualTranslations.zh: 瓌以舟兵攻南柵，不能得，還軍行臺，以疾卒，年六十二，贈侍中。
manualTranslations.literal: Gui attacked the southern palisade with river troops but could not take it. He returned the army to the field headquarters, died of illness at sixty-two, and was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gui attacked the southern palisade with river troops but could not take it. He returned to the field headquarters, died of illness at sixty-two, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 有子光圖。
manualTranslations.literal: He had a son Guangtu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had a son Guangtu.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡言有子某者，皆仕皇朝有聞。
manualTranslations.literal: Wherever it says a man had a son, that son later won renown in service to the imperial court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wherever the text says a man had a son, that son later won renown in service to the imperial court.

sourceRange.text: 開平四年，以景仁為北面招討使，將韓勍、李思安等兵伐趙，行至魏州，司天監言：「太陰虧，不利行師。」太祖亟召景仁等還，已而復遣之。景仁已去，太祖思術者言，馳使者止景仁於魏以待。景仁已過邢、洺，使者及之，景仁不奉詔，進營於柏鄉。乾化元年正月庚寅，日有食之，崇政使敬翔白太祖曰：「兵可憂矣！」太祖為之旰食。是日，景仁及晉人戰，大敗於柏鄉，景仁歸訴於太祖，太祖曰：「吾亦知之，蓋韓勍、李思安輕汝為客，不從節度爾。」乃罷景仁就第，後數月，悉復其官爵。

context.beforeSource: 久之，未有以用，使參宰相班，奉朝請而已。
context.afterSource: 末帝立，以景仁為淮南招討使，攻廬、壽，軍過獨山，山有楊行密祠，景仁再拜號泣而去。
context.beforeLocal: 久之，未有以用，使參宰相班，奉朝請而已。
context.afterLocal: 末帝立，以景仁為淮南招討使，攻廬、壽，軍過獨山，山有楊行密祠，景仁再拜號泣而去。

manualTranslations.zh: 開平四年，以景仁為北面招討使，將韓勍、李思安等兵伐趙，行至魏州，司天監言：「太陰虧，不利行師。」
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiping Jingren was made northern-route pacification commissioner and led Han Qing, Li Si’an, and other troops against Zhao. When they reached Weizhou the Directorate of Astronomy said: “The moon is in eclipse—unfavorable for taking the field.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiping Jingren was made northern-route pacification commissioner and led Han Qing, Li Si’an, and others against Zhao. At Weizhou the Directorate of Astronomy said: “The moon is in eclipse—unfavorable for taking the field.”

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖亟召景仁等還，已而復遣之。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu urgently recalled Jingren and the others, then sent them out again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu urgently recalled Jingren and the others, then sent them out again.

manualTranslations.zh: 景仁已去，太祖思術者言，馳使者止景仁於魏以待。
manualTranslations.literal: Jingren had already departed when Taizu, remembering the diviner’s words, dispatched a messenger at speed to halt him at Wei to await orders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingren had already left when Taizu, remembering the diviner’s warning, sent a messenger at speed to halt him at Wei and await further orders.

manualTranslations.zh: 景仁已過邢、洺，使者及之，景仁不奉詔，進營於柏鄉。
manualTranslations.literal: Jingren had already passed Xing and Ming when the messenger reached him; Jingren did not obey the edict and advanced to encamp at Baixiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingren had already passed Xing and Ming when the messenger caught up; Jingren refused the edict and advanced to camp at Baixiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 乾化元年正月庚寅，日有食之，崇政使敬翔白太祖曰：「兵可憂矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: On gengyin, the first month of the first year of Qianhua, there was a solar eclipse. Jing Xiang, commissioner of the Chongzheng Bureau, told Taizu: “The army ought to worry!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the first month of Qianhua 1, there was a solar eclipse. Jing Xiang, commissioner of the Chongzheng Bureau, told Taizu: “The army ought to worry!”

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖為之旰食。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu went without his noon meal on account of it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu went without his noon meal on account of it.

manualTranslations.zh: 是日，景仁及晉人戰，大敗於柏鄉，景仁歸訴於太祖，太祖曰：「吾亦知之，蓋韓勍、李思安輕汝為客，不從節度爾。」
manualTranslations.literal: That day Jingren fought the Jin forces and was badly defeated at Baixiang. Jingren returned and complained to Taizu; Taizu said: “I know it too—Han Qing and Li Si’an look down on you as an outsider and would not obey your command.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That day Jingren fought the Jin and was routed at Baixiang. Jingren returned and complained to Taizu. Taizu said: “I know it too—Han Qing and Li Si’an look down on you as an outsider and would not obey your command.”

manualTranslations.zh: 乃罷景仁就第，後數月，悉復其官爵。
manualTranslations.literal: Jingren was dismissed and sent to his private residence; several months later all his offices and titles were fully restored.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingren was dismissed and sent home; several months later all his offices and titles were fully restored.

sourceRange.text: 景仁奔于錢鏐，鏐表景仁領宣州節度使。

localRange.text: 景仁奔於錢镠，镠表景仁領宣州節度使。

sourceRange.text: 馬嗣勳，濠州鍾離人也，少事州為客將，為人材武有辯。梁太祖攻濠州，刺史張遂遣嗣勳持牌印降梁。楊行密攻遂，遂又使嗣勳乞兵於太祖。梁兵未至，濠州已沒，嗣勳無所歸，乃留事梁，太祖以為宣武軍元從押衙。太祖西攻鳳翔，行至華州，遣嗣勳入說韓建，建即時出降。天祐二年，羅紹威將誅牙軍，乞兵於梁，梁女嫁魏，適死，太祖乃遣嗣勳以長直千人為綵輿入魏，致兵器於輿中，聲言助葬。嗣勳館銅臺，夜與魏新鄉鎮兵攻石柱門，入迎紹威家屬，衞之。乃益取魏甲兵攻牙軍，牙軍不知兵所從來，莫能為備，殺其八千餘人，遲明皆盡。嗣勳中重瘡卒。太祖即位，贈太保。

context.beforeSource: 徙鎮天平，檀嘗招納亡盜居帳下，帳下兵亂，入殺檀，年五十八，贈太師，謚曰忠毅。
context.afterSource: 王虔裕，瑯琊臨沂人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 馬嗣勳，濠州鍾離人也，少事州為客將，為人材武有辯。
manualTranslations.literal: Ma Sixun was a native of Zhongli in Haozhou. In youth he served the prefecture as a guest general; he was talented in arms and eloquent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Sixun came from Zhongli in Haozhou. As a youth he served the prefecture as a guest general; he was talented in arms and eloquent.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁太祖攻濠州，刺史張遂遣嗣勳持牌印降梁。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu of Liang attacked Haozhou, the prefect Zhang Sui sent Sixun with the seal and credentials to surrender to Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu of Liang attacked Haozhou, prefect Zhang Sui sent Sixun with the seal and credentials to surrender to Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊行密攻遂，遂又使嗣勳乞兵於太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: Yang Xingmi attacked Sui; Sui again sent Sixun to beg troops from Taizu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi attacked Sui, and Sui again sent Sixun to beg troops from Taizu.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁兵未至，濠州已沒，嗣勳無所歸，乃留事梁，太祖以為宣武軍元從押衙。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang troops had not arrived when Haozhou fell; Sixun had nowhere to go and stayed to serve Liang; Taizu made him yabing, an original follower of the Xuanwu army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang troops had not arrived when Haozhou fell. Sixun had nowhere to go and stayed to serve Liang; Taizu made him yabing, an original follower of the Xuanwu army.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖西攻鳳翔，行至華州，遣嗣勳入說韓建，建即時出降。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu attacked Fengxiang in the west; reaching Huazhou he sent Sixun in to persuade Han Jian, who surrendered at once.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu attacked Fengxiang in the west. Reaching Huazhou, he sent Sixun in to persuade Han Jian, who surrendered at once.

manualTranslations.zh: 天祐二年，羅紹威將誅牙軍，乞兵於梁，梁女嫁魏，適死，太祖乃遣嗣勳以長直千人為綵輿入魏，致兵器於輿中，聲言助葬。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Tianyou Luo Shaowei meant to destroy the garrison troops and begged troops from Liang. A Liang princess married into Wei had just died; Taizu sent Sixun with a thousand Long-Direct troops as a funeral escort into Wei, weapons hidden in the carriage, proclaiming they came to assist the burial.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianyou Luo Shaowei meant to destroy the garrison troops and begged Liang for troops. A Liang princess married into Wei had just died; Taizu sent Sixun with a thousand Long-Direct troops in a funeral escort into Wei, weapons hidden in the carriage, claiming they came to assist the burial.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗣勳館銅臺，夜與魏新鄉鎮兵攻石柱門，入迎紹威家屬，衞之。
manualTranslations.literal: Sixun lodged at the Bronze Terrace; by night he and the Xin township garrison troops of Wei attacked Shizhu Gate, entered to receive Shaowei’s household, and guarded them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sixun lodged at the Bronze Terrace. By night he and the Xin township garrison troops of Wei attacked Shizhu Gate, entered to receive Shaowei’s household, and guarded them.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃益取魏甲兵攻牙軍，牙軍不知兵所從來，莫能為備，殺其八千餘人，遲明皆盡。
manualTranslations.literal: He then took more of Wei’s armor and troops to attack the garrison troops. Not knowing where the soldiers had come from, they could not prepare; more than eight thousand were killed and by dawn all were gone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then took more of Wei’s armor and troops to attack the garrison troops. Not knowing where the soldiers had come from, they could not prepare; more than eight thousand were killed, and by dawn all were gone.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗣勳中重瘡卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Sixun was struck by grievous wounds and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sixun was struck by grievous wounds and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖即位，贈太保。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu took the throne Sixun was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne Sixun was posthumously made Grand Guardian.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin troops besieged Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou but could not take it for a long time; then Wang Du of Dingzhou drew the Khitan into invasion.

sourceRange.text: 其已破蜀，因遣使者以唐威德風諭南詔諸蠻，欲因以綏來之，可謂有志矣！安重誨，應州人也。其父福遷，事晉為將，以驍勇知名。梁攻朱宣于鄆州，晉兵救宣，宣敗，福遷戰死。重誨少事明宗，為人明敏謹恪。明宗鎮安國，以為中門使，及兵變于魏，所與謀議大計，皆重誨與霍彥威決之。明宗即位，以為左領軍衞大將軍、樞密使，兼領山南東道節度使。固辭不拜，改兵部尚書，使如故。在位六年，累加侍中兼中書令。

manualTranslations.zh: 其父福遷，事晉為將，以驍勇知名。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Fu Qian served Jin as a general and was famed for fierce courage.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: After six years in office he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Grand Councilor.

sourceRange.text: 安金全，代北人也。為人驍果，工騎射，號能擒生踏伏。事晉為騎將，數從莊宗用兵有功，官至刺史，以疾居于太原。莊宗已下魏博，與梁相距河上。梁將王檀襲太原，晉兵皆從莊宗于河上，太原無備，監軍張承業大恐，率諸司工匠登城扞禦，而外攻甚急。金全彊起謂承業曰：「太原，晉之根本也。一旦不守，則大事去矣！老夫誠憊矣，然尚能為公破賊。」承業喜，授以甲兵。金全被甲跨馬，召率子弟及故將吏得百餘人，夜出北門，擊檀於羊馬城中，檀軍驚潰，而晉救兵稍至。然莊宗不以金全為能，終其世不錄其功。金全與明宗有舊，明宗即位，拜金全振武軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。在鎮二年，召還京師，以疾卒。袁建豐，不知其世家也。晉王討黃巢至華陰，闌得之，時方九歲，愛其俊爽，收養之。長習騎射，為鐵林都虞候，從擊王行瑜、李匡威，以功遷突陣指揮使。從莊宗破夾城，戰柏鄉，遷左廂馬軍指揮使。明宗為衙內指揮使，建豐為副使，從莊宗入魏，取衞、磁、洺三州，拜洺州刺史。擊梁將王千，斬首千餘級，獲其將校七十餘人。遷相州刺史。從戰胡柳，指揮使孟謙據相州叛，建豐還討平之。徙隰州刺史，病風廢。明宗即位，以舊恩召還京師，親幸其第，撫慰甚厚，加檢校太尉，遙領鎮南軍節度使，俾食其俸以卒，贈太尉。

manualTranslations.zh: 安金全，代北人也。
manualTranslations.literal: An Jinquan was a man of northern Dai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An Jinquan came from northern Dai.

manualTranslations.zh: 為人驍果，工騎射，號能擒生踏伏。
manualTranslations.literal: As a man he was fierce and resolute, skilled at mounted archery, and famed for seizing captives alive and trampling hidden foes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fierce and resolute, he excelled at mounted archery and was famed for taking prisoners alive and trampling hidden foes.

manualTranslations.zh: 事晉為騎將，數從莊宗用兵有功，官至刺史，以疾居于太原。
manualTranslations.literal: He served Jin as a mounted general, repeatedly followed Zhuangzong in campaigns with merit, reached the rank of prefect, and due to illness resided at Taiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served Jin as a cavalry general, followed Zhuangzong in campaign after campaign, rose to prefect, and retired to Taiyuan with illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗已下魏博，與梁相距河上。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong had already advanced on Weibo and faced Liang across the Yellow River.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had already marched on Weibo and faced Liang across the river.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁將王檀襲太原，晉兵皆從莊宗于河上，太原無備，監軍張承業大恐，率諸司工匠登城扞禦，而外攻甚急。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang general Wang Tan raided Taiyuan; Jin forces all followed Zhuangzong on the river; Taiyuan was undefended; army monitor Zhang Chengye was greatly alarmed, led the various office craftsmen up the walls to defend, but the external attack was very fierce.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang general Wang Tan struck Taiyuan. Jin’s troops were all with Zhuangzong on the river, and Taiyuan lay undefended. Army monitor Zhang Chengye was terrified and led office craftsmen onto the walls to hold them, but the assault outside grew fierce.

manualTranslations.zh: 金全彊起謂承業曰：「太原，晉之根本也。
manualTranslations.literal: Jinquan forced himself up and said to Chengye: “Taiyuan is Jin’s foundation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jinquan dragged himself upright and told Chengye: “Taiyuan is Jin’s foundation.

manualTranslations.zh: 一旦不守，則大事去矣！
manualTranslations.literal: If it is not held for a day, the great cause is lost!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If it falls for a day, the great cause is lost!”

manualTranslations.zh: 老夫誠憊矣，然尚能為公破賊。」
manualTranslations.literal: “This old man is truly weary, yet I can still break the enemy for you.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: “This old man is truly spent, yet I can still break the enemy for you.”

manualTranslations.zh: 承業喜，授以甲兵。
manualTranslations.literal: Chengye rejoiced and gave him armor and weapons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chengye rejoiced and armed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 金全被甲跨馬，召率子弟及故將吏得百餘人，夜出北門，擊檀於羊馬城中，檀軍驚潰，而晉救兵稍至。
manualTranslations.literal: Jinquan donned armor, mounted a horse, gathered sons, brothers, and former officers to about a hundred men, went out the north gate at night, struck Tan in the Sheep-Horse city; Tan’s army fled in alarm, and Jin relief troops gradually arrived.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jinquan armored himself, mounted, and mustered sons, kin, and old officers—more than a hundred men. That night they went out the north gate and struck Tan in the Sheep-Horse city. Tan’s army broke in panic as Jin relief troops drew near.

manualTranslations.zh: 然莊宗不以金全為能，終其世不錄其功。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet Zhuangzong did not regard Jinquan as capable and throughout his reign never recorded his merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet Zhuangzong did not credit Jinquan’s ability and never recorded his merit in his lifetime.

manualTranslations.zh: 金全與明宗有舊，明宗即位，拜金全振武軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。
manualTranslations.literal: Jinquan had old ties with Mingzong; when Mingzong took the throne, he enfeoffed Jinquan as military governor of the Zhenwu Army and co-equal grand councilor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jinquan had old ties with Mingzong. When Mingzong took the throne, he made Jinquan military governor of the Zhenwu Army and co-equal grand councilor.

manualTranslations.zh: 在鎮二年，召還京師，以疾卒。
manualTranslations.literal: After two years in his post, he was recalled to the capital and died of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After two years in his command he was recalled to the capital and died of illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 袁建豐，不知其世家也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan Jianfeng—his family background is unknown.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Jianfeng’s family background is unknown.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉王討黃巢至華陰，闌得之，時方九歲，愛其俊爽，收養之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Prince of Jin campaigned against Huang Chao and reached Huayin, he happened upon him; Jianfeng was then only nine. The prince admired his bright bearing and took him in to raise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin campaigned against Huang Chao and reached Huayin, he happened upon the boy—then only nine. He admired Jianfeng’s bright bearing and took him in.

manualTranslations.zh: 長習騎射，為鐵林都虞候，從擊王行瑜、李匡威，以功遷突陣指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: As he grew he trained in riding and archery, became chief adjutant of the Iron Forest, followed in attacks on Wang Xingyu and Li Kuangwei, and for merit was transferred to commander of the Shock Array.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He grew up training in riding and archery, became chief adjutant of the Iron Forest, fought Wang Xingyu and Li Kuangwei, and was made commander of the Shock Array for his deeds.

manualTranslations.zh: 從莊宗破夾城，戰柏鄉，遷左廂馬軍指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: He followed Zhuangzong in breaking the twin fortifications and fought at Baixiang, then was transferred to commander of the left wing horse army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong in breaking the twin fortifications, fought at Baixiang, and was made commander of the left wing horse army.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗為衙內指揮使，建豐為副使，從莊宗入魏，取衞、磁、洺三州，拜洺州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong was Inner Gate director of command, Jianfeng was his deputy; they followed Zhuangzong into Wei, took the three prefectures of Wei, Ci, and Luo, and Jianfeng was made prefect of Luo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was Inner Gate director of command, Jianfeng served as his deputy. They followed Zhuangzong into Wei, took Wei, Ci, and Luo prefectures, and Jianfeng was made prefect of Luo.

manualTranslations.zh: 擊梁將王千，斬首千餘級，獲其將校七十餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: He attacked Liang general Wang Qian, beheaded more than a thousand men, and captured more than seventy of his officers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He struck Liang general Wang Qian, took more than a thousand heads, and captured more than seventy of his officers.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷相州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Xiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Xiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 從戰胡柳，指揮使孟謙據相州叛，建豐還討平之。
manualTranslations.literal: At Huliu, director of command Meng Qian seized Xiang prefecture and rebelled; Jianfeng returned and put the revolt down.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Huliu, director of command Meng Qian seized Xiang and rebelled. Jianfeng returned and crushed the revolt.

manualTranslations.zh: 徙隰州刺史，病風廢。
manualTranslations.literal: He was moved to prefect of Xi and was disabled by wind illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was moved to prefect of Xi and was disabled by wind illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗即位，以舊恩召還京師，親幸其第，撫慰甚厚，加檢校太尉，遙領鎮南軍節度使，俾食其俸以卒，贈太尉。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he recalled Jianfeng to the capital for old kindness, personally visited his residence, and comforted him very generously. He was made acting Grand Marshal, given titular command of the Zhennan Army, allowed to draw its salary until death, and posthumously made Grand Marshal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, he recalled Jianfeng to the capital for old kindness, visited his home in person, and comforted him lavishly. He was made acting Grand Marshal, given titular command of the Zhennan Army, allowed its salary until death, and posthumously honored as Grand Marshal.

sourceRange.text: 安從進聞之，亦殺贇于家，贇母新死，子母棄尸于道，妻子皆見殺。贇有子三歲，其故吏張守素匿之以免。漢高祖即位，贈弘昭尚書令，贇中書令。劉延朗，宋州虞城人也。初，廢帝起於鳳翔，與共事者五人：節度判官韓昭胤，掌書記李專美，牙將宋審虔，客將房暠，而延朗為孔目官。初，愍帝即位，徙廢帝為北京留守，不降制書，遣供奉官趙處愿促帝上道。帝疑惑，召昭胤等計議，昭胤等皆勸帝反，由是事無大小，皆此五人謀之。而暠又喜鬼神巫祝之說，有瞽者張濛，自言事太白山神，神，魏崔浩也，其言吉凶無不中，暠素信之。嘗引濛見帝，聞其語聲，驚曰：「此非人臣也！」暠使濛問於神，神傳語曰：「三珠倂一珠，驢馬沒人驅。歲月甲庚午，中興戊己土。」暠不曉其義，使問濛，濛曰：「神言如此，我能傳之，不能解也。」帝即以濛為館驛巡官。帝將反，而兵少，又乏食，由此甚懼，使暠問濛，濛傳神語曰：「王當有天下，可無憂！」於是決反，使專美作檄書，言：「朱弘昭、馮贇幸明宗病，殺秦王而立愍帝。帝年少，小人用事，離間骨肉，將問罪於朝！」遣使者馳告諸鎮，皆不應，獨隴州防禦使相里金遣其判官薛文遇計事。帝得文遇，大喜。而延朗調率城中民財以給軍。王思同率諸鎮兵圍鳳翔，廢帝懼，又遣暠問神，神曰：「王兵少，東兵來，所以迎王也。」已而東兵果叛降于帝。帝入京師，即位之日，受冊明宗柩前。冊曰：「維應順元年，歲次甲午，四月庚午朔。」帝回顧暠曰：「張濛神言，豈不驗哉！」由是暠益見親信，而專以巫祝用事。

manualTranslations.literal: Liu Yanlang was a native of Yucheng in Songzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，廢帝起於鳳翔，與共事者五人：節度判官韓昭胤，掌書記李專美，牙將宋審虔，客將房暠，而延朗為孔目官。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, when the Deposed Emperor rose at Fengxiang, five men worked with him: the military governor’s aide Han Zhao Yin, chief clerk Li Zhuanmei, guard officer Song Shenqian, guest officer Fang Hao, and Yanlang as records clerk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor first rose at Fengxiang, five men shared his cause: Han Zhao Yin as military aide, Li Zhuanmei as chief clerk, Song Shenqian as guard officer, Fang Hao as guest officer, and Yanlang as records clerk.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，愍帝即位，徙廢帝為北京留守，不降制書，遣供奉官趙處愿促帝上道。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Min first took the throne, he transferred the Deposed Emperor to Beijing as military commissioner without issuing an edict, and sent palace attendant Zhao Chuyuan to hurry him on the road.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min took the throne, he made the Deposed Emperor Beijing commissioner without a formal edict and sent palace attendant Zhao Chuyuan to hurry him on his way.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝疑惑，召昭胤等計議，昭胤等皆勸帝反，由是事無大小，皆此五人謀之。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor hesitated and summoned Zhao Yin and the others to counsel; they all urged rebellion, and thereafter matters great and small were plotted by these five.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Uncertain, the emperor called Zhao Yin and the others; all urged revolt, and from then on these five decided every matter.

manualTranslations.zh: 而暠又喜鬼神巫祝之說，有瞽者張濛，自言事太白山神，神，魏崔浩也，其言吉凶無不中，暠素信之。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao also delighted in spirits, ghosts, and shamanic rites. A blind man, Zhang Meng, claimed to serve the god of Mount Taibai—the god, he said, was Wei’s Cui Hao—and his words on fortune and disaster never missed. Hao had long trusted him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hao also favored spirit worship. A blind man named Zhang Meng claimed to serve the god of Mount Taibai—said to be Cui Hao of Wei—and his omens never failed. Hao trusted him deeply.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘗引濛見帝，聞其語聲，驚曰：「此非人臣也！」
manualTranslations.literal: Once he brought Meng before the emperor; hearing his voice, the emperor started and said: “This is no ordinary subject!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He once presented Meng to the emperor, who started at his voice and cried: “This is no ordinary subject!”

manualTranslations.zh: 暠使濛問於神，神傳語曰：「三珠倂一珠，驢馬沒人驅。歲月甲庚午，中興戊己土。」
manualTranslations.literal: Hao had Meng inquire of the god, and the god transmitted: “Three pearls join into one pearl; donkeys and horses sink, men drive on. In the year’s months, jia and gengwu; at Zhongxing, wu and jitu.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hao had Meng ask the god, who answered: “Three pearls join into one; donkeys and horses sink while men drive on. In the year’s months, jia and gengwu; at Zhongxing, wu and jitu.”

manualTranslations.zh: 暠不曉其義，使問濛，濛曰：「神言如此，我能傳之，不能解也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Hao did not understand the meaning and had Meng asked; Meng said: “The god spoke thus—I can transmit it, but cannot explain it.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hao could not grasp the meaning and asked Meng, who said: “The god spoke thus—I can relay it, but not explain it.”

manualTranslations.zh: 帝即以濛為館驛巡官。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor then made Meng touring officer of the post stations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor then made Meng touring officer of the post stations.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝將反，而兵少，又乏食，由此甚懼，使暠問濛，濛傳神語曰：「王當有天下，可無憂！」
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor was about to rebel, but his troops were few and food scarce; greatly afraid, he had Hao ask Meng, and Meng relayed the god’s words: “My lord shall possess the realm—have no fear!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: About to rebel but short of troops and food, the emperor was terrified and had Hao consult Meng, who relayed: “My lord shall rule the realm—fear nothing!”

manualTranslations.zh: 於是決反，使專美作檄書，言：「朱弘昭、馮贇幸明宗病，殺秦王而立愍帝。帝年少，小人用事，離間骨肉，將問罪於朝！」
manualTranslations.literal: He then resolved on rebellion and had Zhuanmei draft a proclamation saying: “Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun took advantage of Mingzong’s illness, killed the Prince of Qin, and set up Emperor Min. The emperor is young; petty men hold power, estranging kin, and will bring charges in court!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then rebelled and had Zhuanmei draft a proclamation: “Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun exploited Mingzong’s illness, killed the Prince of Qin, and enthroned Emperor Min. The boy emperor is ruled by petty men who divide the clan—they mean to bring us to court in chains!”

manualTranslations.zh: 遣使者馳告諸鎮，皆不應，獨隴州防禦使相里金遣其判官薛文遇計事。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent envoys racing to notify the provinces; none answered save Xiangli Jin, commissioner of Longzhou, who sent his aide Xue Wenyu to consult.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to the provinces; none answered except Longzhou commissioner Xiangli Jin, who sent his aide Xue Wenyu to counsel.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝得文遇，大喜。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor gained Wenyu and was greatly pleased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed Wenyu and rejoiced.

manualTranslations.zh: 而延朗調率城中民財以給軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Yanlang levied the townspeople’s wealth to supply the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yanlang levied the city’s wealth to feed the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 王思同率諸鎮兵圍鳳翔，廢帝懼，又遣暠問神，神曰：「王兵少，東兵來，所以迎王也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Sitong led provincial troops to besiege Fengxiang. The Deposed Emperor was afraid and again sent Hao to ask the god, who said: “My lord’s troops are few; the eastern troops come to welcome my lord.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Sitong besieged Fengxiang with provincial troops. The Deposed Emperor, afraid, again consulted the god through Hao, who answered: “Your troops are few—the eastern army comes to welcome you.”

manualTranslations.zh: 已而東兵果叛降于帝。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long the eastern troops indeed mutinied and surrendered to the emperor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon the eastern troops mutinied and went over to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝入京師，即位之日，受冊明宗柩前。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor entered the capital; on the day of enthronement he received investiture before Mingzong’s coffin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He entered the capital and, on his enthronement day, received investiture before Mingzong’s coffin.

manualTranslations.zh: 冊曰：「維應順元年，歲次甲午，四月庚午朔。」
manualTranslations.literal: The investiture read: “In the first year of Yingshun, the year jiawu, on gengwu the first day of the fourth month.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The investiture read: “In the first year of Yingshun, cyclical year jiawu, on gengwu the first day of the fourth month.”

manualTranslations.zh: 帝回顧暠曰：「張濛神言，豈不驗哉！」
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor turned to Hao and said: “Zhang Meng’s spirit words—were they not fulfilled!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Hao and said: “Zhang Meng’s oracle—was it not fulfilled!”

manualTranslations.zh: 由是暠益見親信，而專以巫祝用事。
manualTranslations.literal: From this Hao was all the more trusted and favored, and shamanic rites alone governed affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hao grew still more trusted, and shamanic rites alone governed affairs.

sourceRange.text: 任圜，京兆三原人也。為人明敏，善談辯，見者愛其容止，及聞其論議縱橫，益皆悚動。李嗣昭節度昭義，辟圜觀察支使。梁兵築夾城圍潞州，踰年而晉王薨，晉兵救潞者皆解去。嗣昭危甚，問圜去就之計，圜勸嗣昭堅守以待，不可有二心。已而莊宗攻破梁夾城，聞圜為嗣昭畫守計，甚嘉之，由是益知名。其後嗣昭與莊宗有隙，圜數奉使往來，辨釋讒構，嗣昭卒免於禍，圜之力也。嗣昭從莊宗戰胡柳，擊敗梁兵，圜頗有功，莊宗勞之曰：「儒士亦破體邪？仁者之勇，何其壯也！」張文禮弒王鎔，莊宗遣嗣昭討之。

localRange.text: 張文禮弒王镕，莊宗遣嗣昭討之。

context.beforeSource: 莊宗入洛，程於路墜馬，中風卒，贈禮部尚書。
context.afterSource: 嗣昭戰歿，圜代將其軍，號令嚴肅。

manualTranslations.zh: 任圜，京兆三原人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Ren Huan was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ren Huan came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 為人明敏，善談辯，見者愛其容止，及聞其論議縱橫，益皆悚動。
manualTranslations.literal: As a man he was bright and quick, skilled in discourse and debate. Those who saw him loved his bearing; when they heard his sweeping arguments, they were all the more shaken.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bright and quick, skilled in debate, he won admiration for his bearing; his sweeping arguments left listeners shaken.

manualTranslations.zh: 李嗣昭節度昭義，辟圜觀察支使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Li Sizhao governed Zhaoyi, he invited Huan as observation aide.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Sizhao held Zhaoyi, he took Huan on as observation aide.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁兵築夾城圍潞州，踰年而晉王薨，晉兵救潞者皆解去。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang troops built the encircled fort and besieged Luzhou. After more than a year the Prince of Jin died, and the Jin forces sent to relieve Luzhou all withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang troops built the encircled fort and besieged Luzhou. After a year the Prince of Jin died, and every Jin relief force pulled away.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗣昭危甚，問圜去就之計，圜勸嗣昭堅守以待，不可有二心。
manualTranslations.literal: Sizhao was in grave peril and asked Huan whether to stay or leave. Huan urged Sizhao to hold firm and wait—he must not waver.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sizhao was desperate and asked Huan whether to stay or go. Huan urged him to hold on and wait and never waver.

manualTranslations.zh: 已而莊宗攻破梁夾城，聞圜為嗣昭畫守計，甚嘉之，由是益知名。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long Zhuangzong broke the Liang encircled fort. Hearing that Huan had devised Sizhao’s defense plan, he greatly praised him, and from then on Huan grew more famous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong soon broke the Liang encircled fort. Learning Huan had planned Sizhao’s defense, he praised him warmly, and Huan’s name spread.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後嗣昭與莊宗有隙，圜數奉使往來，辨釋讒構，嗣昭卒免於禍，圜之力也。
manualTranslations.literal: Later Sizhao and Zhuangzong fell out. Huan repeatedly went back and forth as envoy, explaining away slanders and intrigues, and Sizhao at last escaped disaster—this was Huan’s doing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Sizhao and Zhuangzong quarreled. Huan shuttled between them, clearing away slander, and Sizhao at last escaped ruin—Huan’s work.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗣昭從莊宗戰胡柳，擊敗梁兵，圜頗有功，莊宗勞之曰：「儒士亦破體邪？
manualTranslations.literal: Sizhao followed Zhuangzong to fight at Huliu and routed the Liang army. Huan did considerable service. Zhuangzong praised him: “A scholar too throws off restraint?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sizhao followed Zhuangzong to Huliu and routed the Liang army. Huan served well. Zhuangzong praised him: “Even a scholar casts off restraint?

manualTranslations.zh: 仁者之勇，何其壯也！」
manualTranslations.literal: The courage of the humane—how mighty!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The courage of the humane—how mighty!”

sourceRange.text: 愍帝即位，贈圜太傅。趙鳳，幽州人也，少以儒學知名。燕王劉守光時，悉黥燕人以為兵，鳳懼，因髠為僧，依燕王弟守奇自匿。守奇奔梁，梁以守奇為博州刺史，鳳為其判官。守奇卒，鳳去為鄆州節度判官。晉取鄆州，莊宗聞鳳名，得之喜，以為扈鑾學士。莊宗即位，拜鳳中書舍人、翰林學士。

context.beforeSource: 明宗知而不問，為下詔，坐圜與守殷通書而言涉怨望。
context.afterSource: 莊宗及劉皇后幸河南尹張全義第，酒酣，命皇后拜全義為父。

manualTranslations.zh: 趙鳳，幽州人也，少以儒學知名。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao Feng was a native of Youzhou and in youth was known for Confucian learning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng came from Youzhou and was known in youth for Confucian learning.

manualTranslations.zh: 燕王劉守光時，悉黥燕人以為兵，鳳懼，因髠為僧，依燕王弟守奇自匿。
manualTranslations.literal: Under the Prince of Yan Liu Shouguang, when all Yan people were tattooed for military service, Feng was afraid, shaved his head to become a monk, and hid himself with Shouguang’s younger brother Shouqi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Liu Shouguang, Prince of Yan, when every Yan man was tattooed for the army, Feng shaved his head as a monk and hid with Shouguang’s brother Shouqi.

manualTranslations.zh: 守奇奔梁，梁以守奇為博州刺史，鳳為其判官。
manualTranslations.literal: Shouqi fled to Liang. Liang made Shouqi governor of Bozhou and Feng his aide.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shouqi fled to Liang, which made him governor of Bozhou and Feng his aide.

manualTranslations.zh: 守奇卒，鳳去為鄆州節度判官。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shouqi died, Feng left to become Yanzhou military governor’s aide.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Shouqi died, Feng became military aide at Yanzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉取鄆州，莊宗聞鳳名，得之喜，以為扈鑾學士。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jin took Yanzhou, Zhuangzong heard Feng’s name and was delighted to gain him, making him Curtained Chariot academician.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jin took Yanzhou, Zhuangzong heard of Feng, was glad to have him, and made him Curtained Chariot academician.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗即位，拜鳳中書舍人、翰林學士。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Feng was made Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin academician.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Zhuangzong’s accession Feng became Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin academician.

manualTranslations.zh: 張憲字允中，晉陽人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Xian, courtesy name Yunzhong, was a native of Jinyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian, courtesy name Yunzhong, came from Jinyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 為人沈靜寡欲，少好學，能鼓琴飲酒。
manualTranslations.literal: As a man he was calm, reticent, and sparing of desire. In youth he loved learning and could play the zither and drink wine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Calm, reticent, and sparing of desire, he loved learning in youth and could play the zither and take wine.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗素知其文辭，以為天雄軍節度使掌書記。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong had long known his literary skill and made him chief secretary to the Tianxiong Army military governor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had long known his literary gifts and made him chief secretary to the Tianxiong Army governor.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗即位，拜工部侍郎、租庸使，遷刑部侍郎、判吏部銓、東都副留守。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Xian was made Vice Minister of Works and Commissioner for Land Tax and Corvée Labor; he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments, acting director of the Board of Civil Office examinations, and deputy regent of the eastern capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Zhuangzong’s accession Xian became Vice Minister of Works and land-tax commissioner, then Vice Minister of Punishments, acting director of civil examinations, and deputy regent of the eastern capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 憲精於吏事，甚有能政。
manualTranslations.literal: Xian was expert in administrative affairs and governed with real ability.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xian was expert in office work and governed with real ability.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rubi was skilled in painting and calligraphy, but his prose fell short of Xiji’s.

manualTranslations.zh: 其父簡求為河東節度使，為唐名家，故汝弼亦多知唐故事。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Jianqiu had been Hedong military governor of a famous Tang house, so Rubi too knew Tang precedent well.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉王薨，莊宗嗣為晉王，承制封拜官爵皆出汝弼。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Prince of Jin died and Zhuangzong succeeded as Prince of Jin, all commissions and ennoblements issued on imperial authority came from Rubi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin died and Zhuangzong succeeded him, every commission and ennoblement under imperial authority came from Rubi.

manualTranslations.zh: 十八年，卒。

sourceRange.text: 德光責延廣曰：「南北失懽，皆因爾也。」召喬瑩質其前言，延廣初不服，瑩從衣領中出所藏書，延廣乃服。因以十事責延廣，每服一事，授一牙籌，授至八籌，延廣以面伏地，不能仰視，遂叱而鎖之。

manualTranslations.zh: 遷右領軍大將軍，入謝，召諸將軍設食朝堂，儀鸞、翰林、御廚供帳飲食，文進自如，有司不敢劾。
manualTranslations.literal: Promoted to Grand General of the Right Garrison Guard, he entered to give thanks. The emperor summoned the generals and set out food in the court hall; the Ceremonial Escort, Hanlin, and Imperial Kitchen supplied tents, food, and drink. manualTranslations.zh: 周太祖鎮鄴，文進等用事居中，及謀殺楊邠等，文進夜作詔書，制置中外。

manualTranslations.zh: 邠等已死，文進點閱兵籍，指麾殺戮，以為己任。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Bin and the rest were dead, Wenjin reviewed the rolls, directed the slaughter, and made it his personal task.

manualTranslations.zh: 周太祖在鄴聞邠等遇害，初以為文進不與，及發詔書，皆文進手跡，乃大詬之。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou Taizu at Ye heard that Bin and the rest had been killed. At first he thought Wenjin had not taken part, but when the edicts were issued, all were in Wenjin’s hand—and he cursed him bitterly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Ye, Zhou Taizu heard Bin and the rest had been killed. At first he thought Wenjin was innocent, but when the edicts appeared, every line was Wenjin’s hand—and he cursed him bitterly.

sourceRange.text: 莊宗即位，拜右武衛上將軍。莊宗亦好角觝，嘗與王較而屢勝，頗以自矜，因顧存賢曰：「爾能勝我，與爾一鎮。」存賢搏而勝之。同光二年春，幽州符存審病，莊宗置酒宮中，歎曰：「吾創業故人，零落殆盡，其所存者惟存審耳！今又病篤，北方之事誰可代之？」因顧存賢曰：「無以易卿。角觝之勝，吾不食言。」即日以為盧龍軍節度使。是歲，卒于幽州，年六十五。贈太傅。

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗即位，拜右武衛上將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he appointed Cunxian general of the Right Martial Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne he made Cunxian general of the Right Martial Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗亦好角觝，嘗與王較而屢勝，頗以自矜，因顧存賢曰：「爾能勝我，與爾一鎮。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong also loved wrestling; he often tested himself against Wang and won repeatedly, growing quite proud. He turned to Cunxian and said: "If you can beat me, I will give you a command."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong also loved wrestling; he often wrestled Wang and kept winning until he grew proud. He turned to Cunxian and said: "Beat me and I will give you a command."

manualTranslations.zh: 存賢搏而勝之。
manualTranslations.literal: Cunxian wrestled and defeated him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cunxian wrestled and beat him.

manualTranslations.zh: 同光二年春，幽州符存審病，莊宗置酒宮中，歎曰：「吾創業故人，零落殆盡，其所存者惟存審耳！
manualTranslations.literal: In spring of Tongguang 2, Fu Cunshen in Youzhou fell ill. Zhuangzong set out wine in the palace and sighed: "Of the old companions who built this realm, nearly all are gone—the only one left is Cunshen!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In spring of Tongguang 2 Fu Cunshen in Youzhou fell ill. Zhuangzong drank in the palace and sighed: "Of the friends who built this realm with me, nearly all are gone—the only one left is Cunshen!

manualTranslations.zh: 今又病篤，北方之事誰可代之？」
manualTranslations.literal: Now he lies gravely ill. Who can take his place in the north?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now he is gravely ill. Who can take the north?"

manualTranslations.zh: 因顧存賢曰：「無以易卿。
manualTranslations.literal: He turned again to Cunxian and said: "No one can replace you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He turned to Cunxian and said: "No one can replace you.

manualTranslations.zh: 角觝之勝，吾不食言。」
manualTranslations.literal: I will not break my word on that wrestling wager."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I will not break my word on that wrestling match."

manualTranslations.zh: 即日以為盧龍軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: That same day he made him military governor of the Lu Long Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That day he made him military governor of the Lu Long Army.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲，卒于幽州，年六十五。
manualTranslations.literal: That year he died in Youzhou, aged sixty-five.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year he died in Youzhou at sixty-five.

manualTranslations.zh: 贈太傅。
manualTranslations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sourceRange.text: 存孝，代州飛狐人也。本姓安，名敬思。太祖掠地代北得之，給事帳中，賜姓名，以為子，常從為騎將。文德元年，河南張言襲破河陽，李罕之來歸晉，晉處罕之于澤州，遣存孝與薛阿檀、安休休等以兵七千助罕之還擊河陽。梁亦遣丁會、牛存節等助言。戰于溫縣，梁軍先扼太行，存孝大敗，安休休被執。是時，晉已得澤、潞，歲出山東，與孟方立爭邢、洺、磁，存孝未嘗不在兵間。方立死，晉取三州，存孝功為多。

context.beforeSource: 由是大懼常稱疾，天復二年卒，年四十一。
context.afterSource: 明年，潞州軍亂，殺李克恭以歸唐，梁遣李讜攻李罕之于澤州，存孝以騎兵五千救之。

manualTranslations.literal: Cunxiao was a native of Feihu in Daizhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Cunxiao came from Feihu in Daizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 本姓安，名敬思。
manualTranslations.literal: Originally surnamed An, personal name Jingsi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Born An Jingsi.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖掠地代北得之，給事帳中，賜姓名，以為子，常從為騎將。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu overran the north beyond Dai he took him, assigned him to serve in the headquarters tent, bestowed surname and personal name, made him a son, and kept him constantly as a cavalry commander.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu took him campaigning beyond Dai, put him in the headquarters tent, gave him the Li name, adopted him, and kept him as a cavalry commander.

manualTranslations.zh: 文德元年，河南張言襲破河陽，李罕之來歸晉，晉處罕之于澤州，遣存孝與薛阿檀、安休休等以兵七千助罕之還擊河陽。
manualTranslations.literal: In Wende 1, Zhang Yan of Henan raided and broke Heyang; Li Hanzhi came over to Jin; Jin stationed Hanzhi at Ze Prefecture and sent Cunxiao with Xue Atan, An Xiuxiu, and others with seven thousand men to help Hanzhi strike back at Heyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Wende 1 Zhang Yan of Henan stormed Heyang; Li Hanzhi came to Jin; Jin posted Hanzhi at Zezhou and sent Cunxiao with Xue Atan, An Xiuxiu, and seven thousand men to help him retake Heyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁亦遣丁會、牛存節等助言。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang also sent Ding Hui, Niu Cunjie, and others to aid Yan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang sent Ding Hui, Niu Cunjie, and others to aid Yan.

manualTranslations.zh: 戰于溫縣，梁軍先扼太行，存孝大敗，安休休被執。
manualTranslations.literal: They fought at Wen County; Liang first held the Taihang passes and Cunxiao was heavily defeated; An Xiuxiu was captured.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Wen County Liang held the Taihang passes first; Cunxiao was smashed and An Xiuxiu was taken.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，晉已得澤、潞，歲出山東，與孟方立爭邢、洺、磁，存孝未嘗不在兵間。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Jin had already taken Ze and Lu and each year marched into Shandong to contend with Meng Fangli for Xing, Ming, and Ci; Cunxiao was never absent from the fighting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin already held Ze and Lu and each year marched into Shandong against Meng Fangli for Xing, Ming, and Ci; Cunxiao was always in the fighting.

manualTranslations.zh: 方立死，晉取三州，存孝功為多。
manualTranslations.literal: When Fangli died, Jin took the three prefectures and Cunxiao's merit was greatest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Fangli died Jin took the three prefectures, and Cunxiao's merit was greatest.

sourceRange.text: 陝州王珙與其兄珂爭立於河中，遣嗣昭助珂，敗珙於猗氏，獲其將三人。梁軍救珙，嗣昭又敗之于胡壁堡，執其將一人。光化元年，澤州李罕之襲潞州以降梁，梁遣丁會應罕之，嗣昭與會戰含山，執其將一人，斬首三千級，遂取澤州。二年，晉遣李君慶攻梁潞州，君慶為梁所敗，太祖酖殺君慶，嗣昭攻克之。三年，出山東，取梁洺州，梁太祖自將攻之，遣葛從周設伏於青山口。嗣昭聞梁太祖自來，棄城走，前遇伏兵，因大敗。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Gong of Shaanzhou fought his brother Ke for Hezhong; he sent Sizhao to aid Ke, beat Gong at Yishi, and took three of his generals.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang marched to save Gong; Sizhao beat them again at Hubi Fort and captured a general.

manualTranslations.zh: 光化元年，澤州李罕之襲潞州以降梁，梁遣丁會應罕之，嗣昭與會戰含山，執其將一人，斬首三千級，遂取澤州。

manualTranslations.zh: 二年，晉遣李君慶攻梁潞州，君慶為梁所敗，太祖酖殺君慶，嗣昭攻克之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year Jin sent Li Junqing to attack Liang at Luzhou; Junqing was beaten by Liang; Taizu poisoned and killed Junqing, and Sizhao stormed the city and took it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year Jin sent Li Junqing against Liang at Luzhou; Liang beat him; Taizu poisoned Junqing; Sizhao stormed the city and took it.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，出山東，取梁洺州，梁太祖自將攻之，遣葛從周設伏於青山口。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year he marched into Shandong and took Liang's Ming Prefecture; Liang Taizu came in person to attack and sent Ge Congzhou to lay an ambush at Qingshan Pass.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The third year he marched into Shandong and took Liang's Mingzhou; Liang Taizu came in person and sent Ge Congzhou to ambush at Qingshan Pass.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗣昭聞梁太祖自來，棄城走，前遇伏兵，因大敗。
manualTranslations.literal: Hearing Liang Taizu had come himself, Sizhao abandoned the city and fled; he ran into the ambush ahead and suffered a great defeat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearing Taizu had come himself, Sizhao abandoned the city and fled straight into the ambush and was crushed.

sourceRange.text: 張居翰，字德卿，故唐掖廷令張從玫之養子。昭宗時，為范陽軍監軍，與節度使劉仁恭相善。天復中，大誅宦者，仁恭匿居翰大安山之北谿以免。其後，梁兵攻仁恭，仁恭遣居翰從晉王攻梁潞州以牽其兵，晉遂取潞州，以居翰為昭義監軍。莊宗即位，與郭崇韜並為樞密使。莊宗滅梁而驕，宦官因以用事，郭崇韜又專任政，居翰默默，茍免而已。魏王破蜀，王衍朝京師，行至秦川，而明宗軍變於魏。莊宗東征，慮衍有變，遣人馳詔魏王殺之。詔書已印畫，而居翰發視之，詔書言「誅衍一行」，居翰以謂殺降不祥，乃以詔傅柱，揩去「行」字，改為一「家」。時蜀降人與衍俱東者千餘人，皆獲免。莊宗遇弒，居翰見明宗於至德宮，求歸田里。天成三年，卒於長安，年七十一。

context.beforeSource: 同光元年，贈左武衛上將軍，謚曰正憲。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Juhan, courtesy name Deqing, was the adopted son of Zhang Congmei, a former Tang director of the palace provision bureau.

manualTranslations.zh: 昭宗時，為范陽軍監軍，與節度使劉仁恭相善。
manualTranslations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhaozong he served as army supervisor of the Fanyang army and was on good terms with military governor Liu Rengong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Zhaozong he served as army supervisor at Fanyang and was on good terms with the military governor Liu Rengong.

manualTranslations.zh: 天復中，大誅宦者，仁恭匿居翰大安山之北谿以免。
manualTranslations.literal: During Tianfu, when eunuchs were executed on a great scale, Rengong hid Juhan in a valley north of Mount Da'an to escape.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu purge of eunuchs, Rengong hid Juhan in a valley north of Mount Da'an to save his life.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後，梁兵攻仁恭，仁恭遣居翰從晉王攻梁潞州以牽其兵，晉遂取潞州，以居翰為昭義監軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, when Liang troops attacked Rengong, Rengong sent Juhan to follow the Prince of Jin in attacking Liang's Luzhou to draw off their forces; Jin then took Luzhou and made Juhan army supervisor of Zhaoyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, when Liang attacked Rengong, Rengong sent Juhan with the Prince of Jin against Liang's Luzhou to draw off Liang's army; Jin took Luzhou and appointed Juhan Zhaoyi army supervisor.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗即位，與郭崇韜並為樞密使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he and Guo Chongtao were jointly made Bureau Commissioners.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Juhan and Guo Chongtao were made joint Bureau Commissioners.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗滅梁而驕，宦官因以用事，郭崇韜又專任政，居翰默默，茍免而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and grew arrogant; eunuchs thereby came to power, Guo Chongtao again monopolized government, and Juhan kept silent, merely seeking to escape harm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he grew arrogant; eunuchs took power, Guo Chongtao dominated the government, and Juhan kept quiet, merely trying to stay out of trouble.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏王破蜀，王衍朝京師，行至秦川，而明宗軍變於魏。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince of Wei conquered Shu; Wang Yan went to the capital; when they reached Qinchuan, Mingzong's army mutinied at Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wei conquered Shu, Wang Yan set out for the capital; at Qinchuan, Mingzong's troops mutinied at Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗東征，慮衍有變，遣人馳詔魏王殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong marched east, fearing Yan might rebel, and sent a messenger with urgent orders for the Prince of Wei to kill him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong marched east, fearing Yan might turn rebellious, and sent urgent orders to the Prince of Wei to kill him.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔書已印畫，而居翰發視之，詔書言「誅衍一行」，居翰以謂殺降不祥，乃以詔傅柱，揩去「行」字，改為一「家」。
manualTranslations.literal: The edict was already sealed; but when Juhan opened and read it, the edict said "Execute Yan and his whole party." Juhan held that killing surrendered men was ill-omened, so he pressed the edict against a pillar, wiped away the character for "party," and changed it to "family."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict was already sealed, but Juhan opened it and read: "Execute Yan and his whole party." He held that killing surrendered men was ill-omened, pressed the edict to a pillar, wiped out the character for "party," and changed it to "family."

manualTranslations.zh: 時蜀降人與衍俱東者千餘人，皆獲免。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time more than a thousand Shu submitters traveling east with Yan were all spared.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: More than a thousand Shu men who were traveling east with Yan were all spared.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗遇弒，居翰見明宗於至德宮，求歸田里。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong was assassinated, Juhan met Mingzong at Zhide Palace and asked to retire to the countryside.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong was assassinated, Juhan met Mingzong at Zhide Palace and asked to return home to the fields.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成三年，卒於長安，年七十一。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng he died at Chang'an, aged seventy-one.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng 3 (928) he died at Chang'an, aged seventy-one.

sourceRange.text: 仁恭多智詐，善事人，事晉王愛將蓋寓尤謹，每對寓涕泣，自言：「居燕無罪，以讒見逐。」因道燕虛實，陳可取之謀，晉王益信而愛之。乾寧元年，晉擊破匡儔，乃以仁恭為幽州留後，留其親信燕留得等十餘人監其軍，為之請命于唐，拜檢校司空、盧龍軍節度使。其後晉攻羅弘信，求兵於仁恭，仁恭不與，晉王以書微責誚之，仁恭大怒，執晉使者，殺燕留得等以叛。晉王自將討之，戰于安塞，晉王大敗。光化元年，遣其子守文襲滄州，逐節度使盧彥威，遂取滄、景、德三州。為其子請命于唐，昭宗遲之，未即從，仁恭怒，語唐使者曰：「為我語天子，旌節吾自有，但要長安本色爾，何屢求而不得邪！」昭宗卒以守文為橫海軍節度使。

context.beforeSource: 匡威為弟匡儔所逐，仁恭聞亂，乃擁戍兵攻幽州，行至居庸關，戰敗，奔晉，晉以為壽陽鎮將。
context.afterSource: 仁恭父子率兩鎮兵十萬，號稱三十萬以擊魏，屠貝州。

manualTranslations.zh: 仁恭多智詐，善事人，事晉王愛將蓋寓尤謹，每對寓涕泣，自言：「居燕無罪，以讒見逐。」
manualTranslations.literal: Rengong was cunning and deceitful and skilled at winning people over. Toward Gai Yu, the Prince of Jin's beloved general, he was especially careful; each time he faced Yu he wept and said: "I am guilty of nothing in Yan yet was driven out by slander."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rengong was shrewd and slippery, good at courting men. With Gai Yu, the Prince of Jin's favorite general, he was especially careful—each meeting ended in tears as he said: "I did no wrong in Yan yet was driven out by slander."

manualTranslations.zh: 因道燕虛實，陳可取之謀，晉王益信而愛之。
manualTranslations.literal: He then spoke of Yan's true strength and weakness and laid out plans for taking it, and the Prince of Jin believed him all the more and cherished him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He laid out Yan's strengths and weaknesses and how to take it, and the Prince of Jin trusted and favored him all the more.

manualTranslations.zh: 乾寧元年，晉擊破匡儔，乃以仁恭為幽州留後，留其親信燕留得等十餘人監其軍，為之請命于唐，拜檢校司空、盧龍軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: In Qianning 1 Jin broke Kuangchou and made Rengong acting commissioner of Youzhou, leaving more than ten trusted men including Yan Liude to oversee his army and petitioning Tang on his behalf; he was appointed Acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Lu Long army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Qianning 1 Jin defeated Kuangchou and made Rengong acting commissioner of Youzhou, leaving a dozen trusted men including Yan Liude to watch his troops while he sought Tang confirmation; he received Acting Minister of Works and the Lu Long command.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後晉攻羅弘信，求兵於仁恭，仁恭不與，晉王以書微責誚之，仁恭大怒，執晉使者，殺燕留得等以叛。
manualTranslations.literal: Later when Jin attacked Luo Hongxin and asked troops of Rengong, Rengong refused. The Prince of Jin wrote a mild reproach; Rengong was furious, seized Jin's envoy, killed Yan Liude and the others, and rebelled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jin later attacked Luo Hongxin and asked Rengong for troops, Rengong refused. The Prince of Jin sent a reproach; Rengong flew into a rage, seized the Jin envoy, killed Yan Liude and the rest, and rebelled.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉王自將討之，戰于安塞，晉王大敗。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince of Jin came in person to punish him; they fought at Anse and Jin suffered a great defeat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin marched against him in person; at Anse Jin was routed.

manualTranslations.zh: 光化元年，遣其子守文襲滄州，逐節度使盧彥威，遂取滄、景、德三州。
manualTranslations.literal: In Guanghua 1 he sent his son Shouwen to raid Cangzhou, drove out the military commissioner Lu Yanwei, and took Cang, Jing, and De prefectures.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Guanghua 1 he sent Shouwen to strike Cangzhou, drove out Commissioner Lu Yanwei, and seized Cang, Jing, and De.

manualTranslations.zh: 為其子請命于唐，昭宗遲之，未即從，仁恭怒，語唐使者曰：「為我語天子，旌節吾自有，但要長安本色爾，何屢求而不得邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: He asked Tang to confirm his son; Zhaozong delayed and would not at once consent. Rengong was angry and told the Tang envoy: "Tell the Son of Heaven for me—I already hold the command; I only want the standard colors from Chang'an. Why must I beg again and again and still not receive them?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He petitioned Tang to confirm his son; Zhaozong stalled. Rengong raged and told the envoy: "Tell the emperor—I already have the command; I only want the imperial colors from Chang'an. Why must I keep asking and never receive them?"

manualTranslations.zh: 昭宗卒以守文為橫海軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: At last Zhaozong made Shouwen military commissioner of the Trans-Maritime army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhaozong finally made Shouwen commissioner of the Trans-Maritime army.

sourceRange.text: 匡威素少鎔，以謂無能為也，因與鎔方轡詣府，將代其位。行過親事營，軍士閉門大譟，天雨震電，暴風拔木，屋瓦皆飛。屠者墨君和望見鎔，識之，從缺垣中躍出，挾鎔于馬，負之而走，亂軍擊殺匡威、正抱，燕人皆走。匡儔雖憾其兄，而陽以大義責鎔甚急。鎔既失燕援，而晉軍急攻平山，劫鎔以盟，鎔遂與晉和。其後梁太祖下晉邢、洺、磁三州，乃為書詔古本作招。鎔，使絕晉而歸梁，鎔依違不決。一作訣。

localRange.text: 匡威素少镕，以謂無能為也，因與镕方轡詣府，將代其位。行過親事營，軍士閉門大噪，天雨震電，暴風拔木，屋瓦皆飛。屠者墨君和望見镕，識之，從缺垣中躍出，挾镕於馬，負之而走，亂軍擊殺匡威、正抱，燕人皆死。匡儔雖憾其兄，而陽以大義責镕甚急。镕既失燕援，而晉軍急攻平山，劫镕以盟，镕遂與晉和。其後梁太祖下晉邢、洺、磁三州，乃為書詔镕，使絕晉而歸梁，镕依違不決。

sourceRange.text: 光化三年，梁兵攻定州，郜遣處直率兵拒之，戰于沙河，為梁兵所敗。兵返入城逐郜，郜出奔晉，亂兵推處直為留後。梁兵圍之，處直遣人告梁，請絕晉而事梁，出絹十萬匹犒軍，乃與梁盟。梁太祖表處直義武軍節度使，累封太原王。太祖即位，封處直北平王。其後梁兵攻王鎔，鎔求救于晉，處直亦遣人至晉，願絕梁以自効。晉兵救鎔，處直以兵五千從，破梁軍於柏鄉。其後晉北破燕，南取魏博，與梁戰河上，十餘年，處直未嘗不以兵從。

context.beforeSource: 處直為後院中軍都知兵馬使。
context.afterSource: 處直好巫，而客有李應之者，妖妄人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 光化三年，梁兵攻定州，郜遣處直率兵拒之，戰于沙河，為梁兵所敗。
manualTranslations.literal: In Guanghua 3 Liang attacked Dingzhou; Gao sent Chuzhi to resist with troops. They fought at Shahe and were beaten by Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Guanghua 3 Liang attacked Dingzhou. Gao sent Chuzhi to meet them at Shahe and was defeated.

manualTranslations.zh: 兵返入城逐郜，郜出奔晉，亂兵推處直為留後。
manualTranslations.literal: Troops returning to the city drove out Gao; Gao fled to Jin and the mutineers made Chuzhi acting commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The troops turned on Gao in the city; he fled to Jin and the mutineers made Chuzhi acting commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁兵圍之，處直遣人告梁，請絕晉而事梁，出絹十萬匹犒軍，乃與梁盟。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang besieged the city; Chuzhi sent word to Liang, offering to break with Jin and serve Liang, presented a hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, and made alliance with Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang besieged him. Chuzhi offered to abandon Jin for Liang, sent a hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, and made peace with Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁太祖表處直義武軍節度使，累封太原王。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang Taizu memorialized Chuzhi as military commissioner of the Yiwu army and repeatedly enfeoffed him Prince of Taiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu confirmed Chuzhi as Yiwu commissioner and repeatedly enfeoffed him Prince of Taiyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖即位，封處直北平王。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu took the throne he enfeoffed Chuzhi Prince of Beiping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne he made Chuzhi Prince of Beiping.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後梁兵攻王鎔，鎔求救于晉，處直亦遣人至晉，願絕梁以自効。
manualTranslations.literal: Later when Liang attacked Wang Rong and Rong begged Jin for aid, Chuzhi too sent envoys to Jin offering to break with Liang and prove his worth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, when Liang attacked Wang Rong and Rong called on Jin, Chuzhi also sent envoys offering to break with Liang and prove his loyalty.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉兵救鎔，處直以兵五千從，破梁軍於柏鄉。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin marched to save Rong; Chuzhi followed with five thousand men and defeated Liang at Baixiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin marched to save Rong; Chuzhi brought five thousand men and helped break Liang at Baixiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後晉北破燕，南取魏博，與梁戰河上，十餘年，處直未嘗不以兵從。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereafter Jin broke Yan in the north and took Weibo in the south and fought Liang along the Yellow River for more than ten years; Chuzhi never failed to follow with troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For more than ten years Jin broke Yan in the north, seized Weibo in the south, and fought Liang along the river; Chuzhi always marched with them.

sourceRange.text: 晏球屯軍望都，與都及契丹戰，大敗之曲陽，都及禿餒得數騎遯去，閉城不復出。初，莊宗軍中闌得一男子，愛之，使冒姓李，名繼陶，養於宮中以為子。明宗即位，安重誨出以乞段徊，徊亦惡而逐之。都使人求得之。至是，紿其眾曰：「此莊宗太子也。」被以天子之服，使巡城上，以示晏球軍，軍士識者曰：「繼陶也。」共詬之。都居城中，兵少，惟以契丹二千人守城，呼禿餒為餒王，屈身事之。諸將有欲出降者，都伺察嚴密，殺戮無虛日，以故堅守經年。天成四年二月，城破，都與家屬皆自焚死，王氏遂絕于中山。而處存有子鄴，鄴子廷胤，與莊宗連外姻，為人驍勇，自為軍校，能與士卒同辛苦，明宗時，歷貝、忻、密、澶、隰州刺史。范延光反于鄴，晉高祖以廷胤為楊光遠行營中軍使。破延光有功，拜彰德軍節度使。

manualTranslations.literal: Earlier Zhuangzong's army had seized a boy along the road; he favored him, had him take the surname Li and the name Jitao, and raised him in the palace as a son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhuangzong's army had picked up a boy on the march; he favored him, gave him the Li surname and the name Jitao, and raised him in the palace as a son.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗即位，安重誨出以乞段徊，徊亦惡而逐之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne An Chonghui turned him out as a gift to Duan Huai; Huai too despised him and drove him away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne An Chonghui palmed him off on Duan Huai; Huai despised him and drove him out.

manualTranslations.zh: 都使人求得之。
manualTranslations.literal: Du sent men to obtain him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du sent men to find him.

manualTranslations.zh: 至是，紿其眾曰：「此莊宗太子也。」
manualTranslations.literal: At this point he deceived his followers, saying: "This is Zhuangzong's crown prince."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then he deceived his men, saying: "This is Zhuangzong's crown prince."

manualTranslations.zh: 被以天子之服，使巡城上，以示晏球軍，軍士識者曰：「繼陶也。」
manualTranslations.literal: They dressed him in imperial robes, had him patrol the wall to display him to Yanqiu's army, and soldiers who recognized him cried: "It is Jitao!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They dressed him in imperial robes and paraded him on the wall for Yanqiu's army. Men who knew him shouted: "That is Jitao!"

manualTranslations.zh: 共詬之。
manualTranslations.literal: Together they reviled him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Together they cursed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 都居城中，兵少，惟以契丹二千人守城，呼禿餒為餒王，屈身事之。
manualTranslations.literal: Du held the city with few troops—only two thousand Khitan guarded the walls. He called Tuyu "King Tuyu" and humbled himself to serve him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du held the city with few men—only two thousand Khitan guarded the walls. He called Tuyu "King Tuyu" and bowed to serve him.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸將有欲出降者，都伺察嚴密，殺戮無虛日，以故堅守經年。
manualTranslations.literal: When some generals wished to surrender, Du watched them closely and killed without a day off, and for that reason the siege held for a year.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When generals wanted to surrender, Du watched them closely and killed every day without fail, and the city held for a year.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成四年二月，城破，都與家屬皆自焚死，王氏遂絕于中山。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of Tiancheng 4 the city fell; Du and his household all burned themselves to death, and the Wang line ended at Zhongshan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tiancheng 4 the city fell. Du and his family burned themselves to death, and the Wang line ended at Zhongshan.

manualTranslations.zh: 而處存有子鄴，鄴子廷胤，與莊宗連外姻，為人驍勇，自為軍校，能與士卒同辛苦，明宗時，歷貝、忻、密、澶、隰州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: Chucun had a son Ye, and Ye's son Tingyin was connected by marriage to Zhuangzong's house. A fierce and brave man, he rose from army officer, shared the soldiers' hardships, and under Mingzong served in turn as prefect of Bei, Xin, Mi, Chan, and Xi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chucun had a son Ye, and Ye's son Tingyin married into Zhuangzong's kin. Fierce and brave, he rose from the ranks, shared the soldiers' hardships, and under Mingzong served as prefect of Bei, Xin, Mi, Chan, and Xi.

manualTranslations.zh: 范延光反于鄴，晉高祖以廷胤為楊光遠行營中軍使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye, Jin Gaozu made Tingyin central army commander of Yang Guangyuan's mobile headquarters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye, Gaozu made Tingyin central army commander under Yang Guangyuan's mobile headquarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 破延光有功，拜彰德軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: For breaking Yanguang he was rewarded and appointed military commissioner of the Zhangde army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For defeating Yanguang he was made commissioner of the Zhangde army.

sourceRange.text: 鎔介於其間，而承祖父百年之業，士馬彊而畜積富，為唐累世藩臣。故鎔年雖少，藉其世家以取重，四方諸鎮廢立承繼，有請於唐者，皆因鎔以聞。自晉兵出山東，已破孟遷，取邢、洺、磁三州，景福元年，乃大舉擊趙，下臨城。鎔求救於李匡威，匡威來救，晉軍解去。明年，晉會王處存攻鎔堅固、新市。晉王與處存皆自將，而鎔未嘗臨軍，遣追風都團練使段亮、翦寇都團練使馬珂等，以兵屬匡威而已。匡威戰磁河，晉軍大敗。明年春，晉攻天長軍，鎔出兵救之，敗于叱日嶺，晉軍遂出井陘。鎔又求救於匡威，晉軍解去。初，匡威悅其弟匡儔之婦美而淫之，匡儔怒，及其救鎔也，誘其軍亂而自立。

localRange.text: 镕介於其間，而承祖父百年之業，士馬強而畜積富，為唐累世藩臣。故镕年雖少，藉其世家以取重，四方諸鎮廢立承繼，有請於唐者，皆因镕以聞。初，匡威悅其弟匡儔之婦美而淫之，匡儔怒，及其救镕也，誘其軍亂而自立。

context.beforeSource: 是時，晉新有太原，李匡威據幽州，王處存據中山，赫連鐸據大同，孟方立據邢臺，四面豪傑並起而交爭。
context.afterSource: 匡威內慚不敢還，乃以符印歸其弟，而將奔于京師。
