manualTranslations.zh: 自晉兵出山東，已破孟遷，取邢、洺、磁三州，景福元年，乃大舉擊趙，下臨城。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jin armies marched out from Shandong they had already broken Meng Qian and taken Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures. In Jingfu 1 they launched a major assault on Zhao and took Lincheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Jin marched out of Shandong it had already broken Meng Qian and taken Xing, Ming, and Ci. In Jingfu 1 it struck Zhao in force and took Lincheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 鎔求救於李匡威，匡威來救，晉軍解去。
manualTranslations.literal: Rong begged Li Kuangwei for rescue; Kuangwei came and Jin withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rong called on Li Kuangwei; Kuangwei marched to save him and Jin pulled back.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，晉會王處存攻鎔堅固、新市。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year Jin joined Wang Chucun to attack Jangu and Xinshi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year Jin and Wang Chucun attacked Jangu and Xinshi.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉王與處存皆自將，而鎔未嘗臨軍，遣追風都團練使段亮、翦寇都團練使馬珂等，以兵屬匡威而已。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince of Jin and Chucun both commanded in person, but Rong never went to the field himself—he sent Duan Liang, regimental training commissioner of Pursuing Wind, Ma Ke, regimental training commissioner of Shearing Bandits, and others, placing the troops under Kuangwei only.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Both commanders led in person, but Rong never took the field—he sent Duan Liang of Pursuing Wind and Ma Ke of Shearing Bandits and left the troops to Kuangwei.

manualTranslations.zh: 匡威戰磁河，晉軍大敗。
manualTranslations.literal: Kuangwei fought at Ci River and Jin was badly defeated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Ci River Kuangwei smashed the Jin army.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年春，晉攻天長軍，鎔出兵救之，敗于叱日嶺，晉軍遂出井陘。
manualTranslations.literal: The next spring Jin attacked Tianchang Garrison. Rong sent troops to relieve it, was beaten at Chiri Ridge, and Jin marched out through Jingxing Pass.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Next spring Jin attacked Tianchang Garrison. Rong sent relief, was beaten at Chiri Ridge, and Jin marched out through Jingxing Pass.

manualTranslations.zh: 鎔又求救於匡威，晉軍解去。
manualTranslations.literal: Rong again begged Kuangwei and Jin withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rong begged Kuangwei again and Jin withdrew once more.

sourceRange.text: 前帥史憲誠、何全皡、韓君雄、樂彥貞等，皆由牙軍所立，怒輒遂古本作逐字。殺之。

context.afterSource: 紹威為人精悍明敏，通習吏事，為政有威嚴，然其家世由牙軍所立。

sourceRange.text: 太祖圍滄州未下，劉守光會晉軍破梁潞州。太祖自長蘆歸，過魏，疾作，臥府中，諸將莫得見，紹威懼太祖終襲己，乃乘間入見曰：「今四方稱兵，為梁患者，以唐在故也；唐家天命已去，不如早自取之。」太祖大喜，乃急歸。太祖即位，將都洛陽，紹威取魏良材為五鳳樓、朝元前殿，浮河而上，立之京師。太祖嘆曰：「吾聞蕭何守關中，為漢起未央宮，豈若紹威越千里而為此，若神化然，功過蕭何遠矣！」賜以寶帶名馬。

context.beforeSource: 昭宗東遷洛陽，詔諸鎮繕理京師，紹威營太廟成，加拜守侍中，進封鄴王。
context.afterSource: 燕王劉守光囚其父仁恭，與其兄守文有隙，紹威馳書勸守光等降梁。

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖圍滄州未下，劉守光會晉軍破梁潞州。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu besieged Cangzhou without success; Liu Shouguang joined Jin troops and broke Liang at Luzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu besieged Cangzhou without taking it; Liu Shouguang joined Jin and broke Liang at Luzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖自長蘆歸，過魏，疾作，臥府中，諸將莫得見，紹威懼太祖終襲己，乃乘間入見曰：「今四方稱兵，為梁患者，以唐在故也；
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu returned from Changlu, passed through Wei, fell ill, and lay in the headquarters; his generals could not see him. Shaowei feared Taizu would at last seize him, so he found an opening to enter and said: "Armies rise on every side; the harm to Liang is that Tang still exists;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu came back from Changlu, passed through Wei, fell ill, and lay in the yamen where no general could see him. Shaowei feared Taizu would finish him and slipped in to say: "Armies rise everywhere; Liang's trouble is that Tang still lives;

manualTranslations.zh: 唐家天命已去，不如早自取之。」
manualTranslations.literal: The House of Tang has lost Heaven's mandate—better take it yourself while there is time."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Tang mandate is gone—take the throne yourself while you can."

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖大喜，乃急歸。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased and hurried home.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and hurried home.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖即位，將都洛陽，紹威取魏良材為五鳳樓、朝元前殿，浮河而上，立之京師。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu took the throne and prepared to move the capital to Luoyang, Shaowei took fine timber from Wei for the Five-Phoenix Tower and the Chaoyuan front hall, floated them upriver, and erected them in the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne and planned to move the capital to Luoyang, Shaowei sent Wei's best timber for the Five-Phoenix Tower and Chaoyuan front hall, floated it upriver, and raised it in the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖嘆曰：「吾聞蕭何守關中，為漢起未央宮，豈若紹威越千里而為此，若神化然，功過蕭何遠矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu sighed and said: "I have heard that Xiao He guarded the passes of Guanzhong and built the Weiyang Palace for Han—how does that compare with Shaowei crossing a thousand li to do this, as if by divine transformation? His merit surpasses Xiao He's by far!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu sighed: "Xiao He held Guanzhong and built the Weiyang Palace for Han—how does that compare with Shaowei crossing a thousand li to do this, as if by magic? His merit leaves Xiao He far behind!"

manualTranslations.zh: 賜以寶帶名馬。
manualTranslations.literal: He bestowed jeweled belts and famous horses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He gave him jeweled belts and famous horses.

context.beforeSource: 」後徙鎮海而卒。
context.afterSource: 劉守光，深州樂壽人也。

sourceRange.text: 大順元年，以兵屬張濬伐晉，濬敗，建自含山遯歸。河中王重盈死，諸子珂、珙爭立，晉人助珂，建與王行瑜、李茂貞助珙。昭宗不許，建等大怒，以三鎮兵犯京師。昭宗見建等責之，行瑜、茂貞惶恐戰汗不能語，獨建前自陳述。乃殺宰相韋昭度、李磎等，謀廢昭宗。會晉舉兵且至，建等懼，乃還。晉兵問罪三鎮，兵傅華州，建登城呼曰：「弊邑未常失禮於大國，何為見攻？」晉人曰：「君以兵犯天子，殺大臣，是以討也。」已而與晉和。

context.beforeSource: 當時號為「北韓南郭」。
context.afterSource: 乾寧三年，李茂貞復犯京師，昭宗將奔太原，次渭北，建遣子允請幸華州。

manualTranslations.zh: 大順元年，以兵屬張濬伐晉，濬敗，建自含山遯歸。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Dashun he placed his troops under Zhang Jun to campaign against Jin; Jun was defeated, and Jian fled back from Hanshan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Dashun 1 (890) he lent his troops to Zhang Jun’s campaign against Jin. Jun was beaten, and Jian fled back from Hanshan.

manualTranslations.zh: 河中王重盈死，諸子珂、珙爭立，晉人助珂，建與王行瑜、李茂貞助珙。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Chongying of Hedong died; his sons Ke and Gong contended for succession; Jin supported Ke, and Jian with Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen supported Gong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wang Chongying of Hedong died, his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit. Jin backed Ke; Jian, Wang Xingyu, and Li Maozhen backed Gong.

manualTranslations.zh: 昭宗不許，建等大怒，以三鎮兵犯京師。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhaozong did not permit it; Jian and the others were greatly enraged and led troops from the three circuits against the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhaozong refused. Jian and his allies, furious, marched on the capital from three circuits.

manualTranslations.zh: 昭宗見建等責之，行瑜、茂貞惶恐戰汗不能語，獨建前自陳述。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhaozong received Jian and the others and reproached them; Xingyu and Maozhen were afraid, trembling and sweating, and could not speak; only Jian stepped forward and spoke for himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhaozong confronted Jian and his allies and rebuked them. Xingyu and Maozhen shook with fear and could not speak. Only Jian stepped forward to plead his case.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃殺宰相韋昭度、李磎等，謀廢昭宗。
manualTranslations.literal: They then killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu, Li Xi, and others and plotted to depose Zhaozong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi and plotted to depose Zhaozong.

manualTranslations.zh: 會晉舉兵且至，建等懼，乃還。
manualTranslations.literal: Just then Jin also raised troops and was about to arrive; Jian and the others were afraid and withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin was marching too, and Jian and his allies, afraid, pulled back.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉兵問罪三鎮，兵傅華州，建登城呼曰：「弊邑未常失禮於大國，何為見攻？」
manualTranslations.literal: Jin’s army demanded satisfaction from the three circuits; troops pressed Hua Prefecture; Jian mounted the wall and called out: “My little city has never been disrespectful to your great state—why are we attacked?”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin pressed the three circuits and besieged Hua. Jian mounted the wall and shouted: “My city has never slighted your great state—why attack us?”

manualTranslations.zh: 晉人曰：「君以兵犯天子，殺大臣，是以討也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The men of Jin said: “You led troops against the Son of Heaven and killed great ministers—that is why you are punished.”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin answered: “You marched on the emperor and killed his ministers. That is why we fight you.”

manualTranslations.zh: 已而與晉和。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long they made peace with Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they made peace with Jin.

sourceRange.text: 梁開平二年，思諫卒，軍中立其子彝昌為留後，即拜彝昌節度使。明年，其將高宗益作亂，殺彝昌。

localRange.text: 梁開平二年，思諫卒，軍中立其子彜昌為留後，梁即拜彜昌節度使。明年，其將高宗益作亂，殺彜昌。

sourceRange.text: 建已殺諸王，乃營南莊，起樓閣，欲邀昭宗遊幸，因以廢之而立德王裕。其父叔豐謂建曰：「汝陳、許間一田夫爾，遭時之亂，蒙天子厚恩至此，欲以兩州百里之地行大事，覆族之禍，吾不忍見，不如先死！」因泣下歔欷。李茂貞、梁太祖皆欲發兵迎天子，建稍恐懼，乃止。光化元年，昭宗還長安，自為建畫像，封建潁川郡王，賜以鐵券。建辭王爵，乃封建許國公。梁太祖以兵嚮長安，遣張存敬攻同州，建判官司馬鄴以城降，太祖使鄴召建，建乃出降。

manualTranslations.zh: 建已殺諸王，乃營南莊，起樓閣，欲邀昭宗遊幸，因以廢之而立德王裕。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian had already killed the princes; he then built the Southern Villa and raised towers and pavilions, wishing to invite Zhaozong on an excursion so as to depose him and set up Prince of De Yu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After killing the princes, Jian built the Southern Villa with towers and pavilions, hoping to lure Zhaozong on a visit, depose him, and raise Prince of De Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 其父叔豐謂建曰：「汝陳、許間一田夫爾，遭時之亂，蒙天子厚恩至此，欲以兩州百里之地行大事，覆族之禍，吾不忍見，不如先死！」
manualTranslations.literal: His father Shufeng said to Jian: “You were only a farmer between Chen and Xu; in the disorder of the times you received the Son of Heaven’s great favor to reach this point; yet you wish to attempt a great affair with a domain of two prefectures and a hundred li—the calamity of exterminating the clan—I cannot bear to see it; better to die first!”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Shufeng told him: “You were a farmer between Chen and Xu. In these troubled times the emperor raised you this high. To attempt a coup with two prefectures and a hundred li is to invite the ruin of our whole clan. I cannot watch it—let me die first!”

manualTranslations.zh: 因泣下歔欷。
manualTranslations.literal: He then wept and sobbed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He wept aloud.

manualTranslations.zh: 李茂貞、梁太祖皆欲發兵迎天子，建稍恐懼，乃止。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Maozhen and Liang Taizu both wished to raise troops to welcome the Son of Heaven back; Jian grew somewhat afraid and stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen and Liang Taizu both prepared to march and rescue the emperor. Jian grew afraid and dropped the plan.

manualTranslations.zh: 光化元年，昭宗還長安，自為建畫像，封建潁川郡王，賜以鐵券。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Guanghua, Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, personally painted Jian’s portrait, enfeoffed him Prince of Yingchuan Commandery, and granted him an iron certificate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Guanghua 1 (898) Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, painted Jian’s portrait himself, made him Prince of Yingchuan, and granted him an iron certificate of mercy.

manualTranslations.zh: 建辭王爵，乃封建許國公。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian declined the princely rank and was therefore enfeoffed Duke of Xu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jian refused the princely title and was made Duke of Xu instead.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁太祖以兵向長安，遣張存敬攻同州，建判官司馬鄴以城降，太祖使鄴召建，建乃出降。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang Taizu marched on Chang’an, sent Zhang Cunjing to attack Tong Prefecture; Jian’s judge Sima Ye surrendered the city; Taizu had Ye summon Jian, and Jian then came out and submitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang Taizu marched on Chang’an and sent Zhang Cunjing against Tong. Jian’s judge Sima Ye opened the gates. Taizu sent Ye to call Jian out, and Jian surrendered.

sourceRange.text: __TOC__李茂貞，深州博野人也。本姓宋，名文通，為博野軍卒，戍鳳翔。黃巢犯京師，鄭畋以博野軍擊賊，茂貞以功自隊長遷軍校。光啟元年，朱玫反，僖宗出居興元。玫遣王行瑜攻大散關，茂貞與保鑾都將李鋋等敗行瑜於大唐峯。明年，玫遂敗死。茂貞以功自扈蹕都頭拜武定軍節度使，賜以姓名。扈蹕東歸，至鳳翔，鳳翔節度使李昌符與天威都頭楊守立爭道，以兵相攻，昌符不勝，走隴州。僖宗遣茂貞擊殺昌符，以功拜鳳翔隴右節度使。大順元年，封隴西郡王。

context.afterSource: 二年，樞密使楊復恭得罪，奔於興元，興元節度使楊守亮，復恭之養子也，納之。

manualTranslations.zh: 李茂貞，深州博野人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Maozhen was a native of Boye in Shen Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen came from Boye in Shen Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 本姓宋，名文通，為博野軍卒，戍鳳翔。
manualTranslations.literal: His original surname was Song and his given name Wentong; he was a soldier of the Boye Army and garrisoned Fengxiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Born Song Wentong, he served as a soldier in the Boye Army and was posted to Fengxiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃巢犯京師，鄭畋以博野軍擊賊，茂貞以功自隊長遷軍校。
manualTranslations.literal: When Huang Chao invaded the capital, Zheng Tian led the Boye Army against the rebels, and Maozhen for merit rose from squad leader to army officer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao struck the capital, Zheng Tian led the Boye Army against him. Maozhen rose from squad leader to army officer for his service.

manualTranslations.zh: 光啟元年，朱玫反，僖宗出居興元。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Guangqi, Zhu Mei rebelled and Emperor Xizong went out to dwell at Xingyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Guangqi 1 (885) Zhu Mei rebelled, and Emperor Xizong withdrew to Xingyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 玫遣王行瑜攻大散關，茂貞與保鑾都將李鋋等敗行瑜於大唐峯。
manualTranslations.literal: Mei sent Wang Xingyu to attack Dasanguan; Maozhen with Palace Guard general Li Chan and others defeated Xingyu at Datang Peak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mei sent Wang Xingyu against Dasanguan. Maozhen and Palace Guard general Li Chan defeated him at Datang Peak.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，玫遂敗死。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year Mei was defeated and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year Mei was defeated and killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 茂貞以功自扈蹕都頭拜武定軍節度使，賜以姓名。
manualTranslations.literal: Maozhen for merit rose from commander of the imperial escort to military commissioner of the Wuding Army and was granted his present surname and name.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For his service Maozhen rose from commander of the imperial escort to military commissioner of Wuding and received the surname and name by which he was known.

manualTranslations.zh: 扈蹕東歸，至鳳翔，鳳翔節度使李昌符與天威都頭楊守立爭道，以兵相攻，昌符不勝，走隴州。
manualTranslations.literal: Escorting the emperor east on his return, they reached Fengxiang; Fengxiang military commissioner Li Changfu and Celestial Might commander Yang Shouli contended for the road and attacked each other with troops; Changfu could not prevail and fled to Long Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the eastward return to court they reached Fengxiang. Li Changfu, military commissioner of Fengxiang, and Yang Shouli, commander of Celestial Might, fought over the road. Changfu lost and fled to Longzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 僖宗遣茂貞擊殺昌符，以功拜鳳翔隴右節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Xizong sent Maozhen to strike and kill Changfu, and for merit made him military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xizong sent Maozhen to kill Changfu and, for that service, made him military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

manualTranslations.zh: 大順元年，封隴西郡王。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Dashun he was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi Commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Dashun 1 (890) he was made Prince of Longxi.

manualTranslations.zh: 滿居朗州，引沅水塹其城，上為長橋，為不可攻之計。
manualTranslations.literal: Man made his seat in Langzhou, diverted the Yuan River as a moat for his city, and built a long bridge above it as a plan to make it unassailable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Man made Langzhou his capital. He diverted the Yuan River to moat the walls and built a long bridge across it, planning to make the city impregnable.

manualTranslations.zh: 天祐中，滿卒，子彥恭自立。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Tianyou era Man died, and his son Yan Gong installed himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Tianyou Man died. His son Yan Gong seized power for himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 彥恭附于楊行密，亦嘗攻劫為荊、湖患。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan Gong submitted to Yang Xingmi but also raided and plundered, becoming a scourge to Jing and the lakes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan Gong allied with Yang Xingmi but kept raiding as well, plaguing Jing and the lake country.

manualTranslations.zh: 開平元年，馬殷發兵攻彥恭，恃塹為阻，逾年不能破。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Kaiping Ma Yin sent troops to attack Yan Gong; relying on the moat as a barrier, for more than a year they could not break it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 1 (907) Ma Yin marched on Yan Gong. The moat held them off for more than a year.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，彥恭奔于楊行密，馬殷擒其弟彥雄等七人送于梁，斬于汴市，彥恭卒於淮南，澧、朗遂入于楚。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year Yan Gong fled to Yang Xingmi. Ma Yin captured his younger brother Yan Xiong and seven others, sent them to Liang, and had them executed in the Bian market. Yan Gong died in Huainan, and Li and Lang thereafter fell to Chu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In year 3 Yan Gong fled to Yang Xingmi. Ma Yin seized his brother Yan Xiong and six others, sent the seven captives to Liang, and had them beheaded in Bian. Yan Gong died in Huainan. Li and Lang passed to Chu.

sourceRange.text: 是時，梁將劉鄩等與莊宗相距澶、魏之間，兵數敗。巖曰：「古之王者必郊祀天地，陛下即位猶未郊天，議者以為朝廷無異藩鎮，如此何以威重天下？今河北雖失，天下幸安，願陛下力行之。」敬翔以為不可，曰：「今府庫虛竭，箕斂供軍，若行郊禋，則必賞賚；是取虛名而受實弊也。」末帝不聽，乃備法駕幸西京，而莊宗取楊劉，或傳：「晉兵入東都矣！」或曰：「扼汜水矣！」或曰：「下鄆、濮矣！」京師大風拔木，末帝大懼，從官相顧而泣，末帝乃還東都，遂不果郊。鎮州張文禮殺王鎔，使人告梁曰：「臣已北召契丹，願梁以兵萬人出德、棣州，則晉兵憊矣。

localRange.text: 鎮州張文禮殺王镕，使人告梁曰：「臣已北召契丹，願梁以兵萬人出德、棣州，則晉兵憊矣。

context.beforeSource: 牙兵亂，以魏博降晉，梁由是盡失河北。
context.afterSource: 」敬翔以為然，巖與漢傑皆以為不可，乃止。
context.beforeLocal: 牙兵亂，以魏博降晉，梁由是盡失河北。
context.afterLocal: 敬翔以為然，巖與漢傑皆以為不可，乃止。

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，梁將劉鄩等與莊宗相距澶、魏之間，兵數敗。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Liang generals Liu Zan and others faced Zhuangzong between Cang and Wei; their armies were repeatedly defeated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang generals led by Liu Zan were facing Zhuangzong between Cang and Wei, and their armies kept losing.

manualTranslations.zh: 巖曰：「古之王者必郊祀天地，陛下即位猶未郊天，議者以為朝廷無異藩鎮，如此何以威重天下？
manualTranslations.literal: Yan said: "Ancient kings invariably performed suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. Your Majesty has been enthroned yet has still not sacrificed to Heaven. Critics say the court is no different from a frontier command—how can it awe the realm?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan said: "Ancient kings always sacrificed to Heaven and Earth in the suburbs. Your Majesty has reigned yet never performed the suburban rite. People say the court looks no different from a frontier command—how will it awe the realm?

manualTranslations.zh: 今河北雖失，天下幸安，願陛下力行之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Hebei is lost, yet the rest of the empire is still at peace. I beg Your Majesty to do this resolutely."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hebei is gone, but the rest of the empire is still at peace. I beg Your Majesty to do it at once."

manualTranslations.zh: 敬翔以為不可，曰：「今府庫虛竭，箕斂供軍，若行郊禋，則必賞賚；
manualTranslations.literal: Jing Xiang thought it impossible and said: "The treasury is empty and levies are scraped to feed the armies. If you perform the suburban rites, rewards must follow—
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang refused: "The vaults are empty and every levy goes to the armies. Hold the suburban rites and you must shower rewards—

manualTranslations.zh: 是取虛名而受實弊也。」
manualTranslations.literal: taking empty fame while suffering real harm."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: empty glory for real ruin."

manualTranslations.zh: 末帝不聽，乃備法駕幸西京，而莊宗取楊劉，或傳：「晉兵入東都矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: The Last Emperor would not listen and prepared the imperial carriage for the western capital. Zhuangzong then took Yangliu. Some reported: "Jin troops have entered the eastern capital!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor would not listen and prepared to go to the western capital. Zhuangzong took Yangliu. Rumors flew: "Jin is in the eastern capital!"

manualTranslations.zh: 或曰：「扼汜水矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: Others said: "They hold Sishui!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Others said: "They hold Sishui!"

manualTranslations.zh: 或曰：「下鄆、濮矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: Or: "They have taken Yun and Pu!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Or: "They have taken Yun and Pu!"

manualTranslations.zh: 京師大風拔木，末帝大懼，從官相顧而泣，末帝乃還東都，遂不果郊。
manualTranslations.literal: A great wind in the capital uprooted trees. The Last Emperor was greatly afraid; attendants looked at one another and wept. He returned to the eastern capital and the suburban sacrifice was never carried out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A gale uprooted trees in the capital. The Last Emperor panicked; courtiers wept at one another. He turned back to the eastern capital and never performed the suburban rite.

sourceRange.text: 晉數遣李存孝等出兵以窺山東，三州之人俘掠殆盡，赤地數千里，無復耕桑者累年。方立以孤城自守，求救于梁，梁方東事兗、鄆，不能救也。文德元年，方立乞兵于王鎔以攻晉，鎔許之。方立乃遣其將奚忠信攻晉遼州，而鎔以佗故不能出兵。兵既失約，忠信大敗，而晉兵乘勝攻之。

context.beforeSource: 晉遣李克修為澤潞節度使，方立以邢、洺、磁三州自為昭義軍。
context.afterSource: 方立將石元佐者，善兵而多智，方立嘗信用之。

manualTranslations.zh: 晉數遣李存孝等出兵以窺山東，三州之人俘掠殆盡，赤地數千里，無復耕桑者累年。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin repeatedly sent Li Cunxiao and others to probe Shandong. The people of the three prefectures were plundered almost to extinction; for thousands of li the land was bare, and for years none farmed or raised silkworms again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin kept sending Li Cunxiao and others to probe Shandong. The three prefectures were stripped almost bare; for thousands of li nothing grew, and for years no one farmed or raised silkworms.

manualTranslations.zh: 方立以孤城自守，求救于梁，梁方東事兗、鄆，不能救也。
manualTranslations.literal: Fangli held his lone city and begged Liang for help, but Liang was then engaged in the east at Yan and Yun and could not save him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fangli held out in his lone city and begged Liang for help, but Liang was tied down in Yan and Yun and could not come.

manualTranslations.zh: 文德元年，方立乞兵于王鎔以攻晉，鎔許之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Wende, Fangli asked Wang Rong for troops to attack Jin; Rong agreed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Wende 1 Fangli asked Wang Rong for troops against Jin; Rong agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 方立乃遣其將奚忠信攻晉遼州，而鎔以佗故不能出兵。
manualTranslations.literal: Fangli sent his general Xi Zhongxin to attack Jin’s Liaozhou, but Rong for other reasons could not march.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fangli sent Xi Zhongxin against Jin’s Liaozhou, but Rong could not march for other reasons.

manualTranslations.zh: 兵既失約，忠信大敗，而晉兵乘勝攻之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the promised troops failed to come, Zhongxin was utterly defeated, and Jin forces pressed the attack.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the promised troops never came, Zhongxin was smashed and Jin pressed the attack.

context.beforeSource: 卒年五十二。
context.afterSource: 王師範，青州人也。
context.beforeLocal: 卒年五十二。
context.afterLocal: 王師範，青州人也。

sourceRange.text: 外無救兵，城中食且盡，方立夜出巡城，號令守者，守者皆不應，方立知不可，乃歸飲酖而卒。軍中以其弟洺州刺史遷為留後，求救於梁。梁太祖遣王虔裕將騎兵三百助遷守，遷執虔裕降晉。晉徙遷族于太原，以為汾州刺史，後以為澤潞節度使。天復元年，梁遣氏叔琮攻晉，出天井關，遷開門降，為梁兵鄉道以攻太原，不克。叔琮軍還過潞，以遷歸于梁，梁太祖惡其返覆，殺之。

localRange.text: 外無救兵，城中食且盡，方立夜出巡城，號令守者，守者皆不應，方立知不可，乃歸飲鴆而卒。

manualTranslations.zh: 外無救兵，城中食且盡，方立夜出巡城，號令守者，守者皆不應，方立知不可，乃歸飲酖而卒。
manualTranslations.literal: With no relief from outside and food in the city nearly gone, Fangli went out at night to tour the walls and call orders to the defenders; the defenders would not answer. Fangli knew it was hopeless, returned, drank poison, and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: No help came. The granaries ran dry. Fangli walked the walls at night, shouting orders; no one answered. He knew the game was over, went home, and drank poison.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍中以其弟洺州刺史遷為留後，求救於梁。
manualTranslations.literal: The army made his younger brother Qian, prefect of Ming, acting commissioner and sent to Liang for help.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The army made his younger brother Qian, prefect of Ming, acting commissioner and begged Liang for help.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁太祖遣王虔裕將騎兵三百助遷守，遷執虔裕降晉。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang Taizu sent Wang Qianyu with three hundred cavalry to help Qian hold the city; Qian seized Qianyu and surrendered to Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Wang Qianyu with three hundred horsemen to help Qian hold the city. Qian seized Qianyu and surrendered to Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉徙遷族于太原，以為汾州刺史，後以為澤潞節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin moved Qian’s clan to Taiyuan, made him prefect of Fen, and later military governor of Ze and Lu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin moved Qian’s clan to Taiyuan, made him prefect of Fen, and later governor of Ze and Lu.

manualTranslations.zh: 天復元年，梁遣氏叔琮攻晉，出天井關，遷開門降，為梁兵鄉道以攻太原，不克。
manualTranslations.literal: In Tianfu 1 Liang sent Shi Shucong against Jin through Tianjing Pass; Qian opened the gates and surrendered, guiding Liang troops to attack Taiyuan—they did not take it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 1 Liang sent Shi Shucong against Jin through Tianjing Pass. Qian opened the gates, guided Liang toward Taiyuan, and failed to take it.

manualTranslations.zh: 叔琮軍還過潞，以遷歸于梁，梁太祖惡其返覆，殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Shucong’s army passed Lu on its return and brought Qian back to Liang; Liang Taizu hated his treachery and killed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shucong passed Lu on the march home and brought Qian back to Liang. Taizu hated his double-dealing and killed him.

sourceRange.text: 太祖即位，召為右金吾衞上將軍，居于洛陽。太祖心欲誅之，未有以發。太祖諸子已封王，宴於宮中，友寧妻泣謂太祖曰：「陛下化家為國，諸子人人皆得封，而妾夫獨以戰死，奈何讎人猶在朝廷！」太祖奮然戟手曰：「吾亦幾忘此賊！」乃遣人就洛陽族滅之。使者至，先掘坑於外，乃入告之。師範設席為具，與諸宗族飲酒，謂使者曰：「死，人之所不免，況有罪乎？然懼少長失序，下愧於先人。」酒半，令少長以次起，就戮於坑所，聞者皆哀憐之。同光三年，贈師範太尉。

context.beforeSource: 久之，表師範河陽節度使。
context.afterSource: 李罕之，陳州項城人也。

context.afterLocal: 李罕之，陳州項城人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖即位，召為右金吾衞上將軍，居于洛陽。
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu took the throne he summoned Shifan as general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and had him live in Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne he recalled Shifan as general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and kept him in Luoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖心欲誅之，未有以發。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu wished to kill him but had no occasion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu wanted him dead but had no pretext.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖諸子已封王，宴於宮中，友寧妻泣謂太祖曰：「陛下化家為國，諸子人人皆得封，而妾夫獨以戰死，奈何讎人猶在朝廷！」
manualTranslations.literal: When Taizu’s sons had all been enfeoffed as princes, at a palace feast Youning’s wife wept and said to Taizu: "Your Majesty turned house into state; every son received a fief, yet my husband alone died in battle—how can our enemy still serve at court!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu’s sons had all been made princes, Youning’s widow wept at a palace feast: "Your Majesty turned house into state. Every son got a fief, yet my husband alone died in battle—how can his enemy still walk the court?"

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖奮然戟手曰：「吾亦幾忘此賊！」
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu angrily brandished his hand and said: "I had nearly forgotten this villain!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu slashed the air with his hand: "I had nearly forgotten that villain!"

manualTranslations.zh: 乃遣人就洛陽族滅之。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent men to Luoyang to exterminate the clan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent men to Luoyang to wipe out the clan.

manualTranslations.zh: 使者至，先掘坑於外，乃入告之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the envoys arrived they first dug a pit outside, then entered to announce it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived they dug a pit outside first, then came in to tell him.

manualTranslations.zh: 師範設席為具，與諸宗族飲酒，謂使者曰：「死，人之所不免，況有罪乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Shifan spread a feast and drank with his clansmen, then told the envoys: "Death is what no man escapes, especially when guilty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shifan laid out a feast and drank with his kin, then told the envoys: "Death comes to all, and guilt makes it worse.

manualTranslations.zh: 然懼少長失序，下愧於先人。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yet I fear disorder among young and old and shame my ancestors below."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I only fear disorder among young and old and shame before my ancestors."

manualTranslations.zh: 酒半，令少長以次起，就戮於坑所，聞者皆哀憐之。
manualTranslations.literal: At mid-feast he had elders and juniors rise in order and go to the pit to be executed; all who heard it pitied him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Halfway through the wine he had elders and juniors rise in order and walk to the pit. All who heard it pitied him.

manualTranslations.zh: 同光三年，贈師範太尉。
manualTranslations.literal: In Tongguang 3 Shifan was posthumously made Grand Guardian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 3 Shifan was posthumously made Grand Guardian.

manualTranslations.literal: Yu told Keyong he feared Hanzhi might harbor other designs. Keyong said: "Toward Hanzhi, would I begrudge one commandery? But a hawk’s nature is to fly once it is full!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu warned Keyong that Hanzhi might turn disloyal. Keyong said: "I would not begrudge him a town—but a hawk flies once its belly is full!"

manualTranslations.zh: 光化元年，潞州薛志勤卒，罕之遽入潞州，使人啟晉王曰：「志勤且死，新帥未至，所以然者，備佗盜耳！」

manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Guanghua 1 Xue Zhiqin of Luzhou died. Hanzhi rushed into Luzhou and told the Prince of Jin: "Zhiqin is dying and the new commander has not arrived—I came only to keep out other thieves!"

manualTranslations.zh: 克用大怒，遣李嗣昭攻之。
manualTranslations.literal: Keyong was furious and sent Li Sixiao to attack him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Keyong was furious and sent Li Sixiao against him.

manualTranslations.zh: 罕之執晉守將馬溉、伊鐔等，遣子顥送于梁以乞兵。
manualTranslations.literal: Hanzhi seized Jin garrison commanders Ma Gai, Yi Zeng, and others, and sent his son Hao to Liang to beg for troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hanzhi seized Jin commanders Ma Gai, Yi Zeng, and others and sent his son Hao to Liang to beg for troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁太祖遣丁會守潞州，以罕之為河陽節度使，行至懷州，以疾卒，年五十八。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang Taizu sent Ding Hui to hold Luzhou and made Hanzhi military governor of Heyang. Reaching Huai Prefecture he died of illness at fifty-eight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Ding Hui to hold Luzhou and made Hanzhi governor of Heyang. At Huai Prefecture he died of illness at fifty-eight.

sourceRange.text: 明宗即位，以為樞密使。明宗幸汴州，循留守東都，民有犯麴者，循族殺其家，明宗知其冤，因詔天下除麴禁，許民得造麴。循為人柔佞而險猾，安重誨尤親信之，凡循所言，無不聽用。明宗嘗欲以皇子娶重誨女，重誨以問循，循曰：「公為機密之臣，不宜與皇子婚。」重誨信之，乃止。而循陰使人白明宗，求女妻皇子，明宗即以宋王從厚娶循女。重誨始惡其為人，出循為忠武軍節度使，徙鎮橫海，卒于鎮，年四十八，贈太尉。

context.beforeSource: 」明宗先至，遂納之。
context.afterSource: 孫德昭，鹽州五原人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗即位，以為樞密使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Xun was made commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Xun was made commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗幸汴州，循留守東都，民有犯麴者，循族殺其家，明宗知其冤，因詔天下除麴禁，許民得造麴。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong visited Bian Prefecture, Xun remained at the eastern capital. When a commoner violated the ban on mash wine, Xun executed his whole clan. Mingzong knew it was unjust and therefore ordered the mash-wine ban lifted throughout the realm, allowing the people to brew mash.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong went to Bian, Xun stayed at the eastern capital. A man broke the mash-wine ban and Xun wiped out his family. Mingzong saw the injustice and lifted the ban empire-wide so people could brew mash again.

manualTranslations.zh: 循為人柔佞而險猾，安重誨尤親信之，凡循所言，無不聽用。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun was soft-spoken, fawning, and treacherous; An Chonghui especially trusted him, and whatever Xun said was followed without exception.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun was smooth, fawning, and treacherous. An Chonghui trusted him above all others, and every word Xun spoke was obeyed.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗嘗欲以皇子娶重誨女，重誨以問循，循曰：「公為機密之臣，不宜與皇子婚。」
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong once wished to have a prince marry Chonghui's daughter. Chonghui asked Xun. Xun said: "You, sir, are a confidential minister and ought not marry into the imperial clan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong once wanted a prince to marry Chonghui's daughter. Chonghui asked Xun, who said: "You are a confidential minister—you should not marry into the imperial house."

manualTranslations.zh: 重誨信之，乃止。
manualTranslations.literal: Chonghui believed him and let the matter drop.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chonghui believed him and dropped the plan.

manualTranslations.zh: 而循陰使人白明宗，求女妻皇子，明宗即以宋王從厚娶循女。
manualTranslations.literal: But Xun secretly sent someone to inform Mingzong, asking that his daughter marry a prince, and Mingzong had Prince Song Conghou take Xun's daughter in marriage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But Xun secretly told Mingzong he wanted his daughter to marry a prince, and Mingzong had Prince Song Conghou wed Xun's daughter.

manualTranslations.zh: 重誨始惡其為人，出循為忠武軍節度使，徙鎮橫海，卒于鎮，年四十八，贈太尉。
manualTranslations.literal: Chonghui then came to hate his character, sent Xun out as military commissioner of the Zhongwu Army, transferred him to Henghai, and he died in post at forty-eight, posthumously made Grand Marshal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chonghui then turned against him, sent him out as military commissioner of Zhongwu, moved him to Henghai, and he died there at forty-eight, posthumously made Grand Marshal.

sourceRange.text: 德昭破鎖出昭宗，御丹鳳樓反正，以功拜靜海軍節度使，賜姓李，號「扶傾濟難忠烈功臣」，與承誨等皆拜節度使、同中書門下平章事，圖形凌煙閣，俱留京師，號「三使相」，恩寵無比。是時，崔胤方欲誅唐宦官，外交梁以為恃，而宦官亦倚李茂貞為扞蔽，梁、岐交爭。冬十月，宦者韓全誨劫昭宗幸鳳翔，承誨、從實皆從，而德昭獨與梁，乃率兵衞胤及百官保東街，趣梁兵以西，梁太祖頗德其附己，以龍鳳劍、鬬鷄紗遺之。太祖至華州，德昭以軍禮迎謁道旁。太祖至京師，表同州留後，將行，京師民復請留，遂為兩街制置使。梁兵圍鳳翔，德昭以其兵八千屬太祖，太祖益德之，使先之洛陽，賜甲第一區。昭宗東遷，拜左威衞上將軍，以疾免。太祖即位，以烏銀帶、袍、笏、名馬賜之。疾少間，以為左衞大將軍。末帝立，拜左金吾大將軍以卒。承誨、從實至鳳翔，與宦者俱見殺。王敬蕘，潁州汝陰人也。事州為牙將。唐末，王仙芝等攻劫汝、潁間，刺史不能拒，敬蕘遂代之，即拜刺史。敬蕘為人狀貌魁傑，而沈勇有力，善用鐵槍，重三十斤。潁州與淮西為鄰境，數為秦宗權所攻，力戰拒之，宗權悉陷河南諸州，獨敬蕘不可下，由是潁旁諸州民，皆保敬蕘避賊。是時，所在殘破，獨潁州戶二萬。梁太祖攻淮南，道過潁州，敬蕘供饋梁兵甚厚，太祖大喜，表敬蕘沿淮指揮使。其後梁兵攻吳，龐師古死清口，敗兵亡歸，過潁，大雪，士卒飢凍，敬蕘乃沿淮積薪為作糜粥餔之，亡卒多賴以全活，太祖表敬蕘武寧軍留後，遂拜節度使。天祐三年，為左衞上將軍。太祖即位，敬蕘以疾致仕，後卒于家。

manualTranslations.zh: 德昭破鎖出昭宗，禦丹鳳樓反正，以功拜靜海軍節度使，賜姓李，號「扶傾濟難忠烈功臣」，與承誨等皆拜節度使、同中書門下平章事，圖形淩煙閣，俱留京師，號「三使相」，恩寵無比。
manualTranslations.literal: Dezhao broke the locks and brought Zhaozong out. He took the throne at Danfeng Tower to restore the reign. For merit he was appointed military commissioner of the Jinghai Army, granted the surname Li, and given the title "Loyal Martyr Who Rights the Fallen," while Chenghui and the rest were all made military commissioners and Grand Councillors. Their portraits were hung in the Lingyan Pavilion. All remained in the capital and were called the "Three Commissioner-Chancellors," with favor unmatched.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dezhao broke the locks and led Zhaozong out to Danfeng Tower, where the emperor took the throne again. Dezhao was made military commissioner of Jinghai, given the Li surname and the title "Loyal Martyr Who Rights the Fallen." Chenghui and the others became commissioners and chancellors too. Their faces went up in the Lingyan Pavilion. They all stayed in the capital as the "Three Commissioner-Chancellors," showered with honors such as the court had never given before.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，崔胤方欲誅唐宦官，外交梁以為恃，而宦官亦倚李茂貞為扞蔽，梁、岐交爭。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Cui Yin was just then plotting to execute the Tang eunuchs and looked abroad to Liang for support, while the eunuchs also relied on Li Maozhen as a shield; Liang and Qi contended with each other.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cui Yin was plotting to kill the Tang eunuchs and courted Liang for backing, while the eunuchs leaned on Li Maozhen of Qi. Liang and Qi were at odds.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬十月，宦者韓全誨劫昭宗幸鳳翔，承誨、從實皆從，而德昭獨與梁，乃率兵衞胤及百官保東街，趣梁兵以西，梁太祖頗德其附己，以龍鳳劍、鬬鷄紗遺之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the eunuch Han Quanhui seized Zhaozong and took him to Fengxiang. Chenghui and Congshi both followed, but Dezhao alone sided with Liang. He therefore led troops to guard Yin and the officials on East Street and hurried Liang's army west. Liang Taizu was much obliged by his adherence and sent him the dragon-phoenix sword and fighting-cock gauze.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month eunuch Han Quanhui abducted Zhaozong to Fengxiang. Chenghui and Congshi went along, but Dezhao alone backed Liang. He marched to shield Cui Yin and the officials on East Street and pushed Liang's army west. Zhu Wen rewarded his loyalty with the dragon-phoenix sword and fighting-cock gauze.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖至華州，德昭以軍禮迎謁道旁。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Founder reached Hua Prefecture, Dezhao received and paid respects by the road with military ceremony.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu reached Hua, Dezhao met him by the road with full military honors.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖至京師，表同州留後，將行，京師民復請留，遂為兩街制置使。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Founder reached the capital he memorialized Dezhao as acting governor of Tong Prefecture. As he was about to leave, the people of the capital again asked that Dezhao be kept, and he was therefore made disposition commissioner of the Two Streets.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the capital Taizu named him acting governor of Tong. When Dezhao was about to leave, the capital crowd begged him to stay, and he was made disposition commissioner of the Two Streets.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁兵圍鳳翔，德昭以其兵八千屬太祖，太祖益德之，使先之洛陽，賜甲第一區。
manualTranslations.literal: When Liang troops besieged Fengxiang, Dezhao placed his eight thousand men under the Founder. The Founder was all the more grateful and had him go first to Luoyang, granting him a first-rank mansion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the siege of Fengxiang Dezhao handed his eight thousand men to Taizu. Taizu owed him more than ever, sent him ahead to Luoyang, and gave him a first-rank mansion.

manualTranslations.zh: 昭宗東遷，拜左威衞上將軍，以疾免。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhaozong moved east, Dezhao was appointed general of the Left Majestic Guard and was relieved because of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong moved east, Dezhao became general of the Left Majestic Guard, then left office on account of illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖即位，以烏銀帶、袍、笏、名馬賜之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Founder took the throne he bestowed on him a black-silver belt, robe, tablet, and famous horses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu became emperor he gave Dezhao a black-silver belt, robe, court tablet, and fine horses.

manualTranslations.zh: 疾少間，以為左衞大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When his illness eased a little he was made great general of the Left Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he recovered somewhat he was made great general of the Left Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 末帝立，拜左金吾大將軍以卒。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Last Emperor acceded, Dezhao was appointed great general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and died in that post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he became great general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and died in office.

manualTranslations.zh: 承誨、從實至鳳翔，與宦者俱見殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Chenghui and Congshi reached Fengxiang and were killed together with the eunuchs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chenghui and Congshi reached Fengxiang and were killed along with the eunuchs.

manualTranslations.zh: 王敬蕘
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Jingrao
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Jingrao

manualTranslations.zh: 王敬蕘，潁州汝陰人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Jingrao was a native of Ruyin in Ying Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Jingrao came from Ruyin in Ying Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 事州為牙將。
manualTranslations.literal: He served the prefecture as a guard officer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served the prefecture as a guard officer.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐末，王仙芝等攻劫汝、潁間，刺史不能拒，敬蕘遂代之，即拜刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Tang, Wang Xianzhi and others raided between Ru and Ying. The prefect could not resist, and Jingrao thereupon replaced him and was at once appointed prefect.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Late in Tang, Wang Xianzhi raided between Ru and Ying. The prefect could not hold them off, and Jingrao replaced him and was named prefect on the spot.

manualTranslations.zh: 敬蕘為人狀貌魁傑，而沈勇有力，善用鐵槍，重三十斤。
manualTranslations.literal: Jingrao was imposing in stature, deep and brave in spirit, and strong; he excelled with the iron spear, which weighed thirty jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingrao was huge in build, steady and fierce, and strong. His iron spear weighed thirty jin and few could match him with it.

manualTranslations.zh: 潁州與淮西為鄰境，數為秦宗權所攻，力戰拒之，宗權悉陷河南諸州，獨敬蕘不可下，由是潁旁諸州民，皆保敬蕘避賊。
manualTranslations.literal: Ying Prefecture bordered Huainan West and was repeatedly attacked by Qin Zongquan. Jingrao fought hard to repel him. Zongquan overran all the prefectures of Henan, but Jingrao alone could not be taken; for this reason the people of the prefectures around Ying all sheltered with Jingrao to escape the bandits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ying bordered Huainan West and Qin Zongquan struck again and again. Jingrao fought him off. Zongquan swallowed every Henan prefecture but could not take Ying, and people from the surrounding districts fled to Jingrao for safety.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，所在殘破，獨潁州戶二萬。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time everywhere was ravaged and broken; Ying Prefecture alone had twenty thousand households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The land lay in ruins everywhere, yet Ying still counted twenty thousand households.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁太祖攻淮南，道過潁州，敬蕘供饋梁兵甚厚，太祖大喜，表敬蕘沿淮指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Liang Taizu attacked Huainan and passed through Ying Prefecture, Jingrao supplied Liang troops very generously. The Founder was greatly pleased and memorialized Jingrao as commander along the Huai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Marching on Huainan, Taizu passed through Ying. Jingrao fed his army lavishly. Taizu was delighted and named him commander along the Huai.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後梁兵攻吳，龐師古死清口，敗兵亡歸，過潁，大雪，士卒飢凍，敬蕘乃沿淮積薪為作糜粥餔之，亡卒多賴以全活，太祖表敬蕘武寧軍留後，遂拜節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, when Liang troops attacked Wu, Pang Shigu died at Qingkou. Defeated soldiers fled home, passing Ying in heavy snow while the men starved and froze. Jingrao piled firewood along the Huai to cook porridge and feed them, and many fugitive soldiers owed their lives to him. The Founder memorialized Jingrao as acting governor of the Wuning Army, and he was then appointed military commissioner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Liang attacked Wu and Pang Shigu fell at Qingkou. Broken troops straggled home through Ying in blinding snow, starving and freezing. Jingrao stacked firewood along the Huai and cooked porridge for them; many lived because of it. Taizu named him acting governor of Wuning, then military commissioner.

manualTranslations.zh: 天祐三年，為左衞上將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou he was made general of the Left Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 3 he became general of the Left Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖即位，敬蕘以疾致仕，後卒于家。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Jingrao retired on account of illness and later died at home.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Taizu became emperor, Jingrao retired sick and later died at home.

sourceRange.text: 賀德倫，河西人也。少為滑州牙將。梁太祖兼領宣義，德倫從太祖征伐，以功累遷平盧軍節度使。貞明元年，魏州楊師厚卒，末帝以魏兵素驕難制，乃分相、澶、衞三州建昭德軍，以張筠為節度使；魏、博、貝三州仍為天雄軍，以德倫為節度使。遣劉鄩以兵六萬渡河，聲言攻鎮定，王彥章以騎兵五百入魏州，屯金波亭以虞變；分魏牙兵之半入昭德。租庸使遣孔目吏閱魏兵籍，檢校府庫。德倫促牙兵上道，牙兵親戚相訣別，哭聲盈塗。効節軍將張彥謀於其眾曰：「朝廷以我軍府彊盛，設法殘破之。況我六州舊為藩府，未嘗遠出河門，一旦離親戚，去鄉里，生不如死。」乃相與夜攻金波亭，彥章走出。遲明，魏兵攻牙城，殺五百餘人，執德倫致之樓上，縱兵大掠。

context.beforeSource: 唐興，追贈太師。
context.afterSource: 末帝遣供奉官扈異馳至魏諭彥，許以刺史。

manualTranslations.zh: 賀德倫，河西人也。
manualTranslations.literal: He Delun was a man of Hexi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Delun came from Hexi.

manualTranslations.zh: 少為滑州牙將。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he served as a tooth officer at Huazhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a youth he was a tooth officer at Huazhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁太祖兼領宣義，德倫從太祖征伐，以功累遷平盧軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Liang Taizu also held Xuanyi, Delun followed the Founder on campaign and by merit was repeatedly promoted to military governor of the Pinglu army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhu Wen also held Xuanyi, Delun followed him on campaign and rose by stages to military governor of Pinglu.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞明元年，魏州楊師厚卒，末帝以魏兵素驕難制，乃分相、澶、衞三州建昭德軍，以張筠為節度使；
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming, Yang Shihou of Weizhou died. The Last Emperor, because Wei troops were habitually arrogant and hard to control, split off Xiang, Cao, and Wei prefectures to establish the Zhaode army and made Zhang Jun its military governor;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhenming 1: Yang Shihou of Wei died. The Last Emperor, finding Wei troops proud and unruly, carved out Xiang, Cao, and Wei for a new Zhaode command under Zhang Jun;

manualTranslations.zh: 魏、博、貝三州仍為天雄軍，以德倫為節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei, Bo, and Bei prefectures remained the Tianxiong army, with Delun as military governor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei, Bo, and Bei stayed Tianxiong, with Delun as governor.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣劉鄩以兵六萬渡河，聲言攻鎮定，王彥章以騎兵五百入魏州，屯金波亭以虞變；
manualTranslations.literal: He sent Liu Yun with sixty thousand men across the river, proclaiming an attack on Zhen and Ding, while Wang Yanzhang entered Weizhou with five hundred cavalry and encamped at Jinbo Pavilion to guard against trouble;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Yun with sixty thousand men across the river, feigning a strike on Zhen and Ding, while Wang Yanzhang entered Wei with five hundred horse and camped at Jinbo Pavilion to watch for trouble;

manualTranslations.zh: 分魏牙兵之半入昭德。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent half the Wei tooth troops into Zhaode.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Half the Wei tooth troops were sent into Zhaode.

manualTranslations.zh: 租庸使遣孔目吏閱魏兵籍，檢校府庫。
manualTranslations.literal: The commissioner of rents and labor corvée sent clerks to review Wei troop rosters and inspect the treasury.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rent-and-corvée commissioner sent clerks to audit Wei troop rolls and inspect the treasury.

manualTranslations.zh: 德倫促牙兵上道，牙兵親戚相訣別，哭聲盈塗。
manualTranslations.literal: Delun urged the tooth troops onto the road; kinsmen of the tooth troops took tearful farewells, and weeping filled the streets.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Delun pressed the tooth troops to march. Kinsmen took tearful leave along the road, and weeping filled the streets.

manualTranslations.zh: 効節軍將張彥謀於其眾曰：「朝廷以我軍府彊盛，設法殘破之。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Yan, general of the Xiaojie army, plotted before his followers and said: "The court, because our army district is strong and mighty, has devised means to break it apart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan, general of the Xiaojie army, plotted with his men: "The court sees our district too strong and means to break us.

manualTranslations.zh: 況我六州舊為藩府，未嘗遠出河門，一旦離親戚，去鄉里，生不如死。」
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, our six prefectures were formerly a frontier commandery; we have never marched far beyond the He Gate. To leave kinsmen and homeland at a stroke—death is better than life."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Our six prefectures were a frontier command; we never marched far beyond the He Gate. To leave kin and home at once—better dead than alive."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃相與夜攻金波亭，彥章走出。
manualTranslations.literal: They then together attacked Jinbo Pavilion by night, and Yanzhang fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That night they stormed Jinbo Pavilion together, and Yanzhang fled.

manualTranslations.zh: 遲明，魏兵攻牙城，殺五百餘人，執德倫致之樓上，縱兵大掠。
manualTranslations.literal: At dawn Wei troops attacked the barracks city, killed more than five hundred men, seized Delun and brought him up to the tower, and let the soldiers plunder freely.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At dawn Wei troops stormed the barracks city, killed more than five hundred men, seized Delun and hauled him to the tower, and let the army loot at will.

sourceRange.text: 袁象先，宋州下邑人，唐南陽王恕己之後也。父敬初，梁太府卿、駙馬都尉，尚太祖妹，是為萬安大長公主。象先以梁甥為宣武軍內外馬步軍都指揮使，歷宿、洺、陳三州刺史。太祖即位，累遷左龍武統軍、在京馬步軍都指揮使。

context.beforeSource: 友謙死，其將史武等七人皆坐友謙族誅，天下冤之。
context.afterSource: 太祖遇弒，友珪立。

manualTranslations.zh: 袁象先，宋州下邑人，唐南陽王恕己之後也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan Xiangxian was a native of Xiayi in Songzhou, a descendant of Shuji, Prince of Nanyang under Tang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiangxian came from Xiayi in Songzhou, descended from Prince Shuji of Nanyang under Tang.

manualTranslations.zh: 父敬初，梁太府卿、駙馬都尉，尚太祖妹，是為萬安大長公主。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Jingchu was Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury and Commandant of the Horseshoe Escort under Liang; he married a younger sister of the Founder, who was titled Grand Princess of Wan’an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Jingchu served Liang as Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury and Commandant of the Horseshoe Escort and married the Founder’s younger sister—the Grand Princess of Wan’an.

manualTranslations.zh: 象先以梁甥為宣武軍內外馬步軍都指揮使，歷宿、洺、陳三州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiangxian, as the Founder’s nephew by marriage, became overall commander of horse and foot of the Xuanwu army inside and outside the circuit, and served successively as prefect of Suzhou, Mingzhou, and Chenzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As the Founder’s nephew by marriage, Xiangxian commanded all horse and foot of Xuanwu inside and outside the circuit, then held Suzhou, Mingzhou, and Chenzhou in turn.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖即位，累遷左龍武統軍、在京馬步軍都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Xiangxian was repeatedly promoted to Left Dragon Martial Commander and overall commander of horse and foot in the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the Founder’s accession he rose to Left Dragon Martial Commander and commander of all horse and foot in the capital.

sourceRange.text: 劉玘，汴州雍丘人也，世為宣武軍牙將。梁太祖鎮宣武，玘以軍卒補隊長，稍以戰功遷牙將，為襄州都指揮使。山南節度使王班為亂軍所殺，亂軍推玘為留後，玘偽許之，明日饗士于庭，伏甲幕中，酒半，擒為亂者殺之。會梁遣陳暉兵亦至，襄州平，以功拜復州刺史，徙亳、安二州。末帝時，為晉州觀察留後，凡八年，日與晉人交戰。莊宗滅梁，玘來朝，莊宗勞之曰：「劉侯亡恙，爾居晉陽之南鄙久矣，不早相聞，今日見訪，不其晚邪？」玘頓首謝罪，遣還鎮，遂以為節度使，徙鎮安遠。天成元年，以史敬鎔代之，玘還京師，未至，拜武勝軍節度使，以疾卒于道中，贈侍中。

context.beforeSource: 明年，長流遼州，賜死。
context.afterSource: 周知裕字好問，幽州人也。

context.afterLocal: 周知裕，字好問，幽州人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 劉玘
manualTranslations.literal: Liu Qi
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Qi

manualTranslations.zh: 劉玘，汴州雍丘人也，世為宣武軍牙將。
manualTranslations.literal: Liu Qi was a native of Yongqiu in Bianzhou; for generations his family had served as Xuanwu army guard officers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Qi came from Yongqiu in Bianzhou; his family had served for generations as Xuanwu army guard officers.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁太祖鎮宣武，玘以軍卒補隊長，稍以戰功遷牙將，為襄州都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Liang Founder held Xuanwu, Qi entered as a rank soldier and was made squad leader; gradually through battle merit he was promoted to guard officer and made overall commander of Xiangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhu Wen held Xuanwu, Qi entered as a rank soldier and became squad leader; battle by battle he rose to guard officer and overall commander of Xiangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 山南節度使王班為亂軍所殺，亂軍推玘為留後，玘偽許之，明日饗士于庭，伏甲幕中，酒半，擒為亂者殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Shannan military governor Wang Ban was killed by mutineers; they pushed Qi as acting commissioner. Qi feigned assent; the next day he feasted the troops in the courtyard and hid armored men behind the screens; at mid-feast he seized and killed the ringleaders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shannan governor Wang Ban fell to mutineers who wanted Qi as acting commissioner. Qi pretended yes; next day he feasted the men in the courtyard with armored troops hidden behind the screens, and at mid-feast seized and killed the ringleaders.

manualTranslations.zh: 會梁遣陳暉兵亦至，襄州平，以功拜復州刺史，徙亳、安二州。
manualTranslations.literal: When Liang also sent Chen Hui’s troops, Xiangzhou was pacified; for the merit he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou and was moved through Bozhou and Anzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Hui’s Liang troops arrived too; Xiangzhou was pacified. Qi was made prefect of Fuzhou, then moved through Bozhou and Anzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 末帝時，為晉州觀察留後，凡八年，日與晉人交戰。
manualTranslations.literal: Under the Last Emperor he was observation commissioner at Jinzhou for eight years, fighting Jin forces day after day.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he held Jinzhou as observation commissioner for eight years, battling Jin every day.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗滅梁，玘來朝，莊宗勞之曰：「劉侯亡恙，爾居晉陽之南鄙久矣，不早相聞，今日見訪，不其晚邪？」
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Qi came to court. Zhuangzong consoled him, saying: “Lord Liu, are you well? You have long held the southern marches beyond Taiyuan. Why did you not report sooner? To visit only today—is it not late?”
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Qi came to court. Zhuangzong greeted him: “Lord Liu, are you well? You have long held the southern marches beyond Taiyuan. Why no word until now? To call only today—is that not late?”

manualTranslations.zh: 玘頓首謝罪，遣還鎮，遂以為節度使，徙鎮安遠。
manualTranslations.literal: Qi prostrated himself and begged pardon; Zhuangzong sent him back to his post, then made him military governor and moved him to govern Anyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qi kowtowed and begged pardon; Zhuangzong sent him back, then made him military governor and moved him to Anyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成元年，以史敬鎔代之，玘還京師，未至，拜武勝軍節度使，以疾卒于道中，贈侍中。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, Shi Jingrong replaced him; Qi started back to the capital, and before arriving was appointed military governor of the Wusheng army, but died of illness on the road and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 1, Shi Jingrong replaced him. Qi headed for the capital; before he arrived they made him military governor of Wusheng, but he died of illness on the road and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sourceRange.text: 莊宗遣元行欽討之，行欽攻魏不克，乃遣明宗代行欽。明宗至鄴，軍變，因入城與在禮合。明宗兵反嚮京師，在禮留于魏。明宗即位，拜在禮義成軍節度使，在禮不受命，遂拜鄴都留守、興唐尹。久之，皇甫暉等皆去，在禮獨在魏，患魏軍之驕，懼及禍，乃求徙鎮橫海。歷鎮泰寧、匡國、天平、忠武、武寧、歸德、晉昌，所至邸店羅列，積貲巨萬。

manualTranslations.zh: 莊宗遣元行欽討之，行欽攻魏不克，乃遣明宗代行欽。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong sent Yuan Xingqin to campaign against him; Xingqin attacked Wei but could not take it, and Mingzong was sent to replace Xingqin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sent Yuan Xingqin against him. Xingqin attacked Wei and failed, so Mingzong was sent to replace him.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗至鄴，軍變，因入城與在禮合。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong reached Ye; the army mutinied, and he entered the city and joined Zaili.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong reached Ye. The army mutinied, and he entered the city to join Zaili.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗兵反嚮京師，在禮留于魏。
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong’s troops turned back toward the capital; Zaili remained at Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong’s troops turned back on the capital. Zaili stayed at Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗即位，拜在禮義成軍節度使，在禮不受命，遂拜鄴都留守、興唐尹。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Zaili was made military governor of the Yicheng army; Zaili refused the appointment and was then made Ye capital regent and Xingtang prefect.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Zaili was made military governor of Yicheng. He refused and was made Ye capital regent and Xingtang prefect instead.

manualTranslations.zh: 久之，皇甫暉等皆去，在禮獨在魏，患魏軍之驕，懼及禍，乃求徙鎮橫海。
manualTranslations.literal: After a long while Huangfu Hui and the others all departed; Zaili alone remained at Wei, worried about the Wei army’s arrogance, feared disaster, and sought transfer to Henghai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In time Huangfu Hui and the others left. Zaili alone remained at Wei, feared the arrogant Wei troops, and asked to be moved to Henghai.

manualTranslations.zh: 歷鎮泰寧、匡國、天平、忠武、武寧、歸德、晉昌，所至邸店羅列，積貲巨萬。
manualTranslations.literal: He held successively Taiping, Kuangguo, Tianping, Zhongwu, Wuning, Guide, and Jinchang; wherever he went inns lined the roads and he amassed wealth in the tens of millions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He held Taiping, Kuangguo, Tianping, Zhongwu, Wuning, Guide, and Jinchang in turn. Inns lined the roads wherever he went, and he amassed tens of millions.

sourceRange.text: 子守恩，以蔭補，稍遷諸衞將軍。建立已卒，家于潞，守恩自京師得告歸，而契丹滅晉。昭義節度使張從恩與守恩姻家，乃以守恩權巡檢使，以守潞州，而從恩入見契丹。從恩既去，守恩因剽劫從恩家貲，以潞州降漢。漢高祖即位，以守恩為昭義軍節度使，徙鎮靜難、西京留守，加同中書門下平章事。

manualTranslations.zh: 子守恩，以蔭補，稍遷諸衞將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Shou’en entered service by yin privilege and was gradually promoted to general of the guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Shou’en entered service by yin privilege and rose gradually to general of the guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 建立已卒，家于潞，守恩自京師得告歸，而契丹滅晉。
manualTranslations.literal: After Jianli had died, the family was at Lu; Shou’en obtained leave from the capital to return home, and the Khitan destroyed Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jianli had died and the family was at Lu. Shou’en obtained leave from the capital to return home, and the Khitan destroyed Jin.

sourceRange.text: 相里金字奉金，并州人也。為人勇悍，而能折節下士。事晉王為五院軍隊長。梁、晉戰柏鄉、胡柳，皆有功，遷黃甲指揮使。同光中，拜忻州刺史。是時，諸州皆用武人，多以部曲主場務，漁蠹公私，以利自入，金獨禁部曲不與事，厚其給養，使掌家事而已。遷隴州防禦使。廢帝起兵鳳翔，馳檄四隣，四隣未有應者，獨金首遣判官薛文遇見廢帝，往來計事。廢帝即位，德之，拜保義軍節度使。晉高祖起太原，廢帝以金為太原四面步軍都指揮使。高祖入立，徙鎮建雄，罷為上將軍。天福五年卒，贈太師。

manualTranslations.literal: Xiang Lijin
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiang Lijin

manualTranslations.zh: 相里金字奉金，并州人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiang Lijin, courtesy name Fengjin, was a native of Bingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiang Lijin, styled Fengjin, came from Bingzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 為人勇悍，而能折節下士。
manualTranslations.literal: As a man he was fierce and bold, yet able to humble himself before men of talent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was fierce and bold, yet able to humble himself before men of talent.

manualTranslations.zh: 事晉王為五院軍隊長。
manualTranslations.literal: He served the Prince of Jin as captain of the Five-Court army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served the Prince of Jin as captain of the Five-Court army.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁、晉戰柏鄉、胡柳，皆有功，遷黃甲指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the battles of Baixiang and Huliu between Liang and Jin he won merit in both and was promoted to commander of the Yellow Armor corps.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself at Baixiang and Huliu in the wars between Liang and Jin and was made commander of the Yellow Armor corps.

manualTranslations.zh: 同光中，拜忻州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: During Tongguang he was appointed prefect of Xin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Tongguang he was made prefect of Xin.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，諸州皆用武人，多以部曲主場務，漁蠹公私，以利自入，金獨禁部曲不與事，厚其給養，使掌家事而已。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time every prefecture used military men; many had their retainers run market offices and prey on public and private wealth for personal gain. Jin alone forbade his retainers to meddle in affairs, enriched their support, and had them manage household matters only.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In those days prefectures were run by soldiers; many let retainers control market offices and bleed public and private wealth for themselves. Jin alone barred his retainers from such affairs, paid them generously, and kept them to household duties.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷隴州防禦使。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to defense commissioner of Long.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was made defense commissioner of Long.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝起兵鳳翔，馳檄四隣，四隣未有應者，獨金首遣判官薛文遇見廢帝，往來計事。
manualTranslations.literal: The Deposed Emperor raised troops at Fengxiang and sent proclamations racing to the four neighboring circuits; none answered until Jin alone first sent his judicial officer Xue Wenyu to see the Deposed Emperor and go back and forth planning affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor rose at Fengxiang and sent urgent proclamations to the neighboring circuits; none answered except Jin, who first sent his judicial officer Xue Wenyu to consult with him.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝即位，德之，拜保義軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne he was grateful and made Jin military commissioner of Baoyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne he was grateful and made Jin commissioner of Baoyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉高祖起太原，廢帝以金為太原四面步軍都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jin Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, the Deposed Emperor made Jin overall commander of the foot forces on all four sides of Taiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, the Deposed Emperor made Jin overall commander of the foot forces encircling Taiyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖入立，徙鎮建雄，罷為上將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu entered and took the throne, Jin was shifted to govern Jianxiong, then dismissed to Senior General.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Jin was shifted to Jianxiong, then relieved to Senior General.

manualTranslations.zh: 天福五年卒，贈太師。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in Tianfu 5 and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Tianfu 5 and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sourceRange.text: 莊宗滅梁，見溫琪，曰：「此為梁守平陽者也！」嘉之，因以耀州為順義軍，拜溫琪節度使，徙鎮雄武。明宗時來朝，願留闕下，以為左驍衞上將軍。踰年，明宗謂樞密使安重誨曰：「溫琪舊人，宜與一重鎮。」重誨意不欲與，對以無員闕。佗日，明宗語又及之，重誨曰：「可代者惟樞密使耳。」明宗曰：「可。」重誨不能答。溫琪聞之懼，稱疾不出者累月。已而以為鎮國軍節度使。廢帝時，以太子太保致仕。天福元年卒，贈太子太傅。

context.beforeSource: 遷耀州觀察留後。
context.afterSource: 萇從簡，陳州人也。

manualTranslations.literal: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, saw Wenqi, and said: "This is the one who defended Pingyang for Liang!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, saw Wenqi, and said: "This is the man who held Pingyang for Liang!"

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉之，因以耀州為順義軍，拜溫琪節度使，徙鎮雄武。
manualTranslations.literal: He praised him, thereby made Yao into the Shunyi army, appointed Wenqi military commissioner, and transferred him to govern Xiongwu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He praised him, raised Yao to the Shunyi army, made Wenqi its commissioner, and shifted him to Xiongwu.

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗時來朝，願留闕下，以為左驍衞上將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong came to court, he wished to remain at the capital and was made Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he came to court, asked to remain at the capital, and was made Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 踰年，明宗謂樞密使安重誨曰：「溫琪舊人，宜與一重鎮。」
manualTranslations.literal: After a year Mingzong said to Military Affairs Commissioner An Chonghui: "Wenqi is an old acquaintance; he ought to be given an important post."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After a year Mingzong told Military Affairs Commissioner An Chonghui: "Wenqi is an old friend; he ought to receive an important command."

manualTranslations.zh: 重誨意不欲與，對以無員闕。
manualTranslations.literal: Chonghui did not wish to grant it and replied that there were no vacancies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chonghui did not wish to grant it and answered that there were no vacancies.

manualTranslations.zh: 佗日，明宗語又及之，重誨曰：「可代者惟樞密使耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Another day Mingzong mentioned it again; Chonghui said: "The only post that could be replaced is Military Affairs Commissioner."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Another day Mingzong raised it again. Chonghui said: "The only post that could be replaced is Military Affairs Commissioner."

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗曰：「可。」
manualTranslations.literal: Mingzong said: "Very well."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mingzong said: "Very well."

manualTranslations.zh: 重誨不能答。
manualTranslations.literal: Chonghui had no answer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chonghui had no answer.

manualTranslations.zh: 溫琪聞之懼，稱疾不出者累月。
manualTranslations.literal: Wenqi heard of this and feared; he claimed illness and did not go out for months.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wenqi heard of it, grew afraid, claimed illness, and stayed indoors for months.

manualTranslations.zh: 已而以為鎮國軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Presently he was made military commissioner of Zhenguo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was then made military commissioner of Zhenguo.

manualTranslations.zh: 廢帝時，以太子太保致仕。
manualTranslations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor he retired as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor he retired as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

manualTranslations.zh: 天福元年卒，贈太子太傅。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in Tianfu 1 and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Tianfu 1 and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sourceRange.text: 明宗即位，文進自平州率眾數萬歸唐，明宗得之，喜甚，以為義成軍節度使。居歲餘，徙鎮威勝，加同平章事，入為上將軍，出鎮昭義，徙安遠。晉高祖立，與契丹約為父子，文進懼不自安。天福元年冬，殺其行軍司馬馮知兆、副使杜重貴，送款於李昪，昪遣兵迎之。文進居數鎮，頗有善政，兵民愛之。其將行也，從數騎，自至營中別其將士，告以避契丹之意，將士皆再拜為訣，乃南奔。昪以文進為天雄統軍、宣潤節度使。

context.beforeSource: 攻新州，不克，攻武州，又不克，遂奔于契丹，契丹使守平州。
context.afterSource: 文進身長七尺，狀貌偉然。
context.beforeLocal: 攻新州，不克，攻武州，又不克，遂奔於契丹，契丹使守平州。

manualTranslations.zh: 明宗即位，文進自平州率眾數萬歸唐，明宗得之，喜甚，以為義成軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Wenjin led tens of thousands from Pingzhou back to Tang. Mingzong was overjoyed and made him military commissioner of the Yicheng army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Wenjin led tens of thousands from Ping back to Tang. Mingzong was delighted and made him military commissioner of Yicheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 居歲餘，徙鎮威勝，加同平章事，入為上將軍，出鎮昭義，徙安遠。
manualTranslations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to govern Weisheng, given the additional title of co-equal with the chief ministers, made Senior General in the capital, sent out to govern Zhaoyi, then transferred to Anyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was shifted to Weisheng, made co-equal with the chief ministers, appointed Senior General in the capital, sent out to Zhaoyi, then moved to Anyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉高祖立，與契丹約為父子，文進懼不自安。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne and entered the father-son pact with the Khitan, Wenjin feared for his safety.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu took the throne and made the father-son pact with the Khitan, Wenjin grew afraid.

manualTranslations.zh: 天福元年冬，殺其行軍司馬馮知兆、副使杜重貴，送款於李昪，昪遣兵迎之。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter of Tianfu year 1 he killed his campaign adjutant Feng Zhizhao and deputy Du Chonggui, sent terms to Li Bian, and Bian sent troops to welcome him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In winter of Tianfu 1 he killed his campaign adjutant Feng Zhizhao and deputy Du Chonggui, submitted to Li Bian, and Bian sent troops to receive him.

manualTranslations.zh: 文進居數鎮，頗有善政，兵民愛之。
manualTranslations.literal: Wenjin governed several circuits with good administration, and soldiers and civilians loved him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wenjin held several circuits with good government, and troops and people loved him.

manualTranslations.zh: 其將行也，從數騎，自至營中別其將士，告以避契丹之意，將士皆再拜為訣，乃南奔。
manualTranslations.literal: When he was about to leave, he took a few horsemen, went in person to camp to bid his officers and men farewell, told them he meant to flee the Khitan, and they all bowed twice in leave-taking before he fled south.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he was about to go, he rode with a few followers into camp himself to take leave of his officers and men, told them he meant to escape the Khitan, and after they bowed twice in farewell he fled south.

manualTranslations.zh: 昪以文進為天雄統軍、宣潤節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Bian made Wenjin commander of the Tianxiong army and military commissioner of Xuan-Run.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bian made Wenjin Tianxiong commander and military commissioner of Xuan-Run.

sourceRange.text: 王進，幽州良鄉人也。為人勇悍，走及奔馬。少聚徒為盜，鄉里患之，符彥超遣人以賂招置麾下。彥超鎮安遠軍，軍中有變，遣進馳奏京師，明宗怪其來速，嘉其足力，以隸寧衞指揮。漢高祖為侍衞親軍指揮使，以進為軍校。高祖鎮河東，因以之從，每有急，遣進馳至京師，往返不過五六日，由是愈親愛之，累遷奉國軍都指揮使。從周太祖起魏，遷虎捷右廂都指揮使。歷汝、鄭二州防禦使、彰德軍節度使。顯德元年秋，一本作初。以疾卒，贈太師。

context.beforeSource: 周師伐淮南，以功領饒州刺史，遷濠州刺史，兵攻濠州，以戰傷重卒，贈武清軍節度使。
context.afterSource: 嗚呼！

manualTranslations.zh: 王進
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Jin
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Jin

manualTranslations.zh: 王進，幽州良鄉人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Jin was a native of Liangxiang in Youzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Jin came from Liangxiang in Youzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 為人勇悍，走及奔馬。
manualTranslations.literal: As a man he was fierce and bold, and in running he could keep pace with galloping horses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was fierce and bold, and could outrun a galloping horse.

manualTranslations.zh: 少聚徒為盜，鄉里患之，符彥超遣人以賂招置麾下。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he gathered followers and became a bandit; the neighborhood suffered from him. Fu Yanchao sent men with bribes to recruit him and placed him under his command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In youth he gathered a band and robbed the countryside. Fu Yanchao bribed him into service.

manualTranslations.zh: 彥超鎮安遠軍，軍中有變，遣進馳奏京師，明宗怪其來速，嘉其足力，以隸寧衞指揮。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yanchao governed Anyuan army, there was a mutiny in the camp. He sent Jin racing to report to the capital. Mingzong marveled at his swift arrival and praised his fleet feet, then assigned him to the Ningwei Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yanchao held Anyuan army when the camp mutinied. He sent Jin racing to the capital. Mingzong marveled at his speed and praised his legs, then assigned him to the Ningwei Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢高祖為侍衞親軍指揮使，以進為軍校。
manualTranslations.literal: When Han Gaozu was commander of the Palace Guard, he made Jin a company officer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu commanded the Palace Guard, he made Jin a company officer.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖鎮河東，因以之從，每有急，遣進馳至京師，往返不過五六日，由是愈親愛之，累遷奉國軍都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu governed Hedong, Jin followed him. Whenever there was urgency, Gaozu sent Jin racing to the capital; the round trip took no more than five or six days. From this he grew ever closer to Jin and repeatedly promoted him, until he became commander of the Fengguo army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu governed Hedong, Jin went with him. In every crisis Gaozu sent him racing to the capital—a round trip of five or six days at most. Gaozu grew ever fonder and raised him to commander of the Fengguo army.

manualTranslations.zh: 從周太祖起魏，遷虎捷右廂都指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: He followed Zhou Taizu in rising at Wei and was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Tiger Swift Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He followed Zhou Taizu in the Wei rising and became commander of the right wing of the Tiger Swift Army.

manualTranslations.zh: 歷汝、鄭二州防禦使、彰德軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: He successively served as defender of Ru and Zheng prefectures and military commissioner of the Zhangde army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was defender of Ru and Zheng in turn and military commissioner of Zhangde.

manualTranslations.zh: 顯德元年秋，一本作初。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xiande—one edition reads chu instead of qiu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In autumn of the first year of Xiande—one edition reads chu instead of qiu.

manualTranslations.zh: 以疾卒，贈太師。
manualTranslations.literal: He died of illness and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died of illness and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sourceRange.text: 常思字克恭，太原人也。初從唐莊宗為卒，後為長劍指揮使。歷唐、晉為六軍都虞候。漢高祖為河東節度使，以思為牢城指揮使。高祖入立，領武勝軍節度使，徙鎮昭義。思起軍卒，未嘗有戰功，徒以幸會漢興，遂秉旄節。在潞州五年，以聚斂為事，而性鄙儉。初，思微時，周太祖方少孤無依，食于思家，以思為叔，後思與周太祖俱遭漢以取富貴。周太祖已即位，每呼思為常叔，拜其妻，如家人禮。廣順三年，徙鎮歸德，居三年來朝，又徙平盧，思因啟曰：「臣居宋，宋民負臣絲息十萬兩，願以券上進。」太祖頷之，即焚其券，詔宋州悉蠲除之。思居青州，踰年得疾，歸于洛陽，卒，贈中書令。

context.beforeSource: 可勝道哉！
context.afterSource: 孫方諫，鄭州清苑人也。
context.beforeLocal: 可勝道哉！
context.afterLocal: 孫方諫，鄭州清苑人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 常思
manualTranslations.literal: Chang Si
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chang Si

manualTranslations.zh: 常思字克恭，太原人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Chang Si, courtesy name Kegong, was a native of Taiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chang Si, styled Kegong, came from Taiyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 初從唐莊宗為卒，後為長劍指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: At first he followed Tang’s Zhuangzong as a soldier and later became commander of the Long Sword.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He first followed Zhuangzong as a soldier and later commanded the Long Sword.

manualTranslations.zh: 歷唐、晉為六軍都虞候。
manualTranslations.literal: Under Tang and Jin he served as deputy commander of the Six Armies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Tang and Jin he was deputy commander of the Six Armies.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢高祖為河東節度使，以思為牢城指揮使。
manualTranslations.literal: When Han Gaozu was military governor of Hedong, he made Si commander of the Laocheng garrison.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu governed Hedong, he made Si commander of the Laocheng garrison.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖入立，領武勝軍節度使，徙鎮昭義。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu entered and took the throne, Si held the Wusheng army commission and was transferred to govern Zhaoyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Si held the Wusheng commission and was shifted to Zhaoyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 思起軍卒，未嘗有戰功，徒以幸會漢興，遂秉旄節。
manualTranslations.literal: Si rose from a soldier and had never won battle merit; he held a commissioner’s baton only by the luck of Han’s rise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Si rose from the ranks without battle merit and held a commissioner’s baton only by the luck of Han’s rise.

manualTranslations.zh: 在潞州五年，以聚斂為事，而性鄙儉。
manualTranslations.literal: For five years at Luzhou he made extortion his business, yet by nature he was mean and frugal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Five years at Luzhou he spent extorting wealth, yet by nature he was stingy and frugal.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，思微時，周太祖方少孤無依，食于思家，以思為叔，後思與周太祖俱遭漢以取富貴。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, when Si was still obscure, Zhou Taizu was young, orphaned, and without support, and ate at Si’s home, calling Si uncle. Later both Si and Zhou Taizu rode Han’s rise to wealth and rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Si was still obscure, young Zhou Taizu was orphaned and ate at his home, calling him uncle. Later both rode Han’s rise to wealth and rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 周太祖已即位，每呼思為常叔，拜其妻，如家人禮。
manualTranslations.literal: After Zhou Taizu had taken the throne, he always called Si Uncle Chang and bowed to his wife with the courtesy of family.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Zhou Taizu reigned, he always called Si Uncle Chang and bowed to his wife as kin.

manualTranslations.zh: 廣順三年，徙鎮歸德，居三年來朝，又徙平盧，思因啟曰：「臣居宋，宋民負臣絲息十萬兩，願以券上進。」
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun he was transferred to govern Guide. After three years in post he came to court, then was moved again to Pinglu. Si thereupon petitioned, saying: "When I governed Song, the people of Song owed me one hundred thousand taels in silk interest. I wish to present the bonds to Your Majesty."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangshun he was moved to Guide. Three years later he came to court, then was shifted to Pinglu. Si petitioned: "When I governed Song, the people owed me one hundred thousand taels in silk interest. I wish to present the bonds to Your Majesty."

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖頷之，即焚其券，詔宋州悉蠲除之。
manualTranslations.literal: Taizu nodded assent, then burned the bonds and ordered Song prefecture to forgive the debts entirely.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu nodded, burned the bonds, and ordered Song prefecture to forgive the debts entirely.

manualTranslations.zh: 思居青州，踰年得疾，歸于洛陽，卒，贈中書令。
manualTranslations.literal: Si governed Qingzhou; after more than a year he fell ill, returned to Luoyang, and died. He was posthumously made Grand Councilor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Qingzhou he fell ill within a year, returned to Luoyang, and died. He was posthumously made Grand Councilor.

sourceRange.text: 王環，鎮州真定人也。以勇力事孟知祥為御者，及知祥僭號于蜀，使典衞兵。晉開運之亂，秦、鳳、階、成入于蜀，孟昶以環為鳳州節度使。周世宗即位，明年，遣王景、向訓攻秦、鳳州，數為環所敗，大臣皆請罷兵。世宗曰：「吾欲一天下以為家，而聲教不及秦、鳳，今兵已出，無功而返，吾有慚焉。」乃決意攻之。周兵糧道頗艱，昶遣兵五千出堂倉抵黃花谷以爭糧道。景、訓先知其來，命排陣使張建雄以兵二千當谷口，別遣裨將以勁兵千人出其後，伏堂倉以待其歸。蜀兵前遇建雄，戰不勝，退走堂倉，伏發，盡殪之，由是蜀兵守諸城堡者皆潰。初，昶遣其秦州節度使高處儔以兵援環，未至，聞堂倉兵敗，亦潰歸，處儔判官趙玭閉城不內，處儔遂奔成都，玭乃以城降，成、階二州相繼亦降，獨環堅守百餘日，然後克之。

localRange.text: 初，昶遣其秦州節度使高處儔以兵援環，未至，聞堂倉兵敗，亦潰歸，處儔判官趙比閉城不內，處儔遂奔成都，比乃以城降，成、階二州相繼亦降，獨環堅守百餘日，然後克之。

context.beforeSource: 明年卒于鎮，年六十五，贈侍中，謚忠惠。
context.afterSource: 世宗召見環，歎曰：「三州已降，環獨堅守，吾數以書招之，而環不答，至於力屈就擒，雖不能死，亦忠其所事也，用之可勸事君者。
